  session could push only its own branch, so the backup is a branch made through the GitHub API.

## Current state (PWA v600, 2026-09-22)
- **A long word's line wraps instead of being cut, and the finished card's reading is measured rather than estimated (v600, H with a screenshot of 中华人民共和国地理标志: "Hier wird die Übersetzungszeile abgeschnitten. In so einem Fall bitte zweizeilig werden bzw. mehrzeilig werden." and, two minutes later, "Hier ist das finale Pinyin viel zu klein"):** two faults on one card, both of them a static estimate standing in for a measurement, so they ship as one version. **(1) The line under the pad.** v540 held each `.plrow` to one line (`white-space:nowrap`, `overflow:hidden`) and let the MEANING shrink to an ellipsis — but the meaning is the only part allowed to shrink, so on a word whose characters and pinyin alone are wider than the card the meaning went to **nothing** and the row was **still** sliced off both ends, because a centred flex row overflows symmetrically. Measured at 390 px on H's card: the word row 375 px wide in a 322 px box, `.mn` 0 px, 中华 gone from the left and the last syllable from the right — which is exactly what his screenshot shows. **This is the SECOND time the same cut reached H**, which is the argument for removing the mechanism rather than the symptom: at v540 he sent a 电动车 card whose line read "electric vehicle (commonly refers to e-bikes" with both ends sliced off, and the answer then was `shortSense`, which strips the parenthetical so that particular line fits. It did nothing about the slicing itself, and a long WORD carries no parenthetical to strip. `shortSense` stays — a parenthetical is an explanation and does not belong on that line — but it is no longer what keeps the line inside the card. The row is `flex-wrap:wrap` now with `max-width:100%` and `overflow-wrap:anywhere` on its parts, so whichever part does not fit moves to a line of its own and a part wider than the card on its own breaks inside itself; the row gap is 2 px against the 10 px between the parts, so a wrapped row still reads as one thing (a single `gap` in the `bigtxt` rule would have put 10 px between a word and its own pinyin, and was split into the two axes). **The height had to follow, and this is the part that could have gone wrong silently:** `.cue .padline` is `overflow:hidden`, and `splitFit` assumed the line was exactly `LINE_H` 61 px tall — an assumption that was TRUE only because a row that did not fit was sliced sideways rather than wrapped. It reads `line.scrollHeight` at `--plz` 1 now and gives the tiles `base − (lh+6)`, so a three-row line takes its room from the TILES and not from the pad: measured on H's card at 390 px, the line 61 → 109 px, the pad unchanged at 286 px, the card still ending above the tab bar; and over 40 contexts (10 languages × 390/360 × light/dark) **0 rows cut against v599's 120**, 0 lines cut at the foot, 0 cards past the tab bar, the line 62–109 px against a flat 61, and the pad 286 px on BOTH trees — the room came from the tiles, exactly as intended. The `--plz` growth of v589 is unchanged in spirit but relative to `lh` rather than to the constant, and a grown line that wraps one line more than it did at rest falls back to rest rather than being cut at the foot. **(2) The finished card's reading.** `recapHTML` sized the reading with `min(RECAP_CP, 140/mw cqw, 330/pn cqw)`, where `mw` is the widest WORD in characters — because v555 made each word a `nowrap` span so a break can never fall inside one. On H's card one word is the seven-syllable 中华人民共和国, whose pinyin is **29 characters**, so `140/29 cqw` put the whole reading at **12.7 px** in a 286 px square with **156 px of it empty** — smaller than the 20 px meaning under it. Two changes, both measured: a word of more than `RECAP_WSYL` **3** syllables may now break between its OWN syllables (splitting 供应 into "gōng / yìng" is a real fault, splitting a seven-syllable name across two lines is what any book does, and v555's rule is kept intact where it was written for — the suite asserts 供应 is still one span); and the size is no longer estimated at all but **binary-searched over the real layout** by `recapFit`, the largest whole pixel at which the reading still stands inside its own line clamp and leaves the meaning its room (the v413 rule: read the number from the page). The block is inserted at opacity 0 and the `in` class added on the next frame, so the search finishes before anything is painted. Measured at 390 px: H's card **12.7 → 27 px** (3 lines, unclipped), a four-syllable card 40.8 → 44 (the cap), a two-syllable card 44 → 44; over the 40 contexts **26–31 px against v599's 12.7–25.4**, none clipped or overflowing, and 0 page errors anywhere. `RECAP_MIN` 14 is the floor the search stops at; below it the v577 clamp cuts, as it always did. **The first cut of `recapFit` tested only the HEIGHT, and that is the one real regression this version nearly shipped:** a word set `nowrap` by v555 can be wider than the square while its line count is still 1, so a height-only fit calls it a fit — measured, 蜜雪冰城 came out at the 44 px cap with its one word **475 px wide in a 286 px square**, hanging out of a box with `overflow:hidden`, cut at both ends. That is precisely what the `140/mw` term existed to prevent, and dropping it without replacing it re-opened the hole the version was written to close. `.recap .rp` and `.rm` are capped at `max-width:100%` now, so a word that does not fit shows up as `scrollWidth` past `clientWidth`, and `fits()` tests the width **first**. 蜜雪冰城 lands at 24 px (v599's estimate gave it 23.5 — that card was never the fault), and the suite carries it as a `[guard]` that passes on both trees, since v599 handled it and v600 had to keep handling it. **`RECAP_WSYL` is 4, not 3:** the first cut let a four-syllable word break, which is 蜜雪冰城 and 社会主义 — exactly the words v555 was written for. At 4 only a five-syllable compound may break, H's seven-syllable one among them. **What was NOT changed, deliberately:** the three-line clamp on the reading (v577's own number — raising it would buy another ~4 px and cost the recap its shape), the meaning's own `min(20px, 8.2cqw)` (it is the line under the reading, not the headline), and the per-character 900 ms breath (`charRecapHTML`), which is one syllable and was never the complaint. **The guide's crops did not go stale:** both faults are in the `bigtxt` state and in the recap; the `front` and `learn` crops are taken in the picture state, where `--th` is 0 and the line is clipped away entirely, and `pcard` stops above the line — and this is measured rather than reasoned: across 80 comparisons the picture state's PAINTED geometry (`--cueh`/`--th`/`--ph`, the pad, the card's foot) is identical to v599. A first pass of the comparison reported all 40 contexts as differing, which was the probe and not the app — it was comparing the word line's own intrinsic height, 109 against 61, on an element whose `--th` is `0px` on both trees and which is therefore clipped away and never painted. `tools/guide-shots.js` was not run. Suite `verify-wrapline` (22 checks in five parts: the word row not cut and wrapped — measured as the row against its tallest part, since a 20 px hanzi beside 15 px pinyin on one baseline sits at different tops on BOTH trees and the first version of that check passed on v599 for that reason; the meaning back from 0 px; the line taller than the constant and its box holding all of it; the card still ending above the tab bar and the pad still a usable square; the open card's line at 360 px in German dark; **the recap driven through the app's own path — every stroke of 中 really written — asserting the reading carries a measured inline px and not a `min()` estimate**; the reading bigger than 24 px and bigger than its meaning; a long word split into spans of at most three syllables; and 供应 still one span) — **ALL OK 22 of 22 on v600; on a v599 root 12 of the 22 fail**, every one a `[flip]`, and the ten that pass on both are labelled with their reason. The per-character 900 ms breath (`charRecapHTML`) is measured byte-identical to v599, which is what says the recap change stayed where it was aimed. One `WHATS_NEW` line (a learner sees both) and two `TO_TEST` lines. Not yet field-checked.
- **The two sample cards in the app's instructions become real crops of the app (v599, H: "Real Screenshots for the characters" and, asked which characters he meant, "I meant the sample cards in the instructions"):** v598 made five of the guide's six figures real and left two drawn cards standing in the app — the guide's **privacy** figure, whose card held three drawn character rows (面/鸡/店), and the **empty deck's example card** (`introHTML`, v569's Beispielkarte), whose photo box and write pad were drawn shapes. Both are gone. `guide/front-{light,dark}.webp` is the study card's own front — the photographed door plate 推 over the pad with three strokes standing in ink and the fourth lit with its start dot — and `guide/pcard-{light,dark}.webp` is the open card, the photographed sign 坚果供应 with the card's own character tiles under it, 坚果 grouped and lit. **The mechanism is new and is the point of the version: `gfimg` puts a real crop INSIDE a drawn figure.** `<picture>` does not exist inside SVG, so light and dark are two `<image>` elements and a media query hides one (`.gfd-l`/`.gfd-d` in styles.css, not scoped to `.guide` because the empty deck is on the Learn tab); the app has no theme switch, so the media query is the whole rule, exactly as v598's `<picture>`. The box is **fitted, never stretched** — the crop's aspect ratio is read from `GF_SHOT` (`front:[0.494,0]`, `pcard:[0.834,0]`, the second number unused because these two are not figures of their own), so a regenerated crop of another shape re-centres itself instead of squashing, and the suite checks the rendered box against the file's own intrinsic ratio. **Why each figure keeps a drawn half, which is the decision worth recording.** In the privacy figure the arrow and the 文 chip stay drawn because *what leaves the phone* is not a screen anywhere in the app — there is nothing to photograph — and the crop stops above the card's reading line, which carries the **meaning** and would have put one language into a file that serves ten. In the example card the **fold bar at the card's foot stays drawn**, and for a reason v589 paid for: the real fold row reads "Whole card", which is UI prose, and note n3 ("Open it — the whole card.") points at it — a note pointing at something the picture does not show is the exact fault v589 had to correct here, so the bar is drawn rather than dropped. **The geometry is derived, not typed** (the v401 rule): `IH=140/GF_SHOT.front[0]` gives the crop its height at the mock's own inner width, and the fold bar, the card frame and the viewBox follow from it — the mock is `0 0 168 345.4` now instead of `0 0 168 350`, and the three handwritten notes, which sit in a `space-around` flex column beside it, needed no change at all. The privacy card keeps its old centre and its 132 px height to the pixel (`gfBox(88.3,16,111.4,132)` around `gfimg("pcard",92.3,20,103.4,124)`), so **the figure is the same 160 tall and the arrow starts where it always did**. **Measured on both trees, 10 languages × 390 and 360 px × light and dark, 40 contexts: the guide is EXACTLY as tall as v598's in all 40** (0 px, min and max), the empty deck's example card is **3–4 px shorter**, and 0 elements overflow either screen. **The files:** `tools/guide-shots.js` grew two shots and a `max` cap. `front` follows `learn` with no setup on purpose — the three strokes that shot traced are still standing, so the example card shows ink and the next stroke lit; `pcard` stops its crop at `.chrow` for the meaning reason above. The `max` cap is new and was needed: a crop shown ~100 px wide does not need a 644 px file, and these two are the largest crops of the set shown at the smallest size — capped at 320 device px they are **6 478 / 5 562 / 8 592 / 8 284 bytes**, 28 916 in all, taking the guide's set from 84 KB to **113 KB**. All four are **shell assets** (`front` is on the very first screen a fresh install shows) and are purged by `purge-mirror.yml`. **Dead code left with its last user** (the v307 rule): `GF_FILL` and `GF_LAB` had no reader once the drawn character rows were gone; `gfHan` and `gfBox` stay, for the chip's 文 and the two frames. **What it costs, named:** both figures are now half photograph and half drawing, which is honest but is a seam — and the staleness rule of v598 now covers two more screens, the study card's front and the open card's character row, so `node tools/guide-shots.js` belongs in any PR that moves either. **Not regenerated: the five v598 crops.** The generator's painted sign carries random grain, so a full run rewrites all ten files with no visible change; they were restored from git and only the four new ones are in the diff (phone-only deploys, as few files as possible). Suite `verify-sample` (28 checks across six parts: the example card carrying two `<image>`s and not a drawing, the right light and dark files, only one of them painted per scheme, the drawn photo and strokes gone with their circles, the three notes and arrows untouched, the fold bar still drawn and still **under** the crop, the frame and viewBox following the crop's height, a dark phone really taking the dark file on **both** screens, the sixth figure mixed while the first five stay v598 crops, the three drawn text rows gone with the chip's 文 kept, the figure's 160 viewBox held, the same seven files in all ten languages, all four files served as webp under 12 KB each and decoding, nothing squashed against the files' intrinsic ratios, the three version markers one number, the four files in the worker's shell list, and `GF_FILL`/`GF_LAB` no longer declared) — **ALL OK 28 of 28 on v599; on a v598 root 19 of the 28 fail**, and the nine that pass on both are labelled `[control]`/`[guard]` with the reason beside them (the notes and arrows are untouched by design; the ten-language check passes there too, with five files instead of seven, because it guards the rule and not the change). **`verify-onepage` has two of its 33 checks RETARGETED**, one version after v598 retargeted three of the same suite's, and for the same reason: they asserted that the empty deck *drew* its template stroke in `--label3` and *drew* two equal squares, which is the contract this version reverses — they assert the card is that crop and that the crop's ratio is one square over another (~0.49, not 1), and **they fail on a v598 root**. One of them crashed the suite on v598 before it was guarded (`GF_SHOT.front` is undefined there) — the v419 rule, a suite must report and not crash, cost a run. realfig 21/21, deckpace 34/34, square 19/19, delask 44/44, phototile 39/39, memory 38/38, onephoto 30/30, nofree 15/15. Checked by screenshot at 390 px, the empty deck in English light and the privacy figure in both schemes. **No `WHATS_NEW` line** — the v432 rule, as at v598: a first screen that looks like the app is what a learner expects, not a feature. Two `TO_TEST` lines. Not yet field-checked — H's next look at the empty Learn screen (before his first card, or with the deck empty) and at the guide's last section is the check.
- **The guide's six drawn figures become five real crops of the app and one drawing (v598, H, the third of three requests in one message: "Nimm doch echte Screenshots anstatt solche Fantasiesachen"):** **this reverses v549's own decision, and v549's own words are the door it walks through** — "the literal screenshot was measured before it was rejected … a crop of one part of one screen does fit, and a crop of one part of one screen is a figure." Five of the six sections are led by `guide/<name>-{light,dark}.webp` now — **photo** (the app's own crop frame standing on a photographed sign, in the Crop view), **chars** (the line's four character buttons with one picked in the tint), **learn** (the write pad with three strokes traced in ink, the fourth lit with its start dot and the rest template), **cards** (two square picture tiles, one star hollow and one filled) and **lang** (the ten language chips) — and only **privacy** is still drawn, because "what leaves the phone" is the one section with no screen behind it. **v549's four objections, each answered by measurement rather than waved away.** (1) *A whole screen is too tall:* the guide's content width is 329 px, so a 393 px screen scaled into it is 768 px and six of those are 4600 px against 3560 px of prose. What is photographed is one part of one screen — the crops are 173 to 322 px tall at their own scale, and `GF_SHOT` shows each at the height of the drawn figure it replaces. (2) *A screenshot is in ONE of the ten languages:* so **every crop carries no UI prose at all** — pictures, Chinese characters and the three fixed endonym rows, none of which a translation can lengthen (the v427 rule, kept by construction rather than by measurement), and the suite asserts that the same five files are used in all ten languages. **This is the constraint that shaped every crop, and it was nearly broken twice:** the first `chars` crop took the whole `.cstrip` box and pulled the hint sentence "Tap a character to change it…" into frame, and the first `lang` crop took a sliver of the row's own sentence — both were re-cut to the elements' own union. (3) *At 110 KB a screen it is megabytes:* at WebP quality .86 the ten files are **84 434 bytes**, against a 520 KB gzipped shell — one download, +16 %. The WebP is encoded **in the page** by a canvas `toBlob`, so nothing needs an image library. (4) *They go stale at the next layout change* — v549's real argument, and the only one that needed a mechanism: **`tools/guide-shots.js`** regenerates all ten from the app itself in one command. It is self-contained (its own static HTTP server over the repo, its own sign painter, its own pad-stroke driver that follows the app's own medians through `padPt`), it takes the crops at 390 px × 2 in both colour schemes, and it prints each file's aspect ratio with the line "aspect ratios must match GF_SHOT in app.js". **The shipped files are exactly what that script produced**, not what an ad-hoc harness produced — it was run from the repo and its output copied in, so the command is known to work rather than assumed to. **The markup:** `gfshot(name)` emits `<picture><source srcset="…-dark.webp" media="(prefers-color-scheme:dark)"><img class="gf gfs" src="…-light.webp" alt="" aria-hidden="true" style="width:min(100%,h×ar);aspect-ratio:ar">` — **light and dark with no JS at all**, since the app has no theme switch and follows the phone (index.html's `color-scheme`), and `aria-hidden` because the sentences under the figure say the same thing (v549's own rule, kept). **The width rule is the whole layout decision and it is arithmetic, not taste:** `width:min(100%, h × ar)` with `height:auto` means a wide crop fills the column and comes out **shorter** than `h`, while the square write pad sits **centred** at `h × h` — exactly as the drawn pad figure was a 118 px box centred in a 320 px viewBox. No `object-fit`, so nothing can ever be squashed; the inline `aspect-ratio` holds the row's height before the file has decoded. **`GF_SHOT` is `{photo:[1.954,144], chars:[3.276,96], learn:[1,140], cards:[1.958,150], lang:[2.574,130]}`** — the ratio is the file's own and the height is the budget. **THE ONE THING A FIGURE CHANGE MUST NOT COST IS THE GUIDE'S HEIGHT, and it was measured on both trees:** over 10 languages × 390 and 360 px the page is **80–81 px shorter at 390 px and 24–25 px shorter at 360 px** than v597's — the tallest context of the twenty, Russian at 360, goes **3411 → 3386** —, with 0 overflowing elements in the guide and no sideways scroll anywhere. It did not start that way: the first cut used `margin:10px auto` on the image and the guide came out **21 px TALLER at 390 and 65 px taller at 360**, because five figures × 20 px of new margin outweighed the 78 px the shorter figures saved; the margin is `5px auto` (symmetric — the first version was `0 auto 10px`, which put the crop against the panel's top edge and 10 px of `--card2` under it, measured 0/10 and visible) and five heights were trimmed. **The files are SHELL assets, not vendor ones**, and that is deliberate: the guide is a screen a learner opens offline, and a figure that 404s there is worse than no figure — `sw.js` lists all ten and learned the `image/webp` content type (its `TYPES` map had `png` and not `webp`, so the mirror would have served them as `application/octet-stream`), and `purge-mirror.yml` purges them on every push, so a phone without a VPN gets a regenerated figure within one `MIRROR_EVERY`. **Dead code went with the drawings (the v307 rule):** `gfBar`, `gfPhoto`, `gfArrow` and the token `GF_L3` had no reader left once only `privacy` was drawn; `gfig`, `gfBox`, `gfHan` and the other five tokens stay, and the suite asserts both halves. **What it costs, named rather than dressed up:** (a) the language chips are photographed with **English lit**, so a German reader sees the row with English on — true of a fresh install and of the very screen they came from, and the alternative was one figure per language (10 × 2 × 12 KB = 240 KB for one figure, against 84 KB for the whole set); (b) a layout change now makes a figure stale until the command is run, which is the v549 objection answered rather than removed — **the rule is that the regeneration goes in the same PR as the screen change**; and (c) the guide's figures are no longer pure markup, so they cannot follow a future token change by themselves. **What was checked and deliberately not changed:** the empty deck's drawn mock card (`introHTML`) stays a drawing — it is the first screen a learner meets before any photo exists, so there is no deck to photograph, and v596 had just corrected it. Suite `verify-realfig` (21 checks: six sections with five real crops and one drawing; every crop really decoded, so a 404 fails rather than passing silently; the five names with the light file as `src`; a dark `<source>` on `prefers-color-scheme` for each and a dark phone really taking the dark file; nothing squashed — the rendered aspect ratio equals the file's within 1 %; the wide crops filling the column and the square pad centred under it; **the same five files in all ten languages**, which is what says no per-language set is needed; the guide no taller than v597's in Russian at both widths; all ten files served as `image/webp` and under 120 KB together; the dead helpers gone and the drawn figure's own helpers kept; `GF_SHOT` present; and the ten files in the worker's shell list with the webp type) — **ALL OK 21 of 21 on v598; on a v597 root 15 of the 21 fail**, and the six that pass on both are labelled: four `[control]` (the figure sits under its heading, nothing overflows, the guide is really in German, the drawn privacy figure keeps its helpers) and two `[guard]` with the reason written beside them (the screen-reader check cannot fail where there is no `img` at all; the height check compares v597 with its own recorded numbers). **`verify-onepage` is v596's own suite and three of its 33 checks are RETARGETED, not deleted** — they asserted what the drawn photo, Cards and pad figures *drew*, which is exactly the contract this version reverses; they assert the figure is a real crop and which file it is, while what it *shows* is measured where it happens (`verify-square` for the square picture, `verify-phototile` for the square tiles, `verify-nofree` for the pad), and **they fail on a v597 root**, which is what says the retarget is a repair and not a crutch. deckpace 34/34, square 19/19, delask 44/44, phototile 39/39, memory 38/38, onephoto 30/30, nofree 15/15 on v598. A full-DOM overflow scan over **6 screens × 10 languages × 390 and 360 px: the guide 0 in all 20 contexts, and 0 differences against a v597 baseline everywhere else** (the one `tstack` hit per context is the deliberate clipped-plates measurement artefact named since v465). Checked by screenshot at 390 px in English light and German dark, the whole guide. **No `WHATS_NEW` line** — the v432 rule: a help screen that looks like the app is what a learner expects of a help screen, and a note saying the pictures are real would ask them to remember that they were not. One `TO_TEST` line. **Two harness lessons.** The Camera tab lists only what is being worked on (v470), so a card-less photo is invisible there and `[data-crop]` never rendered — the fixture pins it with `S.openShot`, which is `shotDone`'s own last clause, rather than with `todo:true`, which would have made the boot queue it for reading. And `cropRectStyle()` returns "" unless the rect carries `lw`/`lh`, the layer's own size, so the first `photo` crop came out as a photo with no frame on it at all and looked like a working screenshot. Not yet field-checked — H's next look at More → How to use the app is the check: does it read as the app, and is the chip row's English-lit chip a nuisance to a German reader?

## Current state (PWA v597, 2026-09-21)
- **The finished card stands 300 ms less, and the deck is one grid of squares (v597, H in one message: "Bitte die finale Lösung ein kleines bisschen kürzer stehenlassen. Vielleicht 300 Millisekunden kürzer oder so." and "Make the deck square"):** **(1) The pace, and the arithmetic is the whole decision.** v577 took **8 %** off all three recap constants, which is a *share*; H asks for a **flat 300 ms**, so `NEXT_MS` is **3500 → 3200** and `RECAP_MAX` **5600 → 5300** while **`RECAP_SYL` stays 230** — the floor and the cap move together and the growth per syllable does not, so `recapMs` at 1, 2, 4, 8 and 17 syllables is **3200 / 3200 / 3660 / 4580 / 5300 against 3500 / 3500 / 3960 / 4880 / 5600: exactly 300 ms shorter at every length, the card sitting on the cap included**. Scaling all three by 8.6 %, as v577 did, would have taken 300 ms off a short card and **450 off a long one**, which is not what was asked. **Measured end to end through the app's own clock** rather than by a poll — a rAF loop inside the page times from the moment `.recap:not(.one)` appears to the moment `curIdx()` moves — **3206 ms on v597 against 3502 ms on v596** on 供应, a difference of 296. **The star follows by construction and needed no change** (v576's own point): it is placed at `recapMs(d) − POP1`, so it lifts at 2220 ms instead of 2520 and still finishes with the card; the exit still lifts the reading in the dwell's last `RECAP_OUT` 200 ms, and a tap still takes it at once (asserted, under 1.9 s from the tap). **What it costs, named:** the reading-before-the-reward stretch is 2220 ms where v576 raised it to 2520 and v523 had 2000 — still above the number v576 was built to fix, and it is H's own ask. **(2) The deck is square.** After v591–v596 every photo box in the app is a square, and one tile was not: the **multicard's**, **174 × 239 against every other tile's 174 × 174** (at 360 px 159 × 224 against 159 × 159), because its progress bar and its two-line title stood **under** the picture — which is precisely what v593 took off an ordinary tile ("Cards preview bitte als quadratische Foto Tiles ohne text"). Both move **on** to the picture: the bar is the picture's own bottom edge (3 px, a white track with the green fill), the title sits over a gradient scrim in white, still clamped to two lines with its ellipsis — **v593's own number, H's "Two lines are okay for Multicards", is kept rather than reversed**. **The arithmetic then falls out with nothing to tune:** the stack's 9 px of top margin plus the square picture **are** the tile's 174, so `.ctile.page`'s `padding-bottom` goes 9 → 0 and the tile is square by construction at any width. **Two things had to move out of the band's way, and the second is a collision the measurement forced:** the count chip and the flag/AI/not-checked marks go to the picture's **top** corners (a multicard has no star, so that corner is free) — and in the marking the tick owns the top right, so the count **stands down** (`.ctile.page.pick .cnt{display:none}`) rather than sitting under it; the stack of plates is the tell that is left, which is the primary one anyway (v461/v465). **What it costs, named rather than dressed up: the title's text column is 145 px instead of 154**, about one character a line, so a long multicard name is cut a little sooner — measured, "Meituan — order confirmation, 颐堤港店" still shows two lines and its ellipsis, "Midea — wash programmes" still shows whole; and the scrim covers the lower quarter of the picture. **The two tabs never mix** (v477 splits them), so no grid row ever holds a square tile beside a taller one and `align-items:stretch` has nothing to stretch. No key in any column, **`lang.js` byte-identical** — a shape and a number say nothing in words. Suite `verify-deckpace` (34 checks: the three constants with `RECAP_SYL` untouched, the five-length table, a card written stroke by stroke with its recap timed inside the page, the star still lifting out of it, a tap still taking it; the multicard tile square at 390 and 360 px with the title really inside `.tw` over its own gradient, the bar at the picture's bottom edge, nothing below the picture and `padding-bottom` 0, the long title still clamped and cut with its ellipsis and the short one whole, the stack, the count and the marks all still there and in the top corners, a tap still opening that multicard, the marking's tick with the count stood down, German dark at 360 px, and the ordinary tile unchanged as the control) — **ALL OK 34 of 34 on v597; on a v596 root 15 of the 34 fail, every one of them a `[flip]`**, the run reporting `{"ms":3504,"want":3500}` and `{"w":174,"h":239}`, which is both halves of the defect in two objects, and **every `[control]` passes on both trees**. `verify-onepage` 33 of 33, `verify-square` 19 of 19, `verify-delask` 44 of 44, `verify-phototile` 39 of 39 (its multicard checks are the stack, the count, the bar and "shorter than v592's 275.9 px" — all still true of a 174 px tile, so **nothing had to be retargeted**), `verify-memory` 38 of 38, `verify-onephoto` 30 of 30 and `verify-nofree` 15 of 15 on v597. A full-DOM overflow scan over **5 screens × 10 languages × 390 and 360 px — the Multicards tab added to it for this version — gives 0 differences against a v596 baseline, no sideways scroll, and the multicard tile square with its title at two lines in all twenty contexts**; the one element the scan reports is `.tstack`, whose offset plates are clipped on purpose and which measures identically on v596 (the v465 measurement bug, named again so it is not chased a third time). Checked by screenshot at 390 px in English light and German dark and at 360 px. **No `WHATS_NEW` line** — the v432/v591 rule for the tile (a shape a learner reads as the app simply being drawn properly, with nothing moved out of reach) and the v412/v577 rule for the dwell (a pacing correction to something shipped, where a note saying the card waits less reads as an apology). Two `TO_TEST` lines. Not yet field-checked — H's next finished card is the check (is 3.2 s still enough to read?), and his next look at the Multicards tab: a deck of squares, with the name still readable on the picture.

on a frame **taller than wide** the square is **narrower** (a vertical sign 1050×700 → 700×700), so the text comes out **bigger** (0.36 → 0.53 of the box's width). **A window is a target, not a promise:** `windowRect` still clamps to the photo, so a frame wider than the photo is tall keeps the photo's own height (1400×1200, ar 1.167) — asserted, since a suite that demanded 1.000 everywhere would be asserting something the code has never done. **Measured at 390 px: the open card's box 322 × 214.7 → 322 × 322**, the picture fitted in it with the blurred fill behind, nothing clipped; **the learning card is byte-identical on both trees** — cue 322 × 311, pad 311 × 311 at the same pixel, the card ending at 766 against a tab bar at 782.5 — because the study cue's picture box is sized by the frame's own grid row (v560) and not by `--pr`, so **the frame does not move for the content**, which is v560's rule and the one thing a shape change must not break. **What it costs, named: the open card's picture box is 107 px taller**, so the actions and the fold sit that much further down and the page scrolls a little sooner — the price of the square H asked for. **THE DECK IS NOT CUT AGAIN, and that is H's own word: “in Zukunft”.** `RECUT_V` stays at 5, so every card already on the phone keeps the 3:2 picture it was cut with and shows it fitted in the square box between two bands of blur — exactly what v591 already does in every small box, and what the screenshot of an older card shows. **A re-cut is one constant away** (`RECUT_V` 6 with the v519 mechanism, ~95 ms a card, no undo, and only cards that still have a stored frame and their photo), and it waits for H's word, as v519's own re-cut did (“3:2 with the re-cut”). **Two lists had to learn the old shape or the change would have cost something silently:** `spotRatios()` is `[CARD_RATIO,1.5,16/9,2,4/3]` — without the **1.5** every card cut between v519 and v594 would lose **the mark on its photo** (v533/v552) the moment CARD_RATIO stopped being 3:2, since that mark is derived by recognising which window the picture is; ## Current state (PWA v590, 2026-09-21)
- **A stroke that missed goes the moment one fits, on every pad that has a template (v590, H with a screenshot of his 蜜 card — the character half traced under three thick black scribbles — and a full Diagnostics dump: "So freestyle Striche dürfen nicht stehen bleiben."):** **his own traced-stroke log is the whole diagnosis and the photo was not needed** — `蜜 stroke 6 missed`, `蜜 stroke 6 missed`, `蜜 stroke 6 snapped at 0.06`, `蜜 stroke 7 missed`: two failed attempts at a stroke he then wrote **correctly**, and they stood on the pad for the rest of the character. **The cause is one clause of v570 and it is named in v582's own entry as the price of taking the buttons away** ("a learner who scribbles one slip and then traces cleanly carries that slip's ink to the end of the character with no way to rub it out"): `if(!st.hw) st.free.length=0` — a slip goes at the next stroke that fits **only while the pad is still judging stroke by stroke**, and after two misses in a row `st.hw` is on for good, so from then every slip is kept. Kept for a reason: the loose ink **is** the drawing v141's matcher judges, and a stroke that vanished cannot be written beside (v570). **The clause is `if(!st.hw||st.k)` now: a stroke that FITS the lit template stroke is evidence that the learner is tracing**, so whatever loose ink stands is a failed attempt and not part of a freehand character — while a freehand write from the very first stroke has `st.k` at 0 and keeps its ink untouched. **Measured on the shipped code, both trees, H's own sequence driven with real pointer strokes:** three strokes traced, two slips, then the stroke written correctly — **v588 free 2, v590 free 0**; one more slip after it, which is where his screenshot sits — **v588 three strokes standing, v590 one** (screenshots of the pad taken on both); and the character traced to its end — **v588 flashes green with three scribbles over it, v590 with none**. **THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG AND WAS MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS REJECTED:** clearing the ink on **every** snap (`st.free.length=0` unconditionally) breaks v570's own headline case — the character written in **reverse** order snaps its very last stroke onto template stroke 0, so the unconditional clear wipes the seven strokes the matcher was about to judge and the write is **refused** (measured on a third serving root: `k:1, free:0, accepted false`, against `k:8, accepted, not helped` on v588 and v590 alike). That is why the `st.k` clause is load-bearing rather than decorative, and why the suite's reverse-order check is labelled a **guard** that passes on both trees: it cannot fail on v588, and it does fail on the candidate this version rejected. **What still stands, named rather than glossed:** the stroke the learner has just drawn wrong stays until the next one fits — that is v570's own rule and the shake's companion, the one thing on the pad that says *this is what you drew* —, and a run of consecutive misses piles up (measured on 供: five or six strokes stand while the learner keeps missing, Skip arriving at four, and all of them go at the first stroke that fits). **The one case that cannot be cleaned without cost is the freehand write itself**, where the ink is the character being judged. **Named and not built, since it narrows a documented capability and so waits for H's word (the size gate):** capping the loose ink to the learner's **last** attempt whenever a template stroke has already been traced (`st.k>0`) — the pad would then never carry more than one stray stroke, at the price of the mixed write, where a learner traces the first strokes and then writes the rest freehand (today that still reaches acceptance, since `st.k` plus the loose ink can reach the character's stroke count; with the cap it never could). **Nothing else moves:** `tryHand`'s own drop past `matchTol` (v582), the free pad's Undo and Clear for a character the stroke set lacks, v589's Skip, the quiet miss, the misses rolled back on acceptance (v570's `st.mm0`) and the advance's own clear are untouched, and `lang.js` and `styles.css` are **byte-identical** — ink that no longer stands says nothing in words. Suite `verify-inkgone` (12 checks: three strokes traced with nothing loose, one slip standing while the pad still judges stroke by stroke and going at the next stroke that fits, two slips turning the quiet judging on with **neither Undo nor Clear appearing** (v582), then the failed attempts going at the stroke he writes correctly, his own sequence leaving **one** stroke standing and not three, the finished character flashing green with nothing loose; and the reverse-order write still accepted and not counted as helped with its own ink standing until the matcher had judged it) — **ALL OK 12 of 12 on v590; on a v588 root the three `[flip]` checks fail with H's own numbers, and on the rejected candidate the two `[guard]` checks fail instead.** `verify-memory` **38 of 38** on v590, so v589's contracts are untouched. **No `WHATS_NEW` line** — the v418/v432/v582 rule: ink that appeared uninvited and no longer does is a correction, and a note telling a learner that their wrong strokes no longer stay on the pad reads as an apology for the version that let them. One `TO_TEST` line. **And one thing the probe reproduced by accident, which is v589's own named-not-built item (f) a third time:** a slip drawn in the pad's lower left corner is swallowed by `#pad-show`, so three of nine deliberate misses never reached the canvas at all — the helper buttons still sit inside the pad's square. Not yet field-checked — H's next card is the check: he writes a stroke wrong, it stands while he looks at it, and it is gone the moment the next one fits.

Two More sentences name sections that were renamed at v547 (`More → Your data` → **Your cards**, "switch that off under Privacy" → **under More → Usage sharing**), and **the card detail's schedule line loses the SM-2 jargon it printed to the learner** — "Interval 1 d, ease 2.50, 1 review, next 19/09/2026" is "1 review so far, next on 19/09/2026" (the v551 named-not-built item, closed). **Six dead section-head keys leave all nine columns** (Update notes, Your data, Online AI review, About, Privacy, Help — each confirmed absent from `app.js`), and **six count sentences are corrected at n=1** (the v412 rule: fr/es "{0} flagged for review", "{0} selected", "{0} checked, {1} left.", "{0} translated, {1} left."; de/fr/es "({0} could not be read)"; ru "Delete {0} old photos?"). **480 → 474 keys a column, ru 509 → 503, en 15**, and a string-aware scan of the source agrees with the evaluated count in all ten columns, so no duplicate (the v371 trap); the 184 placeholder "drifts" are the count words, whose value carries `{0}` by construction (v538's own standing finding, 180 then). **(2) `var(--ui)` is referenced twice in `styles.css` and is DEFINED NOWHERE in the repo's history, and an undefined var kills the WHOLE declaration:** `.foldbtn{font:500 15px var(--ui)}` lost its weight and its size, so the "Whole card" row has rendered at the card's inherited **17 px / 400** instead of 15 px / 500 on every study card and every open card for as long as the rule has existed (measured 17/400 → 15/500, the row still 36 px); and `.done .intro .note span{font-family:'Bradley Hand',…,var(--ui)}` dropped the **whole handwriting stack**, so v569's scribbled notes — H's own "handschriftlich am besten auch noch" — could never render in a handwriting face at all. Both take `var(--sans)`. **The rule it stands for: a CSS custom property that is never defined fails silently and takes its whole declaration with it — the only way to find one is to grep every `var(--x)` against the `:root` list.** **(3) The uncovered half was half empty and the answer now takes the room the tiles leave.** `textFit` walks down from `CH_BIG` 96 and a short word stops at the cap, while `th` never shrinks below the pad's height — measured on v588, a one-, two- or three-character card showed **160 px of white (49.5 % of the half)** at 393 px and 96 px at 360, split evenly above and below. `splitFit`'s txt branch writes `--plz`, the factor by which the answer line may grow into that room, and `.card.study.bigtxt .cue .padline` scales its rows with it, capped at `PL_MAX` 1.9 **and at what the widest row can take** — the rows are `nowrap` with an ellipsis on the meaning, so a line fitted only to the height would have been cut ("to pro…", measured on the first cut). **(4) Skip fills the character in, which is what its label says and what the guide has promised since v512.** Until v588 it advanced **one stroke** and then hid itself again (`st.miss=0`), so passing 供 (8 strokes) took **29 wrong strokes and 7 taps on Skip — 36 actions**, measured end to end through real pointer events; on v589 the same card takes **4 and 1**. The character is marked helped exactly as before, so the card is still graded `again` and scores no point. **(5) A character the stroke set lacks can be finished at all.** On a free pad (鼀, 龘, 齉) nothing ever called `miss()`, so `st.miss` stayed **0 for ever**, Show me and Skip could never appear, and a Done the print model would not recognise left the card with **no way to finish** — a swipe grades nothing, so it stayed due for ever. A refused Done is a try now and Skip arrives after four of them: measured, v588 `miss 0 / skip hidden` after four refused Done taps, v589 `miss 4 / skip shown`, and the tap finishes the card. **(6) The reward left mid-flight no longer freezes the counter.** `praiseStart` early-returns when the pad is off the screen — the learner tapped another tab during the dwell — **without clearing `PRAISE_N`**, and `go()`'s own fallback is skipped because `pr` is truthy, so the header kept showing the number from **before** the card: measured, write a clean card and tap More during the dwell and v588 reads **★ 0 while `praiseDay()` is 2**, still 0 on returning to Learn; v589 clears it and the counter reads **2**. And `adv()` moves the index whatever screen is up — the card is already written and recorded by then, so leaving Learn must not leave the session standing on it (the redraw and the scroll still wait for Learn; the other three guards, which mean the state really was superseded, are unchanged). **(7) The card detail's back button never breaks in two.** `.topline` gave neither child `nowrap`, so a long status badge — ru «Не проверено, перевод ещё не готов», id "Belum diperiksa, menunggu terjemahan" — shrank the **back button** below its own content and **← stacked over "Карточки"**: the way out of a card rendering as a mistake, the row 41.8 → 63.5 px. `.topline .del{flex:none;white-space:nowrap}`; the badge is prose and wraps instead. Measured ru 63.5 → 41.8 at both widths, id@360 the same. **(8) More's rows keep their buttons inside the card at 360 px.** The text column cannot shrink below its longest word and pushed the `.btnrow` (`flex:none`) out: the German Import button hung **8.6 px out of its own card**, the Russian Flagged-cards row ran **11.6 px past it with "Поделиться" sliced by the screen edge**, and the Spanish one 12.6 px past its content box. **The obvious fix is wrong and was measured before it was rejected:** a plain `flex-wrap:wrap` wraps on MAX-content, so it moved **every** row's button under its text in every language (+207 px of More in English at 393 px, +308 in Korean and Thai) — and `min-width:0` with `overflow-wrap` broke **seven ordinary Russian words mid-letter** (v432 had already rejected `min-width:0` for reflowing the Mirror row). `flex:1 1 min-content` on the text column wraps only when the two really cannot share a line: measured over 10 languages × 393 and 360 px, **0 buttons past the card, 0 sideways scroll, and not one row changes shape where it fitted**; a wrapped button is right-aligned like `.fieldacts` (v257). **(9) A checkbox's box sits level with the first line of its label.** With `align-items:center` a four-line label (de@360 "Fotos einschließlen (etwa 0.0 MB mehr)") put the tick box **31.5 px down, level with line 3 of 4**, and a five-line Russian one 42.4 px — the control a learner must tap a third of the way down the sentence it belongs to. Measured over five languages × both widths, the offset is now **−1.0 px at every line count** (1, 2, 3, 4 and 5), a one-line label keeps its 44 px touch target, and a multi-line one grows by the 11 px of padding that buys it. **(10) The guide says what the app sends without being asked.** More's "What is sent" and `privacy.html` have named v586's no-tap description fetch since v586; the guide's own privacy paragraph never did, so the one screen a learner reads to find out what leaves the phone was the one that left it out — one clause in all ten columns, phrased against each column's own wording in More (the v459/v534 rule: honesty in the same PR). **(11) The empty deck's drawn card is the card the app actually shows.** `introHTML`'s mock drew the photo, the character tiles and the pad at once — v564's card, which has been impossible since v580 made the cue two states — so the one screen a learner meets before their first photo showed a layout the app cannot produce. It is the front state now — the photo, the pad drawing 工 with one stroke written, the next lit with its dot and the third still template, and the fold row — and the three notes point at the photo, the pad and the fold in that order. **(12) A long press held a moment longer deleted the card it had just marked.** `longPress` installs a capture-phase click eater when the press **fires** and takes it off after a fixed `LP_EAT` 250 ms, so the eater's window is `[LP_MS, LP_MS+LP_EAT]` — **500 to 750 ms measured from the press, not from the release** — and any finger that lifts later sends a live click. Two things then happen, and both were driven end to end with CDP touch holds on both trees: the mark is toggled **straight off again** (v588: a 760, 900 or 1200 ms hold on a card tile leaves `PICK.set.size` **0** where a 700 ms hold leaves 1), and where the tile lies under the pickbar that has just appeared, the click lands on its **Delete** button — measured, a 1.2 s hold on the spot Delete then occupies gives **cards 4 → 3, "Deleted “鸡蛋”"**, with only the five-second Undo between the learner and a lost card. Half a second is the floor of a deliberate hold, not its length, so this is reachable by the ordinary gesture rather than by an edge case. The eater is armed until `pointerup` or `pointercancel` plus `LP_EAT` for the click the browser sends after them, with `LP_MAX` 5000 as the backstop for a pointerup that never arrives (a lost pointer would otherwise eat every click for the session). Measured on v589: 700, 760, 900 and 1200 ms all leave exactly **one** card marked and delete nothing, a plain tap still opens the card, a tap on a second tile still adds to the mark and a second tap on it still unmarks. **The rule it stands for: a guard whose lifetime is a timer from the moment it was armed does not cover the gesture it guards — end it on the event that ends the gesture.** **Dead code and stale records:** `wireChars` (no caller since v536, only a comment named it), `.tags .n` and `.tags .r` (the New/Review pills v512 removed), the `.cue` comment still describing v564's two halves, `(fitPad)` for `(_fitPad)`, `sw.js`'s "~15 MB" for the vendor cache that has held **~23 MB** since v517's 7.3 MB of outlines, and `privacy.html`'s "More → Online AI review" for the row v547 renamed **AI review**. Suite `verify-memory` (38 checks: the fold row's own font and its unchanged height; the answer growing into the empty half with no row cut and the pad unmoved; Skip filling the character in and the free pad's four refused Done taps earning Skip; the counter after a tab tap mid-dwell; the back button on one line in ru and id; More's buttons inside the card at 360 px; the checkbox box level with the first line at one to five lines; the guide, the hint and the empty deck's notes in en and de; the guide naming the no-tap fetch; the long press at 1.2 s marking one card and deleting nothing on the spot Delete then covers; the key counts and the dead keys) — **ALL OK 38 of 38 on v589; on a v588 root 27 of the 38 fail** and the eleven that pass on both are labelled controls in the file. A full-DOM overflow scan over 9 screens × 10 languages × 393 and 360 px: **180 contexts compared, 6 differ and every one of the six is an improvement** (the ru and id back button no longer breaks, the de, es and ru More buttons no longer overflow), 0 page errors. A `WHATS_NEW` line, five `TO_TEST` lines. **NAMED AND NOT BUILT — each changes how H handles the app, so each waits for his word (the size gate), and every one of them was measured, not read:** **(a) after one tap the card is dealt face-up for the rest of the session and across restarts** — `S.cueBig` is session state and neither `stepCard`, `adv()` nor boot resets it, so a learner who taps once out of curiosity gets every later card with the translation showing and no picture, which is the opposite of a memory game; **it reverses v568 on purpose** ("wenn ich irgendwas groß gemacht habe, dann bleibt es immer so lange groß"), which is why it is described rather than taken; **(b) on a card of more than one word the tap shows the FIRST WORD's pinyin and meaning, not the card's** — 鸡蛋供应 "egg supply" uncovers "鸡 jī fowl / 鸡蛋 jī dàn egg", and the card's own reading lives only behind the separate "Whole card" fold; **(f) the helper buttons sit inside the pad's square** (`#pad-show` is 81 × 40 px inside its 323 px side), so a stroke begun in a lower corner is silently lost — **reproduced by accident here: this session's own probe lost four strokes to `#pad-show` before the fixture was moved off the corner**, which is v570's own lesson repeating; **(g) at 360 × 640 the pad is 33 px narrower than the cue above it and the fold row below it** (259 against 292), so v560's "the pad is as wide as the card's inner width" is false on a short screen; **(h) the star counter is a 51 × 28 px button and the review flag 36 × 36**, both under the project's own 44 px rule, and **the review flag is clipped away entirely while the text is big**. **And one standing record is corrected:** CLAUDE.md has carried since v284, and repeated at v401, v402, v432 and v551, that the German and French admin log-in row runs past the viewport — **v537 fixed it and the note was never updated; measured now, `scrollWidth === clientWidth` and the button sits exactly on the card's inner edge in all ten languages at both widths.** Not yet field-checked — H's next session is the check: does Skip now do what it says, and does the app read like the game he described?

- **Check-up fills in what a card is missing while it checks it, and the two rows that used to do that are gone (v588, H in three messages: "Wenn alle Karten oder auch eine Karte mit AI nochmal gecheckt werden, dann gehört der Explain-Text zu dem Update natürlich mit dazu.", then "Descriptions brauchen keinen separaten Punkt unter More. Das sollte alles direkt über Check AI abgefrühstückt werden.", then "Das gleiche gilt für Tags."):** **the finding that settles it was measured, not assumed — the full text check has asked for `"desc"` since v529 and for `"kind"` since v364, in the same JSON, on every card**, and `aiAsk` hands both back on every answer (`desc:x.bad?"":saneDesc(x.desc,zh)`, `kind:String(x.kind||"").trim()`). So Check-up has been **receiving a description and a kind for every card it checked and throwing them away** — `recheckAll` compared only `zh`/`p`/`m` and `continue`d on a card the answer agreed with, which on a healthy deck is nearly every card; and `aiReview`, which stores the answer whole, only reached a card that had something to flag. That is why the two extra runs existed at all, and it is why folding them in **costs nothing**: not one extra call, not one extra token. **`aiExtras(upd,a)` is the one helper**, applied wherever an AI answer lands on a card — `aiReview` (the Review queue's Ask AI and the automatic run, so **one** card checked by hand gets it too, which is the first of H's three messages), `recheckAll` (the whole deck), and `aiAccept` (which already wrote the description since v529 and now writes the tag with it). It writes **the description when the answer's differs from the card's in the app's language** (`descOf` is language-current, so a card described in English gets its German one on a German phone — asserted) and **the kind tag only on a card that carries no tag at all** (v368's own rule, so a tag of H's own is never touched — asserted). **Why these two may be written where the text may not, stated rather than glossed:** v370's reason for never applying a re-check is that on a saved card the reader's per-character confidences are gone, so the v143 guard cannot run and an applied answer would silently rewrite characters every pass had read clearly — **that is about the TEXT**. A description overwrites no reading and a tag overwrites nothing at all, so neither waits for Accept; the text, pinyin and meaning still become a suggestion with its tick and cross exactly as before (asserted: the one card whose meaning really changed keeps its `ai` box). **The run is undoable, with the v587 store:** `saveLastRun("check",["ds","tags"],before,n)`, the `before` map accumulated across the run and written **after every batch**, so a run stopped half way is undoable too; the Undo row reads "Checked 12 cards at 14:32." and one tap puts every `ds` and `tags` back, memory and IndexedDB (asserted both ways). **What went, whole:** `tagAll`, `TAGALL`, `TAG_BATCH`, `toTag`, the tag stage with its four helpers, `applyTagStage`, `rememberTagRun`, `resumeTagAll`, `tagRowHTML`, `tagRefresh` — and v587's own `describeAll`, `DESCALL`, `DESC_BATCH`, `toDescribe`, `rememberDescRun`, `resumeDescAll`, `descLine`, `descRowHTML`, `descRefresh` — 122 lines, plus the `tagOnly` branch of `aiCardPayload` (the v307 rule: its one producer is gone), the settings `tagStage`, `tagRun` and `descRun` from `RESET_KEYS`, the two `resumeXAll()` calls from each of the three resume sites, the two guards from `reloadIdle` and from `undoRunHTML`, and the two lines from `resetAll`. **v587's row lived for one version and that is the honest record**: its measurement — that half of H's ask was already true since v529 — stands and is what this version is built on; only its row was the wrong shape. **The Check-up row says what it now does** (the honesty rule, in the same PR): "The AI keeps getting better. Let it look at your whole deck again — it fills in the descriptions and tags that are missing, and you see every change to a text before you accept it.", and the finished line reports both halves — "Done — 6 cards filled in, 1 card could be better. Look under the Cards tab." (`RECHECK.filled` beside `found`; four shapes, each a whole key per column so no verb or pronoun agrees across a key boundary — the v412 rule: fr and es take label shapes, "Terminé – complété : {0} ; il y a {1} à améliorer.", ru «Готово — дополнено: {0}; можно улучшить: {1}.»). **More's "What is sent" and `privacy.html` go from four buttons to two** ("…when you tap Check-up or Translate all…", "**Three buttons** send card text because you pressed them"), one key replaced in all ten columns with each column's own two button words, and the resume clause and the switch clause on the privacy page with them. **Fourteen dead keys leave all nine columns and three arrive: 491 → 480 a column, ru 520 → 509, en 15**, no duplicate in any of the ten (a string-aware scan of the source agrees with the evaluated count in all ten — the v371 trap), and the static key check reports only its standing hits. **The guide needed no change and that was checked rather than assumed** (the v259 rule): no guide sentence in any of the ten columns named Tag all or the descriptions. **What it costs, named:** the deck's descriptions and tags now come **only** through Check-up, which sends every card's text, pinyin and meaning where Tag all sent ten cards a call for one word and Describe all five a call for a paragraph — so a deck of ~270 cards is **~55 calls once** instead of ~54 + ~17 + ~55, against the relay's DeepSeek cap of 400 a day; and a run that used to write nothing now writes, so the one-deep undo store is spent by it (the v369 rule, unchanged). **`RECHECK.filled` counts cards, not fields**, so a card that got both a description and a tag counts once. Measured over **10 languages × 390 and 360 px: 0 new overflowing elements** — byte-identical to a v587 root, whose two standing hits are the German Import row and the Russian Flagged-cards row (the v432 findings) — widest button 258 px. Suite `verify-checkextras` (28 checks: no Tags row and no Descriptions row under Learning with Check-up still there and nothing offering the two runs; the row's new sentence; a run over six cards writing the description and the kind tag on every card the answer agreed with, in memory and on disk, while the one card whose meaning changed keeps its suggestion **and** gets its description, and a card with a tag of H's own keeps it; one plain check payload with no `explain` or `tagOnly` run beside it; the combined done line; the undo store with `kind:"check"` and keys `ds,tags`, the Undo row and Undo putting every card back on disk; one flagged card checked from the Review queue getting both in one call; the German phone writing the German description beside the English one; More's sentence and privacy.html) — **ALL OK 28 of 28 on v588; on a v587 root 12 of 17 fail and the run then dies at the missing `#undo-run`** (the v419 rule), the five that pass on both labelled controls. `verify-explainblock` 35 of 35, `verify-explainprefetch` 16 of 16, `verify-twostate` 38 of 38 and `verify-nofreeui` 21 of 21 on v588. A `WHATS_NEW` line, and **`WHATS_NEW[587]` goes with the row it named** (the v534 rule: a note describing a control that no longer exists is not a record but a false instruction, and 587 and 588 reach every phone in one update); one `TO_TEST` line, replacing v587's and v368's. **Named, not built:** a card whose description the AI would improve is only re-described when the new text really differs, so a run over a fully described deck writes nothing and reports "nothing to change" — right, and it also means Check-up is now the only way to refresh a description in bulk. ## Current state (PWA v587, 2026-09-21)
- **Every card can be given its description, and the deck is filled in from one button (v587, H: "Bitte explain direkt beim erstellen der Karte laden und speichern. Bzw für alle Karten nachladen, wenn möglich."):** **the first half was measured rather than assumed, and it has been true since v529 — no code was needed for it.** Five write sites were traced: `readingCard` takes the description out of the text check's own answer (`sg.ai.desc`, set by `signAskAI`) or out of the picture answer that replaced the reading (the weak path and `picOnBad` both carry `desc` onto `sg.ai`), the Add form's autofill stores `S.draft.ai.desc`, the Edit form's Ask AI stores `aiDesc` at Save changes, **Accept** on a waiting suggestion stores `a.desc`, and Translate all carries the new language's description with its meaning. So a card the AI checks has been born with one for 58 versions. **What is genuinely left over is what the new row is for, and it is named rather than glossed:** every card made before v529 — the bulk of H's ~270 —, a card the check called `bad` or that was made offline, and **a panel's labels**, where `splitCards` blanks the description on purpose (`picSystem()` asks the model for `""` when `apart` is true: it gives one description for the whole picture, and "this is a washing machine panel" on the 羊毛 card would be false — the run asks per label text instead, which is right). **The row** is More → Learning → **Descriptions**, between Tags and Check-up: the sentence "A few sentences about what a card's text says and where you meet it. New cards get them with the AI check.", the line "No description yet on 21 cards." and **Describe all cards**, shown only while such a card exists and an AI is set up. It is built like Tag all (v368) — the run's state in `DESCALL` and not in the row (v257's rule), the run remembered in setting `descRun` until no card is left, resumed 2.5 s after boot, on reconnect and on foreground **while the AI switch is ticked** (v476), the moving bar with the live count, and v369's Undo last run. **THE ONE DELIBERATE DEPARTURE FROM BOTH PRECEDENTS: the cards are written batch by batch, not staged to the end.** Translate all and Tag all stage because a half-done deck would be **inconsistent** — H's own v264 ask, no deck of mixed languages; a deck where some cards carry a description and some do not has been the normal state since v529, so an interrupted run may keep what it got. Measured in the suite: the connection dies after the first batch and **five of seven cards keep their description on disk**, where a staged run would have written none; the undo store is accumulated across the run and written after **every** batch, so a run stopped half way is undoable too. **`DESC_BATCH` is 5** — Translate all's five rather than Tag all's ten, since two or three sentences a card is the longest answer of the three runs. **What it costs, named:** one call per five cards, so H's ~270 cards are about **54 calls**, against the relay's DeepSeek cap of 400 a day (`textProvider()` sends the text check to DeepSeek, not to Qwen, whose cap is 80) — the whole deck fits inside one day, and the resume carries it over if it does not. The payload asks for the description alone (`explain`, v529's own `why` — "write \"desc\" for this card and nothing else; keep zh, p and m exactly as given"), so a run **cannot** change a text, a pinyin or a meaning; that is asserted, as is the fact that a card which already has one is never sent. **`toDescribe()` is language-current** (`descOf` reads `LANG`): a card described in English counts as undescribed on a German phone, exactly as Translate all counts its meanings — asserted, the German row reading "Noch keine Beschreibung auf 2 Karten." over a deck where one of the two carries `ds.en`. A page card is never counted (`isPage`). `descRun` joins `RESET_KEYS` (the v458 rule — it is keyed by nothing, but it is a run's state and Start over must not leave one armed), `DESCALL` joins `resetAll`'s in-memory wipe and `reloadIdle`'s hold, and `undoRunHTML` gains both its guard and its line. **Honesty in the same PR, since the change makes two standing sentences false:** More's "What is sent" names the new button ("…when you tap Check-up, Translate all, Tag all or Describe all cards…", one key replaced in all ten columns with each column's own button word), and `privacy.html` goes from "Four buttons" to "**Five buttons**", names Describe all cards among the runs that send every card, and names it in the resume clause and in the switch clause. **Eight keys in nine columns: 483 → 491 a column, ru 512 → 520, en 15**, no duplicate in any of the ten (a `grep` of each new key's own `"key":` form gives exactly 9), no placeholder drift, and **every count line rendered at one card in all ten columns** — the v412 rule, no verb or pronoun agreeing across a key boundary: fr and es take the label shape ("Descriptions : {0}, il reste {1}.") because "1 carte décrites" is wrong, and ru is «Пока без описания: {0}.» because «у {0}» would want the genitive that `nOf` cannot give. **The guide needed no change and that was checked rather than assumed** (the v259 rule): of the ten columns' keys only five name Explain or a description at all, and not one of them is a guide sentence — v549's cut took it out. Measured over **10 languages × 393 and 360 px: 0 overflowing elements, every button label on one line**, widest 278 px (ru) in a card of about 322/292, the row 168–208 px tall. Suite `verify-describeall` (20 checks: the row with its sentence, its count and its button, counting neither the described card nor the page card; the tap making **one** call for three cards that asks for the description alone and names none of the described one; every card carrying it in memory and in IndexedDB; the Undo row naming the run and Undo putting all three back on disk with the row offering the run again; a run cut off after its first batch keeping those five on disk with the two untouched, the line "5 described, 2 left." and the run remembered; the connection back and a reload finishing the deck **with no tap** and forgetting the run; the AI review unticked sending nothing from a remembered run; a deck with a description on every card offering no row; More's sentence and privacy.html; the German row, and a card described in English counting as undescribed there; the four count lines at one card in all ten columns; no page error) — **ALL OK 20 of 20 on v587; on a v586 root the first two checks fail and the run then dies at the missing button** (the v419 rule). `verify-explainblock` 35 of 35, `verify-explainprefetch` 16 of 16, `verify-twostate` 38 of 38 and `verify-nofreeui` 21 of 21 on v587, so v580's, v582's, v585's and v586's contracts are untouched. Checked by screenshot at 393 × 869 in light and German dark. A `WHATS_NEW` line (a learner notices a row that fills in their whole deck), one `TO_TEST` line. **Named, not built:** a card whose creation-time answer carried no description is not asked again at the moment it is made — it waits for this row, or for v586's own prefetch when H next comes to it, which is one call either way; and a twenty-label panel costs twenty calls here where the picture answer paid for one description it could not split. ## Current state (PWA v586, 2026-09-21)
- **The description is fetched before the fold is tapped (v586, H on v585 the same hour: "Bitte fang schon an, Explain zu laden, bevor ich überhaupt auf Whole Card getippt habe. Um schneller zu sein."):** v585 put the description inside the Whole card block and had the app ask for one by itself — but only **while the block stood open**, so on an older card H tapped the fold and then watched a busy bar for the three to ten seconds the provider takes. **The ask no longer waits for the fold at all.** `explainSoon(d)` starts it `EXPLAIN_LEAD` **1200 ms** after the card comes up, from both render sites (`if(ansOpen) explainAuto(d); else explainSoon(d);` in `renderStudy`, and the same on the open card under Cards), so on a card written stroke by stroke for ten or twenty seconds (v512) the answer is on the record long before the tap — **measured: with the provider answering in 900 ms, the tap shows the paragraph at once where a v585 root shows the busy bar.** `explainAuto` keeps every one of its guards and is unchanged: `aiAutoOn()`, a stored answer, a running call and a failure each stand it down, so nothing is asked twice and a dead network is not retried on every render. **THE WAIT IS THE COST CONTROL, not a nicety, and it is what makes this affordable:** a card merely **swiped past** is gone well under 1200 ms and costs nothing (one timer for the app — another card cancels it), while a card being written is ten to twenty seconds, so the learner never waits for the wait. **And a render of the SAME card does not restart it** (`EXPLAIN_AT` holds the card the timer is for), or a card re-rendered on every stroke would push its own fetch for ever — the suite drives thirteen renders at 200 ms and asserts **exactly one** call, which catches both failure modes at once (0 would mean the wait restarts, 2+ that it is not once per card). **At the moment it fires the card must still be on the screen**, and that is tested as "the DOM still carries its landing place" (`[data-desc]`) rather than by asking which screen is up — one line, no knowledge of modes, and it covers Learn, the open card and leaving either of them. **What it costs, named and not dressed up: one AI call for every description-less card H stays on for 1.2 s, whether or not he ever opens the block** — where v585 charged one per card whose fold he opened. On a twenty-card session of older cards that is twenty calls to `textProvider()` (DeepSeek, the relay's own cap 400 a day, shared with the text check on every new card and with Check-up), and each of those cards' text leaves the phone with no tap. It is paid **once per card for good** (the description is stored, so the deck's ~270 cards cost ~270 calls spread over the sessions it takes to meet them), and a phone with the AI review unticked pays nothing at all. **So `privacy.html` and More's own "What is sent" sentence are corrected rather than left standing:** the page's AI bullet now says the app asks "when you come to a card that has no description yet — in Learn, or by opening it under Cards … a moment after the card appears and without waiting for you to open **Whole card**", dated 21 September 2026, and the sentence in **all ten columns** has one clause replaced, no key added or removed — "and for one card when you come to it and it has no description yet" for v585's "…when you open Whole card and the card has no description yet" (de „sobald du zu ihr kommst", ru «как только ты до неё дойдёшь», th with no politeness particle); **483 a column, ru 512, en 15**, unchanged, the new key string standing exactly once per column and the old one nowhere in `lang.js` or `app.js`. **Named, not built:** prefetching the **next** card of the session as well (`S.queue[S.idx+1]`) would have the description in hand before H even arrives — and it doubles the calls on a deck of older cards, which is a cost decision rather than a speed one, so it waits for H's word. Suite `verify-explainprefetch` (16 checks: nothing within 300 ms of the card, so the ask is not instant; the card left folded and untouched asking **once** with the description on the record and **nothing on the screen**; the tap then showing the text at once against a deliberately slow provider, and asking nothing a second time; a card swiped past before the lead never asked about; thirteen renders at 200 ms giving exactly one call; the AI review off sending nothing; a card that already has a description asking nothing; the open card under Cards with its block folded away asked about too, with nothing visible; a dead network asked about once — one ask, v201's one retry included —, the opened block then carrying the failure with its one button, and a render not trying again; no page error) — **ALL OK 16 of 16 on v586; on a v585 root 7 of the 16 fail and every one of them is a `[flip]`**, the one `[guard]` labelled in the file with the reason it is vacuous there (v585 asks nothing without a tap, so "a card swiped past costs nothing" cannot bite on it). **`verify-explainblock` is retargeted by one check and is 35 of 35** — its "nothing is asked while it is folded" is the contract this version reverses on purpose, and the file says so where the check stood; `verify-twostate` 38 of 38 and `verify-nofreeui` 21 of 21 on v586, so v580's and v582's frames are untouched. **No `WHATS_NEW` line and no new screenshot** — the v412/v432 rule: nothing on the screen looks different, v585's own note ("the app fetches it for an older card by itself") is still true of what is on the phone, and a note saying a wait is shorter reads as an apology for the wait. One `TO_TEST` line replacing v585's, since the check is one act. Not yet field-checked — H's next tap on Whole card is the check: the text already standing there, with no bar.

## Current state (PWA v575, 2026-09-20)
- **The mark on the photo is dragged along when the photo is opened and closed (v575, H: "Wenn Foto geöffnet und geschlossen wird, muss der Highlight Bereich mitgezogen werden."):** v533 marks the word being written on the photo and v541 made the mark travel with a pinch and a pan — but the mark is placed in the picture's **own pixels** inside the `.spotlayer`, and `cueBig` (v564's tap) only toggles the classes and calls `splitFit`; it never re-places anything. **Measured at 393 × 869 on a v574 root:** the picture's height does not change at all (216.7 px both ways) — what changes is the **clip**, so the picture slides **82.5 px** under its box, and the mark, sitting at a fixed offset in the box, stays put: it goes from **0.38 of the picture's height to 0.76**, a drift of 0.3808, and stands there for as long as the card is folded. The suite traces every frame of the .22 s slide: the mark is off by up to 82.5 px through all 26 of them. **Three things, and each covers a way the layout moves.** **(1) The measurement is a closure the caller can take again.** `spotGeom`'s rendered-picture block becomes `measure()`, which reassigns the `ix, iy, iw, ih` that `put` already closed over — so a re-place is a fresh `measure()` and the same `put`, with no photo decode and no second geometry (`PICSIZE` is untouched). **(2) Every mark remembers the span it stands for** (`spotKeep`, `card._spot={geom,marks:[{el,sp}]}`) and `spotAgain(card)` re-places the ones the DOM still holds, pruning the rest — a render rebuilds the card and the list dies with the element it hangs on. **`splitFit` calls it**, so the pad's own repeated fits (v521) and **every resize (v532 — H's own folding phone)** are covered by the same line: measured on a v574 root, going to 1840 px and back left the mark **0.2531 off**, which nobody had reported. **(3) The tap drags it across the slide, frame by frame.** The box animates for .22 s and the picture travels the whole way, so one placement at the start would leave the mark wrong for the entire fold — `cueBig` runs `spotAgain` on every frame for `SLIDE_MS` 340 ms, and a second tap takes the drag over (`card._spotDrag`) so two taps cannot run two loops. **And the zoomed case, which the suite found rather than the report:** with the picture pinched, `spotGeom` places the marks against the zoom's own `r0` — the rect it measured **before** the zoom began — and `attachPicZoom`'s `measure()` deliberately refuses to take it again while zoomed, since the rendered rect is then the transformed one. So a fold while zoomed left the marks 0.26 off. `v.relayout()` inverts the transform instead: **`transform-origin` is 0 0, so the picture's own top-left maps to `r0 + t` and nothing else — the offset comes back by SUBTRACTING `t`, and only the SIZE divides by `s`.** The first cut divided the offset by `s` too and the drift only fell from 0.26 to 0.053; the corrected inverse gives **0.0002**, and at rest it returns exactly what `measure()` would. `spotAgain` calls it before re-placing, so it runs on every frame of the slide too. **What it costs:** a few rect reads and N style writes per layout change — about 20 frames on a tap, nothing measurable at rest, and `relayout` is a no-op while `s<=1`, which is every card nobody has pinched. **Measured after, at 393 × 869: the mark holds 0.38 of the picture's height through all 27 frames of the close and of the open, worst drift 0.0002 (0.0 px), zoomed and unzoomed alike**, and the resize keeps it at 0.3801. Suite `verify-spotdrag` (13 checks: the word marked on the photo as its own band, the controls; the mark dragged along while the photo closes and while it opens, with the per-frame trace; still on the word when folded; a resize to 1840 px and back; the picture really zooming, the mark still on the word zoomed (v541's contract) and dragged along by the fold while zoomed; the open card under Cards still marking its word; no page error) — **ALL OK 13 of 13 on v575; on a v574 root 5 of the 13 fail**, the two `[guard]` checks named in the file as vacuous there (the layout returns to where it was, so the stale pixels happen to be right again) and every `[control]` passing on both. `verify-topline` 17 of 17 and the smoke probe over the five other screens are unchanged; the empty-space sweep over thirteen screens reports no new slack. No key in any column, `lang.js` byte-identical. **No `WHATS_NEW` line** — the v418 rule: a mark that no longer slides off its word is a correction. One `TO_TEST` line. Not yet field-checked — H's next tap on the photo is the check: the frame stays on the word while the photo folds and opens.
