v571 put it in 58 px type in the middle of the pad, which is where H saw it. **The file carries the readings again — and only where a word really has more than one.** A rewritten value holds one group per reading, separated by **US (0x1f)**, each group opening with its own tone-marked pinyin in brackets: `合 \t [hé] to close; to join; to fit␟[gě] 100 ml; one-tenth of a peck; …`. **1,210 of the file's 115,311 lines change and 114,101 are byte for byte what they were** (same key set, same cap of three senses and 120 characters a group, same order); a value with no 0x1f is the plain old form, and the brackets are exactly what `cleanSense` already strips, so nothing that prints a value raw can show them. **The file grows 2 517 384 → 2 535 496 bytes, +0.7 %**, and `tools/cedict-readings.py` in the repo is the script that does it (the source is the `cedict-json` npm package, CC BY-SA 4.0; `vendor/LICENSES.txt` records the modification, which that licence asks for). **A full rebuild from the current dump was measured and NOT done** — the newer dump carries 5,137 more words and would change the gloss of some 7,900 single-reading ones, which is not what was asked for and would move meanings on cards H already has. **`bestSense(w,py)` takes the reading the screen is showing**, and every caller had it in hand already: the character's own syllable **inside its word** (v517's `cpy` — so 合 in 合同 reads hé and not pinyin-pro's isolated reading), the word's own pinyin, or `pySpaced(w)` in `lineMeaning`. An exact match on the tone-marked reading first, then the same syllable at another tone (乐 Le4 and le4 both romanise to "lè"), and **with no match at all the groups are flattened, which is exactly what the file did before this version** — so the change can only improve a lookup, never make one worse than v572. The three raw fallbacks (`bestSense(w)||DICT.get(w)`) are gone: `bestSense` returns "" only when the entry has no sense at all, where `DICT.get` is empty too, so they were provably dead — and `DICT.get` now has exactly **one** reader in the whole file. **Measured over the 1,210 rewritten words, with pinyin-pro's own reading for each:** the reading matches a group **exactly 1,164 times**, tone-insensitively 28, **not at all 18** — and of those 18, **17 come out byte-identical to v571** (the 18th, 尨, changes because the newer dump reordered it). **442 words change the meaning the screen shows**, and the sample reads as a correction throughout: 价 jià "messenger" → **"price"**, 作 zuò "troublesome" → **"to do"**, 令 lìng "classifier for a ream of paper" → **"to order"**, 伯 bó "one hundred" → **"father's elder brother"**, 几 jǐ "small table" → **"how much"**, 刺 cì "whoosh" → **"thorn"**, 切 qiè "to cut" → **"definitely"** (qiē is the cutting one), 佝 gōu **"Taiwan pr."** → "used in 佝偻" — that last one a gloss that was pure notation. H's own cases: **合 hé "to close"**, 雀 què "sparrow", 行 xíng "to go", 供 gōng "to provide" — and a bare 供 card now reads gòng "to lay", which is the dictionary's own headword reading and what pinyin-pro says for the character alone. **The cache is the other half of the change, and it is why `zt-ocr-v1` is NOT renamed:** the file kept its name, so a phone whose vendor cache holds the v571 copy would be served it for ever — and bumping the cache name would cost **every phone the reader's whole 15 MB** instead of this one file's 2.5 MB. The file's own first line is `#cedict v2` (no tab, so the parser skips it as it always skipped nothing), and `loadDict` drops the cache entry and fetches **once** more with `cache:"reload"` when the header is missing; what comes back is used either way, so a mirror still serving the old file costs one extra fetch a session and never a loop. **What it costs, measured rather than estimated:** the parse is unchanged (105–106 ms on both trees after the fetch), a lookup on a **grouped** word goes 0.0013 → 0.0026 ms and on a plain one stays 0.0005 — microseconds against the handful of lookups a card makes; 18 KB more to download, once. Suite `verify-dict` (19 checks: 合 carrying both groups and 供应 none; `bestSense` on 合/雀/行/供 in both readings, with no reading and with a reading that matches nothing; the line under the pad reading 合 hé "to close" with the word's row untouched; the recap over the pad; the group separator and the bracketed reading never reaching the screen; and the stale-cache case driven end to end — the v571 file seeded into `zt-ocr-v1`, the card still reading right, and the cache holding `#cedict v2` afterwards) — **ALL OK 19 of 19 on v573; on the v572 root 10 of the 19 fail**, the line reading `{"h":"合","py":"hé","mn":"100 ml"}`, which is H's screenshot in one object, and every check labelled a control passing on both. `verify-cuekeep` 86 of 86, `verify-freehand` 22 of 22 and `verify-recapmean` 12 of 12 on v573; the smoke probe passes with no page error. Checked by screenshot at 393 × 869 in light and German dark. `lang.js` is **byte-identical** — the fix says nothing in words. A `WHATS_NEW` line, one `TO_TEST` line. Not yet field-checked — H's next 合 card is the check, and the first start after the update is the other one: the app has to notice the cached dictionary is the old one and fetch it again by itself.

The empty deck's notes stay 1–3 lines everywhere with nothing overflowing (de/en 2 lines, ru 3). **What it costs, named:** a learner who wants the characters in view taps once on every fresh start — the mirror of what H paid until now — and the tiles, the word line and its pinyin and meaning are not on the first screen of a card, so a learner who does not know the tap sees a photo and a pad and nothing naming the word (the hint says it for the first twenty reviews, and the guide says it for good). ## Current state (PWA v570, 2026-09-20)
- **A character written freehand on the pad is judged as a whole and taken (v570, H: "Go für die Freehand-Erkennung" — the Go on the description he was given: "wer schnell hinkrickelt, soll am Ende trotzdem durchkommen. Konkret — *nach zwei danebenliegenden Strichen läuft der Stroke-Matcher von v141 über alles, was du bisher gezeichnet hast, und wenn das Zeichen unter den besten drei ist, wird es als geschrieben akzeptiert; die Strichreihenfolge ist dabei egal*", and, earlier, his correction of what v548 had built: "he does NOT want a selectable alternative mode; he wants that when you scribble fast without following the strokes exactly, at the end it still checks whether what you wrote matches the intended character and accepts it if so"):** until now the pad judged one stroke at a time, so someone who knows the character and writes it at speed, in their own order, missed the lit stroke every time and got a shake for every stroke of a character they were writing correctly. **Three things, and the first is what makes the rest possible.** **(1) A stroke that does not fit stays on the pad.** It was discarded, which means a character could not be written freehand at all — a stroke that vanishes cannot be written beside. It is in `st.free` now, drawn in the learner's own ink exactly as the free pad's strokes have been since v512, **and it goes again as soon as the next stroke fits** (a slip corrected is a slip gone) — until the pad has decided the learner is writing rather than tracing, and from then every stroke stays, snapped or not, so the count of what was drawn is always right. **(2) From the second miss the whole character is judged** (`st.hw`, `HAND_AT` 2, `tryHand`): v141's order-free stroke matcher runs over everything drawn so far — the template strokes already accepted plus the loose ink — and the target among its three best (`HAND_TOP`, the drawing sheet's rule since v141 and v548's) means **written, with no help counted**: one point, `charWrites` +1, the tile green, the pad on to the next character, no Done to tap. **And the misses that led there are rolled back** (`st.mm0`): they were the character being written, not failed attempts at the lit stroke, so they must not cost the card its gold star, which wants `maxMiss <= 1` — without that line a learner who writes freehand would never see the star or the burst again. **(3) Once the pad is judging the whole character it stops calling each stroke wrong** — no shake, no animation of the expected stroke — because that is false information about a character being written correctly; `st.miss` keeps counting, so **Show me still arrives at two tries and Skip at four**, and a pad with loose ink on it now offers **Undo and Clear** (rendered on every pad, hidden until there is something to undo), or a learner with junk on the pad would have no way back. **THE ONE GATE, and it is measured rather than chosen: the matcher is asked only once the drawing holds AT LEAST as many strokes as the character has.** Over 38 characters a drawing with one stroke **missing** puts the target in the matcher's top three **26 times**, and the costs of the two cases overlap — a missing stroke 0.071–0.187, a sloppy but complete character 0.067–0.151 — so **no cost bar separates them; the stroke count does**, and asking earlier is provably useless anyway, since `strokeMatch` only looks at candidates within `matchTol` of the drawing's own count (one rule, two readers now — the pad asks it before spending a match, the v401 lesson). **What else was measured, on the shipped code:** the character from its own medians is first 39 of 39, and jittered by 3 %, 8 % and **14 %** it is still in the top three **39 of 39** (costs 0.012–0.043, 0.035–0.085, 0.067–0.151 — H's three real finger-drawn 团 of v141 cost 0.08–0.13, so a real fast hand sits inside the range that is accepted); **a different character of the same stroke count is in the top three 0 of 38**; the degenerate case a failing learner really produces — the same stroke drawn over and over — is 1 of 39, and that one is 一, where one stroke repeated once **is** the character; with the character complete plus **one** leftover slip on the pad 34 of 34 are still accepted, with **two** only 16 of 34 are inside the matcher's own window at all (all 16 accepted) and with **three** none can ever be — the pad's own way of refusing a mess. **25 ms a match on this box, at most three per character** (the window bounds it). **Diagnostics carries every judgement** — "合 written freehand, 6 strokes — accepted, rank 1, cost 0.041" beside the traced strokes' own lines (`logPadStroke`'s `hand`) — because the field is the only place the accuracy of a real hand can be measured, which is v548's own caveat and still stands. **What it costs, named:** a fluent writer who **joins** two strokes into one writes fewer strokes than the template has and is never accepted (Skip is the way out) — that is the price of closing the 26-of-38 hole, and it is the right way round, since accepting a character written with a stroke missing teaches the wrong character; three leftover slips and acceptance cannot fire at all; the two helper buttons sit in the pad's lower corners (v560) and now appear mid-write, so a stroke that **starts** in a corner hits a button instead of the pad — the same class as Show me and Skip appearing there since v560, measured and accepted, and the suite's own fixture had to be moved off the corner because of it; and the loose ink is not in the resume note (v569 left `free` out on purpose), so a reload mid-scribble comes back on the same character with an empty pad. **v548's Handwriting switch is NOT removed, and the report's own claim that it "würde damit überflüssig" is corrected here:** with it on there is no template from the first stroke and no per-stroke judging at all, which is a different thing from a pad that starts as a tracing pad and gives way — a beginner's card is unchanged, and only a learner who writes rather than traces ever reaches the new path. **One key in nine columns** (the guide's Learn sentence, "Know the character? Write it your own way, in your own stroke order — the pad takes it once what you wrote matches.", each column in its own tone and with its own word for the pad — de das Pad, fr le pavé, es el panel, ja パッド, ko 쓰기판, ru поле, vi bảng viết, th กระดาน, id papan): **485 → 486 a column, ru 514 → 515, en 15**, no duplicate in any of the ten (a string-aware scan of the source; the static key check reports only its two standing hits, `kind:` and `{0} ({1})`). The guide is measured over 10 languages × 393 and 360 px: **0 overflowing elements, no sideways scroll**, the page 44–70 px longer per language and the longest of the twenty (Russian at 360 px) **3194 px**, still inside v549's own 3200 budget. ## Current state (PWA v563, 2026-09-20)
- **The top panel loses its frame, and the app stops reloading itself (v563, H on v562: "Nee, also der Rahmen oben sieht Käse aus. Und außerdem refresht die App seitdem die ganze Zeit und kommt gar nicht mehr zur Ruhe."):** two things, and the second is my own fault twice over. **(1) The look.** v561's grey `--card2` panel with its hairline around the photo, the strip and the word line is gone on H's word; **the geometry stays** — the `.cue` is still exactly as tall as the pad (`--cueh` from `fit()`), the photo box keeps its own hairline and radius, the strip and the line sit where they sat, the "+4 ⌄" pill of v562 stands on the card's white. Measured: `verify-frame` 24 of 24 on v563 with its panel check retargeted to a transparent cue background. **(2) The reload storm, and what actually caused it.** The v561 and v562 PRs bumped `APP_V` in `app.js` and **left `index.html` at "PWA v560" and `sw.js` at "zt-v560"** — the "bump both, plus zt-vN, on every change" rule broken twice in a row (the file lists of #633 and #634 are app.js, styles.css and CLAUDE.md, nothing else). So the shell on `main` was mixed by construction: a phone whose worker cache held the newer `app.js` found `APP_V` 561 or 562 against a label of 560 at **every** boot, `shellCheck` asked the worker to refill the shell, the refill fetched the same v560 `index.html` beside the newer script, the page reloaded, and the boot found the same mismatch again — one reload every ten minutes (the `shellFixAt` guard's own cadence) for as long as `main` stayed that way, with no version in which it would have ended. The worker itself never changed (`sw.js` byte-identical), so no phone ever got a clean v561 or v562 shell either; what H saw as v561/v562 came in through that refill. On top of it the three merges sat inside one GitHub Pages ten-minute cache window (15:02, 15:11, 15:15 UTC), which this file has forbidden since v279. **The fix is the three markers at 563** — a new worker installs, fetches the whole shell with `cache:"reload"`, and the label and the script agree again — **and a cool-down under the app's own reloads:** `reloadNow()` records `lastReload` in the settings and, for a reload the app decided on its own, waits until `RELOAD_COOL` ten minutes have passed since the last one (the reload stays due and comes at the next idle check after that); a reload the user asked for — the mirror row's Check now, `reloadNow(true)` — is never held. So whatever the servers say, the app reloads itself at most once in ten minutes, and a mixed shell costs one reload per ten minutes at the very worst instead of a loop. Suite `verify-cooldown` (5 checks: a first self-reload going through and writing `lastReload`; a second one within the window held with the reload due; a user-requested reload going through inside the window; the window's end releasing the held reload; the setting surviving a reload) — **5 of 5 on v563; on a v562 root the held-reload flip and the `lastReload` note fail.** No key in any column, `lang.js` byte-identical. **No `WHATS_NEW` line** — the v412/v432 rule: a look taken back and a reload that no longer happens; one `TO_TEST` line ("About says v563, no reload by itself more often than every ten minutes"). **The deploy rule, restated because it was broken:** every PR checks `grep APP_V= app.js`, `grep "PWA v" index.html` and `grep CACHE sw.js` before the merge, and the three numbers must be one number; and the merge waits until ten minutes after the last one. Not yet field-checked — H's phone is the check: More → About reading v563 after one start, and the app standing still afterwards.

On a screen too short for two such panels the cue keeps `PHOTO_MIN` 120 of photo and the pad takes the rest, down to `PAD_FLOOR`. **Measured:** at 393 × 869 **cue 323 = pad 323, photo 182**, the pad a 323 px square centred in a 325 px card — the two pixels are what equal panels cost there, named rather than hidden; at 390 × 844 cue 311 = pad 311, photo 170 (v560: pad 322, photo 167); at 360 × 640 photo 120, pad 165. The card's grid is `var(--cueh) auto auto` now, the cue's own grid `minmax(0,1fr) 56px 61px`; the carousel's neighbour takes the card's `--cueh`. **(2) The unfold is in place, nothing doubled.** v560 laid a copy of the rows over the photo while the strip below still showed its row — the same characters twice, H's "doppelt gemoppelt", and it lived one hour. ## Current state (PWA v560, 2026-09-20)
- **THE FRAME: every study card has the same shape, and the strip is one row that follows the pad (v560, H the same hour, on the v559 numbers: "gibt es da nicht irgendwie Best Practices oder Regeln, wie man Apps professionell macht? Du springst jetzt wieder mit verschiedenen Größen für das Writepad, die Bilder und so weiter. Je nach Karte immer unterschiedlich. Das wäre doch viel schöner, wenn es immer gleich ist, immer symmetrisch ist, die Proportionen immer gleich sind." — a fixed frame proposed and mocked from the real app ("zeig"), then his own better idea for the strip: "die Characters so groß lässt in der Mitte und wenn es mehr als eine Reihe ist ... dass man das dann aufklappen kann, anstatt dass das so wegfadet zur Seite und man das scrollen muss, weil mit dem Scrollen gibt es ja auch Probleme, dann kann ich ja die ganze Page nicht mehr richtig swipen", "Go"):** **the rule, and it is the one that makes layouts read as professional: the frame never moves for the content; the content adapts to the frame.** Since v512 the pad was the leftover after the photo, the character rows and the line, so it changed with the text, the language and the viewport, and v519, v522 and v559 each added a card-dependent rule on top. **Now the study card is a CSS grid of fixed rows** (`.card.study:not(.detail)`): the photo row `--photoh`, the strip 56, the word line 61, the pad, the fold row 36, 8 px between them — and **the pad is the anchor: as wide as the card's inner width, so as wide as the photo above it, the same square on every card.** `mountPad`'s fit computes two numbers once per device instead of measuring the card's content: `side = min(inner, cardH − fixed − PHOTO_MIN)` and `photoH = cardH − fixed − side`, where `cardH` is the room from the card's top to 16 px above the tab bar with the page at rest and `fixed` is the sum of the constant rows (`STRIP_H` 56, `LINE_H` 61, the fold button, the padding, the gaps, and the swipe hint of the first twenty reviews while it is there). Only a screen too short for both makes the pad give way, down to `PAD_FLOOR` 160, so the photo keeps `PHOTO_MIN` 120 — a device-level decision, still constant per device. **Measured, cards of 2, 8 and 17 characters:** at 393 × 869 **photo 189, strip 56, line 61, pad 325 × 325, fold 36 on all three, to the pixel** (v559: pad 293 / 265 / 251 and the photo 217 / 183 / 183); at 390 × 844 photo 167 and pad 322; at 360 × 640 photo 120 and pad 165, the card still above the bar. `PAD_MIN`, `PAD_BELOW`, v521's tail budget and v559's `.wrapped` box are gone; the resize and pageshow re-fits of v521/v532 stay, since `cardH` is measured. **The picture in the photo row:** a picture near the row's own shape keeps its size and is clipped by the row, centred on its text (`.picbox.clip`, set in fit when the picture's ratio reaches `CLIP_RATIO` 0.8 of the row's — v329 centres the window on the frame, so the text stays whole and only surroundings above and below go; the v559 mechanism, generalised), a picture much taller than the row (a label's own square frame) is fitted inside it instead; the whole-photo tap fits the whole photo into the same row. **The strip (`chrowHTML` → `.chrow` the viewport, `.chin` the flow; `stripFit`):** the tiles stay at `CH_MAX` 56 on the study card — no shrinking, H's "so groß lässt" —, a text that does not fit one row is laid out in rows of what fits (the v519 wrap, `STRIP_GAP` 8 between rows), and the strip, 56 px tall with `overflow:hidden`, **shows the row the pad is on** by translating the flow, sliding (.22 s, the app's own curve) from the row it left when the pad moves to a character in another row (`STRIP_ROW` remembers the last row per card, since every advance re-renders the card). **Nothing scrolls sideways, so the swipe keeps the whole card** — v518's rule that a scrolling strip owns the horizontal gesture ends with the scrolling strip. **A chevron at the strip's right end** (`.chmore`, `hidden` unless the strip holds more than one row, `aria-expanded`, the existing "Characters" key as its label) **and the strip's own empty room unfold every row over the photo** (`stripOpen`: `.chall` inside `.zone1`, a copy of the flow with the same tiles in the same states — the tint one, the green ones, the outlined word —, scrolling vertically inside the photo row when seventeen characters need five rows; a tap on a tile puts it into the pad through the same `pick` the strip's tiles use, which re-renders and so closes it; a tap anywhere else, the chevron again or Escape closes it; built on the tap, never in the card's markup, so nothing on the card is doubled). **Show me, Skip, Undo, Done and Clear live inside the pad's square** now, in its lower corners (`.padwrap .padacts`, absolute, `space-between`), and the free character's note at the pad's top — so a button appearing can never resize anything, which is v517's rule by construction where until now it was a budget. **The open card under Cards keeps every row in view** (the v519/v522 fit: shrink, then wrap, no chevron) — it has no pad and no frame to keep. The carousel's neighbour is the same grid with the card's own `--photoh` (Learn's `ready` hands it over), so it rides in at the card's exact height; `actsSize` (v530) is gone with the helper row it measured. **What it costs, named:** 28 px less photo on a one-row card than v559 (217 → 189 at 393 × 869); on a long sign the strip shows one row of the text at a time — the whole text is on the photo and in the word line, and the chevron says there is more, which the v519 tester never had; one tap more to jump to a character in another row; texts of six single characters now take two rows where v522 fitted seven on one at 40 px — `CH_MIN` still exists for the open card, and giving the strip the shrink first is one line if H wants seven in a row. The swipe hint of the first twenty reviews comes out of the photo for those cards (189 → about 149 in English). No key in any column, `lang.js` byte-identical. **The mock came first and taught one thing:** a grid column sized `auto` grows to the canvas's 720 px attribute width before fit sizes it, so the strip measured itself against a 720 px card and never wrapped — `grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr)`. Suite `verify-frame` (21 checks: the pad as wide as the card and the photo; the strip one row at 56 px on the pad's row with the chevron; the 3:2 picture clipped, centred; the card above the bar; the chevron unfolding all eight tiles over the photo with the frame unmoved, a tap on 超 in the overlay putting it into the pad, closing it and sliding the strip to row 2 by exactly 64 px with the frame byte-identical; a tap outside closing it with nothing picked; a stroke on the pad still counted as a miss; Show me inside the pad's square; the neighbour mid-stroke with the same frame and height; the open card under Cards with all eight tiles on two rows and no chevron; a two-character card and a seventeen-character one with the identical frame, the latter unfolding seventeen tiles; a square picture fitted, not clipped; 390 × 844 and 360 × 640; German dark; no page error) — **ALL OK on v560; on a v559 root its first three flips fail and the run then dies at the missing chevron** (the v419 rule). Checked by screenshot at 393 × 869: the frame on 8 and 17 characters, the overlay open, the strip on row 2, Show me in the pad, German dark. A `WHATS_NEW` line, three `TO_TEST` lines. Not yet field-checked — H's next session is the check: three cards of different lengths with nothing moving between them, the strip sliding to the second row of 盒马鲜生 / 超市入口 by itself, and the chevron unfolding the rows.

Every zone above the pad stood at a size he had chosen himself (the 3:2 box v519, the 56 px tiles v522, the two-row line v518), so the pad was what was left. **Two levers, both taken.** **(1) The gaps:** the six margins between the zones and the card's own padding are 12 → 8 and 16/18 → 12/14 (`.chrow`, `.chrow.wrap`'s row gap 8 → 6, `.padline` 10 → 6, `.padwrap`, `.fold`, `.card.study`), `PAD_BELOW` 54 → 50 with the fold's margin — **+22 px of pad on every card**, wrapped or not. **(2) On a wrapped card only, the photo box is 16:9 instead of 3:2, and the 3:2 window keeps its own size inside it** — clipped by 8 % at the top and at the bottom, not fitted narrower with the blurred fill beside it (that was measured too and rejected: the sign 16 % narrower). Bitte korrigieren."):** no screenshot, so the handover was measured on composited frames first (the v555 rule — `Page.startScreencast`, the pad's rectangle scored per frame for pixels that differ from the card's surface and for dark strokes). **On v557: the pad visible with the character through the flash, then dark for the whole second the reading stands (the ink 3 %, the reading's own text), then at 1.9 s after the last stroke THREE FRAMES of the pad at full brightness with the character's black strokes (99.7 % / 9.5 %), fading out over .2 s under the whole card's recap.** The cause is `cardDone`'s own render: it rebuilds the card, `mountPad`'s `fit()` reads the layout during that render, so the fresh pad's first style is computed at opacity 1, and `recapping` — added in the same task — then starts a TRANSITION 1 → 0 instead of committing 0. **On a v556 root the same frames show the same fade** (99.7/9.5 at 0.78 s, then 20 → 8 %), and it never read as a glitch there, because the pad had never been dark: it was the v523 crossfade, the pad stepping back under the reading. v557 made the pad dark for a second first, and the same fade became a pop — the v554 finding one step later. **Two lines:** `cardDone(dark)` commits the fresh pad to 0 with the transition off (`transition:none`, the class, a forced reflow, the transition given back — `padFadeIn`'s own trap, v555, the other way round) whenever it follows a reading; and the last-character branch puts `recapping` back on the OLD padwrap before `cardDone`'s two record writes (`checkCard`, `recordGrade`, some 300 ms of IndexedDB), since after a tap the reading's exit had let that pad start fading back up under nothing. He took the first. **The mechanism is one line in `charDone`:** where the pad found no next character it called `cardDone()` directly; it now runs the same `charRecap` every middle character gets, waits for its fade (`gone`, v555), and only then `cardDone` — **one after the other, never on top of each other**, which was v553's reason for leaving it out. `cardDone` renders a fresh padwrap and puts `recapping` on it in the same task, so the pad stays dark between the two readings (measured: the pad at 0 through every frame of the reading after its own .2 s fade — the v555 handover, unchanged). **A one-character card skips it:** there the whole card's pinyin IS that one syllable, and "jī" followed by 鸡 / jī / chicken would be the very stack v553 avoided (`tg.filter(x=>x.w).length>1` is the test). **A tap still takes the reading at once**, and since `cardDone` puts its own listener on afterwards, a second tap takes the whole card's recap — so a learner who wants nothing of it is two taps from the next card, as before he was one. **What it costs, measured rather than estimated:** the whole card's recap comes **1.42 s after the last stroke instead of 0.32 s** (the reading up at 0.3 s, standing 0.84 s, lifting 0.2 s), so every finished card of two characters or more takes about **1.1 s longer**, some 20 s over a twenty-card session, all of it skippable with one tap; and the guard is the sibling branch's (`!cv.isConnected||S.pad!==st` → return), so a card left by a tab tap during that second is not recorded here, where until v556 the window for that was the 300 ms flash — named, not widened further. Everything drawn on the photo now lives in one **`.spotlayer`** inside the box, and `apply()` gives that layer the picture's own move: the layer sits at the box's origin while the picture sits at `r`, so the translation that puts a picture point where the picture's own transform puts it is **`r*(1-s)+t`** — derived once, rather than re-placing every mark on every frame, which would need the geometry (and a photo decode) each time. `--wz` is `1/scale` on the layer, so a 1.5 px ring stays 1.5 px at 5× instead of becoming 7.5. And `spotGeom` reads the zoom's own **`r0`** — the rect it measured before it began — while the picture is enlarged, since the rendered rect is then the transformed one. **(2) The zoom did not survive the next character, and that is the defect under H's third sentence.** `charDone` calls `render()` to move the pad on, which rebuilds the card, and a fresh `attachPicZoom` started at scale 1 — so zooming in and writing one character threw the zoom away. `PIC_ZOOM` keeps it per picture (`zoomKey`: the card, and separately its whole-photo view and a peeked one, which are different pictures), in memory only, and `attachPicZoom` drops it the moment another picture is shown — **the zoom is the picture on screen, not a setting**. It is restored once the picture really has its size, resetting to rest first so `measure` may take a fresh `r0`. **(3) Then the picture follows the pad**: `spotWord` calls `zoom.follow(centre of the word)` on the next frame, which pans so that point is in the middle of the box and puts the box on a 380 ms transition (`GLIDE_MS`, `.zgl`) — clamped like any pan, so a word at the picture's edge comes as close as the edge allows; at rest (scale 1) nothing moves, since the whole picture is already on screen, and the finger always wins (a pointerdown takes the transition off). **(4) The ring.** v533 chose a tint line for *dezent* and a red shop front swallows it; it is a **white core between two dark flanks** now — v461's own finding, that the boundary is carried by the EDGE between the runs and so survives a white sign, a black panel and a red one alike — with the tint kept as the wash inside, where it still says whose mark this is on an ordinary photo. - **The recap stands alone, the pad finishes its word, a dismissed suggestion stays dismissed, and the note under a photo is honest (v535, H in two messages: "Wenn das Wort nach erfolgreichem schreiben noch einmal angezeigt wird, sollte das graue Pad nicht mehr sichtbar sein, da sonst zu unruhig · Bitte immer erst ein Wort ausschreiben und dann die anderen Characters · The same AI suggestion shouldn't pop up again and again", then, with a screenshot of Chrome's Google bar over the app: "Don't let those Google messages pop up"):** four things, and two of them are real defects rather than polish. **(1) The recap.** v523 dimmed the pad to a tenth under the card's own text; a tenth of a 田字格 with the stroke template still in it is a grey character behind the black one, which is the "unruhig". `.padwrap.recapping .wpad` is `opacity:0` — the recap stands on the card's own surface, nothing behind it. **(2) The pad finishes the word it is in.** `charDone` took **the first unwritten character of the card** (`tg.findIndex(x=>x.w&&!done)`), which is word order only while you write straight through — tap 供 of 鸡蛋供应, write it, and the pad went back to **鸡** with 应 left standing, so the word was never written out. It looks inside the current word first (`x.wi===cur.wi`) and falls back to the card when that word is done; a character in no dictionary word (a number) has no word to finish and falls straight through. Measured end to end: 供 → **应** → 鸡, where v534 gives 供 → 鸡 → 蛋. **(3) The same suggestion came back on every start, and it cost an AI call each time.** H's screenshot is a flagged garbage card with "1 AI suggestion" on the Cards tab; `dismissed(d)` cleared `ai` and `mt.suspect` and left `flag` and **`mt.pending`** — and `aiAuto` takes every card with `mt.pending` and no `ai`, so the next start asked again, got the same answer and stored it again, for ever. **A dismissal is a decision and the card records it:** `aiNo` = a fingerprint of what an automatic check is about (`c` + `p` + `m`, `aiFp`), written by `dismissed` and honoured by `aiAuto` and `aiQueue` through `aiRefused(d)`. **The buttons are deliberately untouched** — Check-up, Ask AI and the Review queue's own tap are the learner asking, and they ask; only the run that needs no tap stands down. **And it needs no second field to clear:** an edit, an accepted suggestion or a new reading changes `c`/`p`/`m` and so changes the fingerprint, and the card is checkable again by itself (measured: a changed meaning puts it back in the queue). `aiNo` is a card field like `ai`, so export and import carry it with no line of their own and an older app ignores it. **(4) The note under a photo.** A long press on it raised Android's selection toolbar and a Google search over the app — the v248/v249/v272 rule, which exempts prose so a meaning can be copied, and a status line under a photo is not prose: `.shot .ok` is `user-select:none`. **And the same line was printing failures in the success green** (`app.js` wrapped *every* note in `class="ok"`, `color:var(--ok)`), so "The AI could not be reached, and the reading alone was too unsure for a card." read in the same green as "Card saved — 供应." — the one moment the app has failed, told in its success colour. `QSBAD` marks the ids whose note says the reading failed (set by `failPending` and by the no-text branch, cleared wherever a success note is written and wherever the note itself goes), and `.shot .ok.bad` is the same line in `--label2`; a note restored from the record across a restart (`s.note`, v509) is a failure note by construction and takes the same class. No key in any column, `lang.js` byte-identical. **What it costs, named:** a card whose suggestion H dismisses is never offered again by itself, so a later model that would answer better is only reached through Check-up — which is the point, and the button is there; and the pad's word-first order means that on a card whose words are read out of order a tap now commits to that whole word before the pad moves on. Suite `verify-wordfirst` (17 checks: the card landing on 鸡, a tap putting 供 in the pad, the write moving it to 应 and only then back to 鸡; the recap over the pad with the pad at opacity 0; a suggestion waiting, the dismissal clearing it while flag and pending stay, the automatic run and the queue dropping the card, `aiNo` on the record in IndexedDB, and a changed meaning making it checkable again; a failed reading and a failure from this session both in the label colour and not the success green, a saved card keeping the green, and no note taking a text selection; no page error) — **ALL OK on v535; on a v534 root the word-first check fails with the pad back on 鸡, the pad reads 0.1 instead of 0, and the run then dies at the missing `aiRefused`** (the v419 rule). `verify-recap`'s "the pad steps back" is retargeted at the invisible pad — the honest record of the contract this version reverses; recap 15, writepad 54, onewidth 32, r518 29, lockoff 11, detailfoot 14, swaplayout 18, honest 21, wordspot 11, foldwake 11 ALL OK; the load probe passes. Checked by screenshot at 393 × 917 in light and German dark: the recap on the card's own surface with no pad behind it. A `WHATS_NEW` line (the word order and the suggestion are both the learner's), one `TO_TEST` line. Not yet field-checked — H's next finished card is the check (the characters alone, nothing grey behind them), his next tap on a character in the middle of a word (the pad finishing that word), and the suggestion he dismisses staying gone after a restart.
- **What the app says about itself is true again (v534, H: "Bitte mache ein komplett Audit, polish nochmal über alles rüber, check, dass keine losen Enden vorhanden sind, keine Widersprüche, alles Sinn macht und bitte auch, dass alles super professionell und kundenfreundlich aussieht."):** six sweeps ran over the whole app in parallel — code hygiene, layout over ten languages, wording and translations, does-everything-still-work, contradictions, first impression — and their findings are shipped as a short series; this is the first, the half where the app made a claim about itself that was no longer true. **The two that matter for the Play Store's Data Safety form**, both found by comparing `privacy.html` against the code line by line: the page said a Feedback message "carries no name, no cards and no photos unless you type them" while **v511 added Add screenshot**, which posts a JPEG of the user's own screen as base64 in the row's `shot` column; and it said "**Four** buttons send card text because you pressed them" and named them, while **v529's Explain** is a fifth (`explainCard` sends the full `aiCardPayload` for one card). Both are named now, the page's date moves to 19 September 2026, and **the app's own "What is sent" sentence gains the same clause in all ten columns** ("…and for one card when you tap Explain under its meaning"), each column using its own v529 word for Explain (Erklären, Expliquer, Explicar, 解説, 설명, Объяснить, Giải thích, อธิบาย, Jelaskan). **And the "once a day" claim is corrected in the two places that still made it** — the Usage sharing row and the guide's last paragraph, ten columns each: `sendReport(true)` has posted a second row on every background transition since v219 when a card changed (`REPORT_DIRTY`), `privacy.html` was corrected at v459 and these two were not, so the app contradicted its own privacy page. **Three things the learner sees, each of them false:** the guide's first section said "tap a text on it for its characters, pinyin and meaning, **and grade it right there**" — since v453 every photo whose texts stand apart is a multicard, whose sheet offers Generate flashcard and **no grades** (`app.js:8351` renders them only for a pre-v453 marked photo), so the sentence contradicted the very next paragraph, the Cards section and the project's own headline rule; the clause is gone from all ten columns (the Korean also lost a verb ending I had mistyped, 뜠어요 → 나와요, caught by rendering the column rather than reading it). **More → About showed two adjacent lines that contradicted each other:** `whatsNewHTML` lists the last five notes, which were 533, 531, 529, 527 and **526** — and 526 reads "A character you press and hold opens every card of its walk … **green** on the button", while 531 one line above says the hold "is switched off for now" and v528 had already made the lock **blue**. `WHATS_NEW[526]` is removed: **a release note is what a learner is told is new in the app they are holding, so a note describing a gesture that does nothing is not a record but a false instruction** — the older lock notes (513, 518, 520) stay, since only the last five are ever shown and they are the history. **And the owner's Still-to-test list asked H to confirm both that the lock is off and that it works:** six of its rows are lock checks that `LOCK_ON=false` makes impossible, two of them naming green where v528's whole point was H's "Muss nicht grün sein". They move to a fifth group, **"Parked — the lock is off (v531)"** — kept, not deleted, because the code is kept too — the v528 row says blue, and `toTestOpen()` leaves them out of the count, so the row reads 171 checks waiting instead of 177. **One honest reader size:** three places named three numbers for the same eleven files — the reading box "~12 MB", More → Text recognition "(14 MB, once)" and `sw.js`'s comment "~12 MB" — and **the measured sum is 14.90 MiB / 15.62 MB**, so all three say ~15 MB. No key added or removed (**473 a column, ru 502, en 14**, three keys' text replaced and six values spliced), no duplicate in any of the ten. Suite `verify-honest` (21 checks: privacy.html naming five buttons, Explain, Add screenshot with its 1400 px and the new date, and no longer claiming no photos at all; More carrying the Explain clause, the second daily row and "(15 MB, once)"; About with no press-and-hold promise, 526 out of the last five and 531's own note still there; Still to test with its parked group, six parked, the count leaving them out and the chip blue; the guide without the grading clause, still explaining Generate flashcard, and naming the second row; the German guide and the German "Erklären" clause; no page error) — **ALL OK on v534; on a v533 root 19 of its 21 fail**, the two that pass on both labelled controls. wordspot 11, foldwake 11, lockoff 11, detailfoot 14, swaplayout 18, r518 29, writepad 54, desc 24 ALL OK; the load probe passes. **No `WHATS_NEW` line** — a corrected sentence is the v418/v473 kind of thing, and one of this version's own changes is that a note the learner cannot act on does not belong there. **What it cannot do:** say whether the models honour any of it — this version changes what the app says, not what it does. Not yet field-checked — H reading More → AI review, More → Still to test and the guide is the check, and the Play Data Safety form is now fillable from a page that matches the code.
- **The word being written is marked on the photo, quietly (v533, H: "Bitte ausgewählte Worte dezent im Bild highlighten"):** the app lights the word on its tile (`.chw.on`, v517) and reads it in the line above the pad (v527), and until now nothing said **where on the sign it stands** — on a four-character card the learner had to find it by eye. `spotWord` draws one `.wspot` over the word's own run of characters: a 1.5 px tint ring with a 1 px white flank outside it, so it holds on a white sign and on a black panel alike, and `--tint-soft` inside — **never the 9999px shadow of the locked character's spotlight** (v520), which dims the whole picture, since H asked for *dezent*; a first cut drew a 2 px ring with a dark flank as well and read as a label rather than a hint (seen on the screenshot, not in the numbers). It follows the pad and the tap by itself, since both go through `render()`, and the **open card** marks the word its line is reading the same way (v531's `detailLit`). **The geometry is v520's and is now derived once for both marks** (`spotGeom`, factored out of `spotChar`): the frame is the text's rectangle on the photo (v244), the picture the 3:2 window around it (v519) or a split label's own frame (v362), the photo's lines share the frame's height evenly and a line's characters its width by their `lineUnits` (v339) — so `wordSpan(d,x)` is the run from `x.wstart` of `x.word` in its own photo line. **What it cannot promise, named:** it is the v520 estimate, not a measurement — on a sign whose characters are unevenly spaced the ring sits a little off, which is why it is soft-edged; a turned frame, a peeked photo (v155) and a picture that is neither a window nor the frame get **no** mark rather than one in the wrong place; and a card whose one word **is** the whole text gets none either, since there would be nothing to single out. **One thing the change pays for itself with:** `spotChar` decoded the whole photo through `createImageBitmap` on **every render** to learn its pixel size; `PICSIZE` caches it per card (40 cards, oldest out), so four renders of one card now decode it **once** — measured 0 in the suite, where the same probe on a v532 root counts one per render. No key in any column, `lang.js` byte-identical. Suite `verify-wordspot` (11 checks on a card copied onto a photo of its own, since every seeded card shares one photo and is therefore a v452 page front: the mark exactly once on the landing word with the tile lit and the pad on 鸡; it covering the text's first half and sitting inside the picture; the ring tint with a white flank, the wash `--tint-soft` and **no** dimming and no `.spot`; a tap on 应 moving it to the second half; a one-word card that is the whole text getting none; a card without a frame getting none and no error; the open card marking the word its line reads and following its tap; four renders decoding the photo at most once; German dark in the dark tint; no page error) — **ALL OK on v533; on a v532 root 9 of its 11 fail.** swaplayout 18, r518 29, writepad 54, onewidth 32, lockword 20, foldpos 18, padtail 12, spot 14, recap 15, lockwalk 23, outline 16, lenorder 10, desc 24, ghostpad 10, lockoff 11, detailfoot 14, foldwake 11 ALL OK; the load probe passes. Checked by screenshot at 393 × 917 in light, German dark and on the open card. A `WHATS_NEW` line, one `TO_TEST` line. Not yet field-checked — H's next card is the check: does the ring point at the right word on a real sign, and is it quiet enough?

- **The stroke tables no longer block the main thread at startup, a fold's resize refits the row with the pad, and Diagnostics says what a fold did (v532, H: "open/close foldable phone sometimes freezes the startup screen from the app. Please fix."):** **not reproduced** — the harness has no fold, and nothing in the code loops on layout (every `while` was read; `chrowFit` steps a bounded range, `fit()` is arithmetic) — so this version is what can be measured rather than a guess about the cause, and it names what the next dump will say. **(1) The parse.** The medians (2.4 MB gzipped) and the Kai outlines (7.3 MB, v517) were each read with one `Response.text()` and parsed in one synchronous loop at the first card of a session. Measured with a long-task observer at startup on Learn: **one 260 ms task unthrottled, 992 ms at 4× CPU throttle**, and the `.text()` of the outline stream alone a **766 ms task at 4×** — it inflates and decodes the whole 19 MB into one string before the first line exists. A phone folded in that second shows a screen that does not move. `eachLineOf(res,fn)` reads the file as a stream now: the buffer is fed to the `DecompressionStream` in `FEED_CHUNK` 128 KB slices (handed the whole 7 MB at once the inflater did all of it in one 229 ms task before the first chunk came out — measured, the v419 kind of finding), each 64 KB chunk is decoded with a streaming `TextDecoder`, its lines handed to the parser, and the thread freed before the next (`yieldNow`, `scheduler.yield` where it exists); the file is never whole in memory. **Measured after: 0 long tasks at 1× (from 1), and at 4× the longest 211 ms (from 992), total 395 ms (from 1185)** — the one left sits inside the outline parse and is not the walk or the parse (both run without any long task on their own after boot), most likely a garbage-collection pause while the tables are retained; named, not chased. The parse itself takes longer in wall time (384 and 212 ms at 1× in the sandbox, `PARSE_MS`), since it shares the thread instead of taking it. **(2) The resize.** A fold's burst of resize events is coalesced into one frame (`_rsz`), and **the character row is fitted again beside the pad** — v521's listener re-fitted the pad alone, so after an unfold the row kept the folded screen's size; the open card's row too. A page brought back from the back/forward cache (`pageshow` with `persisted`, which a fold can hand Chrome) is measured again the same way. **(3) Diagnostics** carries one line for the next dump: `main thread · long tasks N (T ms in all, longest M ms, last …) · parse strokes N ms, outlines N ms · resizes 393×917→1840×1200 2 s ago; …` — the long tasks since the page loaded through a `PerformanceObserver` (`LONG`), the parse times, the last six size changes (`RESIZES`, a change of size only) and a cache restore. Owner's English, no key in any column, `lang.js` byte-identical. **What it costs, named:** the templates arrive a little later at the first card (the parse is spread over more frames), and the observer is one more listener for the page's life. **What it cannot say:** whether H's freeze is this stall, Chrome's own splash screen on an activity recreated by the fold, or a page discarded while folded — his next dump after a fold, and one word on whether the frozen screen is the app's Learn card or the icon on grey, are what will. Suite `verify-foldwake` (11: the tables parsed with no task over 100 ms at 1× and both parse times on record, the tables whole; a viewport change from 393 × 917 to 1840 × 1200 refitting the row (a spy on `chrowFit`) and the pad at the unfolded width, the change on record with both sizes; twenty resize events in one go one refit; folded again the pad back at 317 and the row at 56 px with no overflow; the Diagnostics line; the open card's row refitted on a resize; no page error) — **ALL OK on v532; on a v531 root 7 of its 11 fail** (the four that pass on both are controls). swaplayout 18, r518 29, writepad 54, onewidth 32, lockword 20, foldpos 18, padtail 12, spot 14, recap 15, lockwalk 23, outline 16, lenorder 10, desc 24, ghostpad 10, lockoff 11, detailfoot 14 ALL OK; the load probe passes. **No `WHATS_NEW` line** — a stall that no longer happens is the v418 kind of correction; one `TO_TEST` line. Not yet field-checked — H folding and unfolding the phone on a fresh start is the check, and if it still freezes, More → Diagnostics → the `main thread` line.

- **The lock is off behind a kept switch, and the open card follows the study card (v531, H: "Deaktiviere die lock Funktion erstmal wieder, aber verwerfe sie nicht. Ich werde sie später evtl. reaktivieren. / Cards View dem Learn View nachziehen."):** two things in one PR. **(1) The lock.** The long press on a character that locks it and walks every card carrying it (v513, v526, v528, the photo spotlight of v520) sits behind `LOCK_ON=false`, read through `lockOn()` at the four places where the lock enters: the tile's `longPress` in `renderStudy`, the hint's clause in `swipeHint`, the guide's Learn sentence, and the resume note at boot (`rv.lock` is ignored, or a phone locked at the moment of the update would have come back locked with no hold to release it). `S.lockChar` is therefore never set, and every lock surface — the chip, the word's outline, the line's padlock, the walk, the spotlight, `walking()` — stays inert by construction; **nothing is deleted**: `lockChar`, `unlockChar`, `walkOf`, `spotChar`, the CSS, the keys and `WHATS_NEW[513]` all stay, and `true` brings it back. `lockOn()` also honours the setting `lockOn`, which nothing in the app writes: it is the harness's way in, since the lock suites' reload checks need the switch to hold across a boot where a page variable would not (`seed(page,{lock:true})`); the five suites that drive the hold — lockword, lockwalk, spot, outline, r518 — seed it and pass unchanged. **(2) The open card** (`detailCardHTML`, the "Cards view" read as the card detail — the Cards list is picture tiles, and the only screen there that has a Learn counterpart is the open card): the study card's own v527 order — the photo, the character row, **the word's line under the row, always there** (`detailLit`: the tapped character's word, else the first writable one — as the pad's line is always there in Learn; until v530 it showed only for a tapped character, and the same character tapped again put it out; now it puts the line back on the first word), the six actions where the pad stands, and **the fold "Whole card" at the foot**, leading with the card's characters (`.anshanzi`, the traditional form when the card has one) and then pinyin, meaning, description or Explain, the flag note and the AI box — where v518/v527 had "Pinyin and meaning" above the line. **The block stays open by default** (`S.detailHide=false`): this is the screen for looking a card up, and the fold state is a way of reading, not a layout. Opening it by its button scrolls the block above the tab bar as in Learn (`revealBlock`, `showAns` factored out of `renderStudy` for both). Star and Flag are not doubled: they are in the actions, so the block carries no `.backacts` row. The carousel's neighbour on the open card is built by the same function and comes in with the same order. The `.card.study.detail .padline{margin-top:12px}` override is gone, so the line sits at the study card's 10 px. No key in any column, `lang.js` byte-identical (the fold reuses "Whole card"). **What it costs, named:** a learner who used the hold has nothing that says why it stopped except the release note; the open card's block is one fold further down than it was, under the six actions, and on a phone whose card fills the screen one scroll away — the v527 trade on a second screen. Suites `verify-lockoff` (11: the switch off; a real 700 ms hold locking nothing — no lock, walk, chip, padlock, outline, spotlight or buzz — with the session where it was; the hint and the guide without the press-and-hold sentence and still naming the stroke and the swipe; a resume note carrying a lock ignored, the session kept at its card; the setting lockOn bringing the hold back with its chip, padlock, outline, walk and buzz (a control on both trees) and the hint naming it again; German; no page error) — **ALL OK on v531; on a v530 root 6 of its `[flips]` fail** — and `verify-detailfoot` (14: the two-word card's zones in the study order; the line there without a tap reading 鸡蛋 with 鸡 marked and lit; the fold reading Whole card, its block leading with 鸡蛋供应 then pinyin, meaning and Explain; Star, Flag and Delete in the actions with no second row; a tap on 应 reading 供应 and the same tap again putting the line back on 鸡蛋; the fold closing and reopening above the bar; 養樂多 leading a traditional card's block; the neighbour of the open card in the same order and the swipe landing; Star still marking; German dark with Ganze Karte; no page error) — **ALL OK on v531; on a v530 root 9 of its 14 fail**. `verify-r518`'s "the same character again puts it out" and `verify-swaplayout`'s "the detail untouched" are retargeted — the honest record of the two contracts this version reverses; swaplayout 18, r518 29, writepad 54, onewidth 32, lockword 20, foldpos 18, padtail 12, spot 14, recap 15, lockwalk 23, outline 16, lenorder 10, desc 24, ghostpad 10 ALL OK; the load probe passes. Checked by screenshot at 393 × 917 in light and German dark. A `WHATS_NEW` line (the hold that does nothing and the moved block are both the learner's), two `TO_TEST` lines. Not yet field-checked — H's next open card is the check: the word's line under the characters, and Whole card where his thumb expects it.

- **The swiped-in card is exactly as tall as the one it replaces (v530, H with a screenshot of a freshly swiped card: "Bei einer neu geswipten Karte erscheint ein leeres großes Pad. Dadurch scheint das Bild unruhig zu springen. Bitte korrigieren."):** the carousel's neighbour (v417) carries an empty pad in place of the canvas, and that ghost was styled `width:100%;aspect-ratio:1` — the card's full width — while the real pad is what `fit()` leaves above the tab bar: **measured mid-stroke, a 322 px ghost against a 246 px pad at 390 × 844, a 325 px ghost against 317 at 393 × 917.** Two smaller things rode on it: the neighbour was a plain `.card` with 22 px of top padding where the study card has 16 (`.card.study{padding-top:16px}`), and it carried neither the hint a fresh phone's card ends in nor the helper row's height when Show me is showing. So at 390 × 844 the neighbour came in **82 px taller than the card**, its fold row at 793.7 under a tab bar at 782.5, and everything under the photo hopped up at the snap — the picture itself did not move (the neighbour is top-aligned on the card), which is why `verify-r518`'s "nothing moves at the snap" check, which reads the picture box, stayed green through it. Three things: **(1) the ghost takes the standing pad's own rendered side** — `ghostSize(card)` reads `#wpad`'s bounding box when the neighbour is built and writes it inline, the CSS square staying as the fallback for a card without a pad —, and **the helper row its height** (`actsSize`, `min-height` from `#padacts`); **(2) the neighbour carries the study card's own class** (`cls:"study"` from the peer closure, through v460's `{html,cls}`), so it takes the 16 px padding and every other `.card.study` rule — the picbox ratio, the zone, the spotlight — instead of a second copy of them; **(3) it ends in `swipeHint(nd)`** as the card does, which is what v417's "the peer is exactly as tall as the card it replaces" had claimed and the peer's markup had never done. **Measured:** at 393 × 917 and 390 × 844, hints on and off, with Show me showing, in German dark — the neighbour's height equals the card's to the tenth of a pixel, the ghost equals the pad (317 / 246), the fold row stands at the same pixel mid-stroke and after the snap (784.7 / 711.7), and the neighbour's fold row is above the tab bar where v529 put it under. `verify-r518`'s box check still holds on both trees, since the picture box never moved. **What it costs, named:** the neighbour is built from the standing card's measurements, so a card whose pad is on its 200 px floor slides in a neighbour with a 200 px ghost even when that neighbour's own pad, once rendered, would be taller — the pad then grows at the snap, which is the floor's own cost (v519) and not new; and the ghost is measured once per stroke, so a resize mid-stroke is not followed. No key in any column, `lang.js` byte-identical. Suite `verify-ghostpad` (10 checks: the folded screen with hints on — the ghost 317 like the pad, the neighbour as tall as the card with its fold row at the card's own, the study class, the 16 px padding and the hint on both; the swipe landing with the picture unmoved and the fold row where the neighbour's stood; hints off — the same equality and no hint on either; the swipe back; 390 × 844 with the ghost 246 and the neighbour's fold row above the bar; Show me showing with a 40 px row on both; German dark with Ganze Karte; no page error) — **ALL OK on v530; on a v529 root 8 of its 10 checks fail** (the two that pass on both are labelled controls). `verify-swaplayout`'s neighbour-order check reads the six zones without the hint since (the honest record: the neighbour carries the hint from this version on); swaplayout 18, r518 29, writepad 54, onewidth 32, lockword 20, foldpos 18, padtail 12, spot 14, recap 15, lockwalk 23, outline 16, lenorder 10, desc 24 ALL OK; the load probe passes. Checked by screenshot at 390 × 844 mid-stroke in light and German dark: the neighbour's empty pad ends where the card's pad ends. **No `WHATS_NEW` line** — a swipe that no longer hops is the v418 kind of correction; one `TO_TEST` line. Not yet field-checked — H's next swipe is the check: the next card's pad the same size as the one leaving, and nothing under the photo jumping at the snap.

- **A card can carry a short description in the app's language, and Explain asks for one (v529, H mid-v526: "Meaning unten kann dann noch ausführlichere Beschreibung enthalten", then, on the v527 report that named it as its own version: "Go for the ausführlichere Beschreibung"):** the "Whole card" block at the card's foot (v527) shows the card's text, pinyin and meaning, and the meaning is one line — a sign or a dish, not what it is or where one meets it. **The field.** `ds` = `{en:"…", de:"…"}`, one description per language on the card, the shape of `ms` (v265): `descOf(d)` reads the app's language's, `setDesc(card,s,ml)` writes one, a card without one in the current language simply has none — no fallback to another language, since a description is prose and a German phone showing an English paragraph under a German meaning is the v256 pill's problem twice over. A card field like `ms`, so export and import carry it with no line of their own and an older app ignores it; **a changed text drops every description** (`applyCardUpdate`, beside the meanings it already drops). **Where it comes from — the calls the app already makes.** `aiSystem()` asks for `"desc"` beside `"m"` ("two or three short sentences in {language} for the learner: what the text says in its context (a sign, a dish, a button, a slogan, a brand), what its key characters or words mean when that helps, and where one meets it in China; plain words, no markdown, no pinyin; \"\" when the text is bad"), and `picSystem()` the same for a picture answer (`""` when `apart` — a panel's description is not one label's, and `splitCards` blanks it on every label for the same reason); `aiAsk` and `aiReadPicture` hand it back through **`saneDesc`** — `saneM`'s own checks (never the text itself, never all-Han outside Japanese), at least 12 characters, cut at `DESC_MAX` 700 with an ellipsis on a word boundary. So it lands on **every card the AI checks or reads**: the Read preview's and the automatic card's `readingCard` (`sg.ai.desc`, stored under the answer's language), a review's suggestion (`d.ai.desc`, written by **Accept**), the **Edit form's Ask AI** (`aiDesc`, written at Save changes, and the v341 late answer's path), the **Add form's** fill (`S.draft.ai.desc` → `addManual`), and **Translate all**, whose stage carries the new language's description with its meaning and whose undo store names `ds` beside `m`, `ml`, `ms`. **Where it shows.** `backHTML` draws it under `.mean` as `p.desc` (15 px, `--label2`, left-aligned at one measure inside the centred block — prose, not a label) on every screen the back has: the Learn block, the detail's `#d-ans`, the camera's finished card. **And where the card has none, Explain** (`descHTML` with `explain:true` — the Learn block and the detail only; the camera's finished card never, its check still on its way) — its state class is `.desc.want`, not `.desc.ask`: `.ask` is the question sheet's fixed full-screen backdrop (v222), and the first cut borrowed the word and laid an invisible sheet over the whole card that took every tap, which `verify-swaplayout` and `verify-writepad` caught at their next click on the fold (the v421 class-collision lesson, one class along): a quiet `.del` button under the meaning, shown while an AI is on (`aiOn()`, so the relay counts), whose tap runs **`explainCard`** — one `aiAsk` for this card alone with `why` "write \"desc\" for this card and nothing else; keep zh, p and m exactly as given" (`aiCardPayload`'s `explain`), the moving bar in the button's place meanwhile (`EXPLAIN[id]` "busy"), the paragraph **put into the DOM in place** (`refreshDesc` over `[data-desc]`, never `render()`, which would rebuild the pad under a finger — measured: the pad canvas is the same element before and after) and **scrolled whole above the tab bar** (`revealEl`, the v527 rule); a dead call leaves "The AI could not be reached." under the button and an answer without a description "No description came back. Try again.", both with the button back. Offline the tap says so and sends nothing. **Three keys and one guide sentence in nine columns** ("Explain" — de Erklären, ja 解説, ko 설명, ru Объяснить, th อธิบาย; "Explaining …"; "No description came back. Try again."; and the Learn paragraph's "Explain under the meaning asks the AI for a few sentences about the card — what the text says and where you meet it.", appended as its own key so the v527 sentence is untouched — the v259 rule): **469 → 473 a column, ru 502, en 14**, no duplicate in any of the ten (the string-aware source walker and the evaluated counts agree). **What it costs, named:** about 80–150 more output tokens on every text check and picture answer — the relay's count is unchanged, since it rides the call the app already makes —, one call per Explain tap against the relay's daily cap, and a longer block: on a phone whose card fills the screen the description is one more scroll after the fold, which is the v527 trade. **What it cannot promise:** the sandbox cannot reach Qwen or DeepSeek (the v405 rule), so whether the models honour the clause — length, language, no pinyin — is H's next card to say; `saneDesc` is the net under a wrong answer, not a proof of a right one. **The photo path's cost of the first cut, and why the picture prompt asks too:** with `desc` in the text check alone, every card that comes through the picture (over half of H's photos, v439) would have had none until Explain — so the picture prompt asks as well, and only a panel's labels wait for the tap.
