- **The first field round on the write pad, answered as one version (v518, H, 2026-09-18, eight items in one message after v517 landed: "I don't get out of the character locked mode anymore · Vibration there doesn't work · Locked on/off should be more obvious, maybe with a padlock icon? · Completing a row of characters: when automatically jumping to next, pinyin and meaning under the pad don't follow. And they should Always be visible · Cards overview should follow layout. Without drawing pad: edit, star, etc instead · No 'also in other cards' in learn mode. Only on Cards mode. · Swiping cards in learn mode somehow jumps the image … Swiping shouldn't be only possible on the image, all other areas as well, except maybe the pad. · The left and right arrows next to the pad change cards, but that design won't win an award … better ideas?"):** seven built, the eighth answered with three proposals and not built (a design ask waits for a "go"). **(1) The lock's release.** Driven with real touch events through CDP on a v517 root, a *tap* on the locked character released it exactly as v513 says, so the tap path was never broken — what H did is what his own phase-6 prompt says he would do, **press and hold again**, and until v517 a second hold on the locked character re-locked it (`longPress(b,()=>lockChar(...))`, no branch for the locked one) while the hint that says "tap it" is gone after 20 reviews. A hold on the locked character releases now, the tap still does, and the hint and the guide's Learn sentence say both (one key replaced in nine columns, the old one gone — its only other user is `WHATS_NEW[513]`, whose text differs). **(2) The buzz** was `navigator.vibrate(12)` at every site since v354, and 12 ms is under what most phone motors render at all; **no field run has ever confirmed a buzz** — v354's, v513's and v517's are all "not yet field-checked". One helper `buzz(p)`: 40 ms for a hold, `[30,60,30]` for the release, 20 for a finished character. **It cannot be measured here** — the harness stubs `navigator.vibrate` and counts calls — so the phone is the only check, and if 40 ms is still silent the next suspect is MIUI's own haptics switch rather than the app. **(3) A padlock** (`MARK_LOCK`, an inline SVG disc in the button's top-right corner, `.lockmark`, inverted on the current character) on the locked character's button on every card of the walk, gone at the release. **(4) The line under the pad is always there and follows the pad.** v517 showed it only behind the open answer or after a tap, and the lit word was the tapped one (`S.wordCh`) — so when the pad moved on to the next character by itself the line stayed on the old word and the tile stayed lit on it. Both are the pad's now: the lit word is the word of the character the pad is on (`litWi=cur?cur.wi:null`), `padLine(d,cur)` runs on every render, the `hidden` attribute and the tap-off are gone, `S.wordCh` and `wordOn` with them. Measured: on landing the line reads the first word with the answer folded; two characters written by real strokes move the pad to 供 and the line and the light to 供应 without a tap. **And the line has to be in the pad's budget, which the first cut of this version missed and the ratio measurement below caught before the merge:** `fit` still counted v517's `PAD_BELOW` 46 for what sits under the pad, so with the line always there the card ran 121 px under the tab bar at 390 × 844 and 53 on H's folded screen (`cardEnd` 904 against `nav` 783) while the pad-above-the-bar check stayed green — the overflow was below the pad, which that check never looked at. `PAD_BELOW` is **84** (the line at its two-row height plus the helper row's margin) and `.padline` carries `min-height:61px`, so a one-character word does not change the pad; measured under the pad with hints off: line 61, helper row 0, the card ending at 759 against the bar's 783. **What the line costs, named:** at 390 × 844 the pad is **289 px** now and no longer the card's 322 — the v517 symmetry H asked for holds on his own folded screen (393 × 917: pad 325, the width cap) and on the unfolded one, and gives 33 px back to the line on the common phone size; the swipe hint of the first twenty reviews stays outside the budget, as v517 decided, and scrolls the card by 93 px until it goes. **(5) The open card is the study card without the pad** (`detailCardHTML`): the photo in the one 2:1 box, the character row grouped by word, the answer block **open** — this screen is for looking a card up — folded by its own button (`#d-fold`, `S.detailHide` is that fold now; the tap on the picture only swaps crop and whole photo), the line under it for a tapped character (`S.detailCh`, held with the card; the same character again puts it out, since there is no pad here to keep it), and **the six actions inside the card where the pad would stand** (`detailActsHTML`); the schedule line and the linked-photos row stay under the card on the pane. The character row is one helper for all three screens (`chrowHTML`: the study card, its carousel neighbour and the detail), so they cannot drift. Four keys go dead with the old preview's hints ("Tap the character to show / hide the answer", ", or the photo for the whole picture / for the text alone") and leave nine columns (the v403 rule): **474 → 470 a column, ru 503 → 499, en 14**, no duplicate in any of the ten. **(6) No linked-photos row on the study card**; the detail keeps it. **(7) The swipe.** The jump was the neighbour's box: `makePeer` drew it with `frontPic(nd,{page:true})` — no `fixed` — and a page front took the general `.picbox.page{aspect-ratio:var(--ratio)}` rule, since the peer is `.card.peer` and not `.card.study`; a three-line neighbour came in at 4:3 (242 px) and snapped to 2:1 (161). `fixed:true` on the peer and `.card.peer .picbox.page{aspect-ratio:2}`; measured mid-stroke, the neighbour's box is as tall as the card's own (161 == 161) and nothing moves at the snap. And the surface: `wireSwipe` stood down on every button, which on the study card is the whole character row and the fold; it stands down only on the pad, the helper row, the chevrons, fields and chips now, and on **a character row that scrolls** — `.chrow` is `overflow-x:hidden` by default and takes `.scrolls` (`overflow-x:auto`, `touch-action:pan-x pan-y`) only when it is wider than the card (`chrowScrolls`, measured after each render), because a scrolling row owns the horizontal pan and a swipe there would fight it. **What that costs, named:** a card whose row overflows — 骑车勿盯还车勿忘 does at 390 px, six tiles at 428 px against 322 — is swiped from the photo, the fold, the answer or the line, not from its row. **(8) The chevrons: three proposals, not built** — see the report to H; the guide's "or tap the arrows beside the pad" sentence stands until he picks. **(9) A finished card stays folded** (H, minutes later: "Pinyin and meaning open after completing writing a card. Makes card jump, shouldn't."): `cardDone` opened the answer block on the last stroke since v512, and the block appearing above the pad pushed the pad down; with the line under the pad carrying the word's pinyin and meaning since (4), the block has nothing left to say there and stays folded — the fold button opens it, and the release of a locked character (v513) still opens it on purpose. Suite `verify-r518` (25 checks, real touch through CDP: the hold locking with a 40 ms buzz and the padlock, the padlock on the next card of the walk, a second hold releasing with the two pulses, the tap still releasing; the line on landing with the answer folded and the pad's word lit without a tap, two characters written by real strokes moving line and light to 供应, a tap on 应 reading it inside its word, the second tap leaving both; a card on another photo with no linked row in Learn; the detail as the study card with its 2:1 box, row, open answer with pinyin, no pad, the six actions inside the card, the linked row and no overflow, the fold's button, a tapped character lit and read, the second tap putting it out; the fold button as a swipe surface, the three-line neighbour's box as tall as the card's mid-stroke with nothing moving at the snap, a character button as a swipe surface on a row that fits, the pad never one, an overflowing row scrolling instead; no page error) — **ALL OK on v518; on a v517 root 10 of its first 13 checks fail and the run then dies at the missing `.card.study.detail`**, the 3 that pass on both labelled controls. `verify-onewidth` (32, three checks added: the finished card leaving the block folded, the whole card ending above the tab bar with hints off on all three cards, the line two rows tall on a one-character word; and its "the pad is as wide as the card" retargeted at 289 ≤ 322, the cost named above) and `verify-writepad` (54) ALL OK with four checks retargeted — v517's "the same character tapped again puts the word out" and "the lit word does not survive onto the next card", and v512's "the line under the pad is hidden while the answer is folded" and "the whole card written: the answer block opens", each the contract this version reverses on purpose; `verify-lockwalk` (22), `verify-recut4` (19), `verify-hdrfilter` (23), `verify-newflag` (27), `verify-piczoom` (11) ALL OK — newflag died once at its second photo's Save-now button at the end of a nine-suite sequential run and passed whole on its own, the reader racing under load and not the app. Checked by screenshot in light and German dark: the line and the lit word on landing, the padlock, the open card. A `WHATS_NEW` line, six `TO_TEST` lines. Not yet field-checked — H's next session is the check, and the buzz is the one thing only his phone can answer.

- **One geometry on every card, the real Kai outlines as the template, a tap that reads a word, and a star for a finished one (v517, H on the three proposals put to him as screenshots from the real app: "Implement your recommendations", then mid-turn "You also don't need clear and undo at the bottom", then "Implement this only … plus highlight words", then "Misunderstanding. apply the L1 / brush / outlines / praise patch. Plus highlight words"):** phase 5 of `SPEC-flashcard-layout.md`, four things in one deploy. **(1) The photo box and the pad are constants, and the reason they were not is arithmetic rather than taste.** Two zones grew with the photo's line count at the same time — v514's picture ratio (2:1 / 3:2 / 4:3) and the character buttons' one row per line — so they compounded and the pad took what was left: **measured at 390 × 844 with the answer folded, photo 161/215/242, buttons 60/128/196, pad 309/200/200, the card running 6/19/114 px past the tab bar**, and the pad narrower than the picture above it (309 against 322), which is the asymmetry H was looking at. Now the study card's box is **`FRONT_RATIO` 2** whatever the text (`frontPic(d,{fixed:true})`, `.card.study .picbox.page{aspect-ratio:2}`) — **the picture is still CUT at v514's per-line ratio and fitted inside with the v232 blurred fill, and the card detail still shows each card's own shape**, which is `verify-recut4`'s own control — and the characters are **one row that scrolls sideways** (`.chrow` row/nowrap/`overflow-x:auto`, each photo line still its own `.chline` group with a hairline between). `fit` then measures the same numbers on every card: it takes the answer block's height back off the top (so **opening the answer no longer shrinks the pad**, 322 → 322 where v516 went 252 → 200) and counts a constant **`PAD_BELOW` 46** instead of whatever actually sits under the pad, so the helper row appearing, the swipe hint and the linked-photos row make the card scroll rather than the pad shrink. **Measured: photo 161 and pad 322 on a one-, two- and three-line card at 390 px, 238 at 360 px, nothing overflowing sideways in either.** **Undo and Clear leave the helper row** (H, mid-session) and are drawn only for a character the stroke set lacks, where the learner really is drawing freehand — both handlers are null-guarded, since the buttons may not exist. **(2) The template is the real Kai outline.** Until v516 a template stroke was a constant-width round-capped polyline through the raw median samples, and those samples wobble — the first stroke of 我 runs y 348, 350, 358, 370, 368, 378 — so every sample showed as a kink; a stroke of even thickness cannot read as writing whatever it follows. **`vendor/outlines.txt.gz` (7.31 MB gzipped, 9,534 characters)** carries the true Arphic Kai outline of every stroke, out of the same `graphics.txt` the medians come from, quantised onto a 256 grid (**measured against the raw paths and the 512 grid: indistinguishable, including the 12,255 paths that carry a negative coordinate**) and stored y-up, flipped at draw time by the transform `translate(off,off) scale(k,-k) translate(0,-OUT_Y0)` — our medians are `900 − y` of the source, verified on 丁 and 我. It is **loaded in the background after the medians and nothing waits for it** (`loadOutlines`, through `vendorFetch`, cached in `zt-ocr-v1`), and it is **deliberately not in `OCR_FILES`** — the v401 trap, where one non-reader entry silently kills `warmReader` for every existing user. Until it lands, and for any character it lacks or whose stroke count disagrees (`outlinesFor`), **`brushPath` draws instead**: the samples smoothed (Chaikin, twice) and given a width along the stroke from its own inferred kind (`strokeKind` — 横/竖/撇/捺/点 and their hooks, from direction, length and the turn at the tail; the median file carries no stroke type, so a wrong guess costs a stroke drawn a little too evenly, never a wrong shape). The learner's own ink is smoothed by the same Chaikin and keeps its even width. "Show me" still animates along the centreline, since a fraction of a filled outline is not a thing. **(3) A tap lights the whole word and reads it** — H's own framing, and it needed no new data model: `padTargets` already returns `wi`/`word`/`wstart` per character and `groupRow` already renders one `.chw` per dictionary word, so the tile only needed lighting (`.chw.on`). The line under the pad carries the word with the tapped character marked, its pinyin and meaning, **and a second row for the single character** when the word has more than one — **its syllable taken out of the word's own pinyin rather than looked up alone**, so 应 in 供应 reads **yìng** and not its isolated yīng. The same character tapped again puts the word out; the tap still picks the character to write, so nothing the pad could do before is lost; the lit word is held with its card (`S.wordCh={c,i}`) and cannot survive onto the next one. **One thing this exposed and fixed:** `bestSense` skipped surnames, variants and abbreviations but not a Taiwan-pronunciation note, so 应 came out meaning "Taiwan pr." — it skips that too now, which also mends the parts row. **(4) A finished word is praised** (§ 12): a star lifts out of the pad and flies an arc into a **counter at the right of the top bar**, which then **stays while the day has points in it** — a counter to watch grow rather than a receipt that fades, so the bar does not jump twice a card — and the praise is proportional: a card written clean sends a **gold** star with a ring spreading out of the pad, a card that needed a Skip sends a plain one. `NEXT_MS` **900 → 1500**, a tap anywhere on the card that is not a control skips straight on, `prefers-reduced-motion` keeps the pause and the number and drops the travel, and the star's origin is **clamped to the visible part of the pad**, since the answer block opening can push the pad below the fold. **Nothing about the schedule, the grade, the points arithmetic or the repeat pass changes** — the counter reads `daily[day].w`, the figure More → Progress already calls "Written today", and no key was needed in any column (the label reuses `"Written today"`, 474 a column, ru 503, en 14, `lang.js` byte-identical). Suite `verify-onewidth` (29 checks: the box and the pad identical across one-, two- and three-line cards with the pad as wide as the card and whole above the tab bar; every photo line still its own group; the answer block leaving the pad alone; no Undo/Clear on a template character and both on a free one; the outlines loading, matching stroke for stroke and being refused when they do not; the tap lighting exactly the word's characters, the two lines, the character's in-word reading, the tap-off, another word taking the light, a one-character word getting one line, and the light not surviving the card; the star, the gold and the ring on a clean card, the counter, the origin on screen, the tap skipping, the dwell, and the counter staying) — **ALL OK on v517; on a v516 root 7 of its first 10 checks fail and the run then dies at the missing `OUTLINE_OF`**, and the 2 that pass on both are labelled controls. `verify-lockwalk` (22), `verify-hdrfilter` (23), `verify-newflag` (27) and `verify-piczoom` (11) ALL OK; **`verify-writepad` (54) ALL OK with three hardcoded waits retargeted** — it slept 1100 ms for the old 900 ms dwell, and a suite that pins a number breaks on every change to it, so it reads `NEXT_MS` from the page (the v413 lesson); **`verify-recut4` (19) ALL OK with one check retargeted**, its "the study card's box of a two-line card measures 3:2" being the v514 contract this version reverses on purpose, with the detail's per-card ratio directly above it as the control. **A harness lesson worth keeping:** a pixel-exact synthetic stroke never registers, because identical coordinates fire no `pointermove` — `verify-writepad`'s own helper has always added jitter, and the new suite must too; and a fixed 0..n-1 stroke run races the pad, whose finished character holds a 300 ms flash before moving on, so the writer follows `S.pad.k` instead. Checked by screenshot in light, German dark and at 360 px: the outline template, mid-write, the lit word with its two lines, the star and ring with the counter. A `WHATS_NEW` line, four `TO_TEST` lines. **What it costs, named:** the characters no longer sit one row per photo line, so a two-line sign is one long row and a long text has to be scrolled to reach its last characters; **7.31 MB** lands on the phone once; every finished card holds 600 ms longer, about 12 s over a twenty-card session, skippable with a tap; and the counter takes 62 px of the top bar, so a long filter name is cut about 50 px sooner than at v516. Not yet field-checked — H's next session is the check: the pad the same size on every card, the template reading as writing rather than wire, a tap on a word he does not know, and the star.
- **The Due and Done capsules are gone from the top bar, and on Learn the filter pill stands where they stood (v516, H, mid-session: "Due und Done da oben sind quatsch. Mach die weg und platziere stattdessen die Filter dort."):** the two capsules had counted the session since v82 (Due = the cards left, Done = the day's writes since v512, the walk's count since v513), and the Learn filter pill of v365 sat in `#main` between the bar and the card, taking a row of the screen the card is measured against (v512's `fit`). Now `setStats` fills `#stat-filter` in the bar with `learnFilterHTML()` — the v425 pill, one control, with the sheet it always had — and wires it; the Deck capsule keeps the other tabs, and `learnChipsHTML`/`wireLearnChips`, the `.learnchips` rules and the `#stat-open`/`#stat-done` elements are gone. **The v308 rule still gates it:** a deck whose learnable cards carry no tag, no star and no unchecked card has a sheet of one row, so the slot stays empty rather than offering a control over nothing. **The bar keeps its height** — the pill is 28 px in the bar against the chip's 36 elsewhere (`#stat-filter .chip.fpill`), so an empty slot and a filled one both measure 50 px at 390 px; a long name ("Not yet checked (4)") ends in an ellipsis at 54 vw instead of pushing the logo (measured: the pill starts 157 px right of the logo's end at 390 px). **What went with the capsules:** the keys `"Due"` and `"capsule:Done"` from nine columns and the `en` column (the v403 dead-key rule) — **476 → 474 a column, ru 505 → 503, en 15 → 14**, no duplicate —, and the walk's own count of v513, which the chevrons say; `S.done` still counts (the v423 resume note carries it) and is simply not shown. Suite `verify-hdrfilter` (23 checks at 390 and 360 px: the empty slot on the seed's untagged deck; no Due, no Done; the pill in the bar reading All cards, inside the bar and not above the card, the Deck capsule hidden, no sideways overflow; the pill opening Learn's sheet; a tag picked naming the pill lit with the session following it, the pill clear of the logo and the bar at its height; a long filter name inside the bar; the Cards tab with the Deck capsule back and no pill; the tag taken off leaving the slot empty; German Alle Karten and Karten; no page error) — ALL OK on v516. `verify-lockwalk`'s three capsule reads are retargeted at the walk's own count in state (the honest record: the capsule is gone), and it, `verify-writepad` (54) and `verify-newflag` (27) are ALL OK on v516. Checked by screenshot in light and German dark: the pill at the right of the bar on Learn, plain and lit. A `WHATS_NEW` line, one `TO_TEST` line. Not yet field-checked — H's next look at Learn is the check: the filter at the top right where Due stood, and the card a row higher.
- **A card from a photo is "not yet checked" until the act of checking clears it, and the flag means "wrong" again (v515, H: "go for 3 and 4" — phase 4 of `SPEC-flashcard-layout.md`, § 9 —, then, on the first cut that flagged every photo card with the note "new — check text, pinyin and meaning": "Make better suggestion for flagging", and "Go" on the design below; the first cut was pushed and replaced under the same number before anything was deployed):** with every new card flagged the ⚑ meant two things at once — "the app is unsure" (v325) and "H has not looked yet" — so the Flagged filter lost its signal and its count grew by one with every photo until a tap took it off. **The state is its own field, `unchecked:true`**, born on every card `readingCard` builds — the automatic card, Save now (whose card `finishPending` fills from the built card), every label of a split panel and the preview's own Save card — and inherited by a flashcard generated from a multicard text (`makeFlashcard`, the v503 shape); a card typed in the Add form is the learner's own and is born checked; absent = checked, so every card from before v515 is checked and export and import carry the field with no line of their own. **It is cleared by checking, never by a tap on it** (`checkCard`): the first full write in Learn (`cardDone`, with the answer block opening), the card detail opened (`renderCardDetail`, the write landing behind the render), an edit saved or an AI suggestion accepted (`applyCardUpdate`), and the flag set by hand (`setFlag` on — a verdict is a look). A swipe past, a chevron and a tab tap clear nothing. **The ⚑ is v514's again:** the `SIGN` records are born without it, the v143 guard tests `!sg.flag` as before, and the note key of the first cut is gone from nine columns; v245's Save-now note and v325's "the reading looks unsure" stand where they stood. **What H sees:** a row **Not yet checked (N)** in the filter sheet — on Cards in the Status group, an OR beside Flagged (v366), counting the open tab's own (v477: the Cards tab counts the flashcards, the Multicards tab a page once through its texts), shown only while a card is unchecked and dropped by `normaliseFilters` when the last one is checked (the v308 rule); on Learn its own Status group beside Starred (`learnNew`, the star's shape: the session then holds every unchecked card with the eight-new cap lifted, v429, and stands down when none is left) — and **the session puts unchecked cards first inside the due group and the new group** whatever the order (`newFirst` after `byWeight`). On the study card the corner glyph has **three states**: a hollow ⚐ on an unchecked card (`.picflag.new`, one tap flags it and so checks it), the tint ⚑ on a flagged one (one tap clears), and **nothing once the card is checked and clean** — the answer block's Flag button stays for re-flagging. The Cards tile shows a quiet **New** chip where the due chip sits (`cardStatus`: a fresh card has no progress row, so the place is free), and a page whose text is unchecked carries the mark at its foot (`.tm.new`). **Two keys in nine columns** ("Not yet checked" — de Noch nicht geprüft, ru Ещё не проверены, th ยังไม่ได้ตรวจ; "tile:New" with its English in the `en` column, since `"New"` already serves the deck bar's legend in the plural — ru Новая against Новые) **and one guide key replaced in ten** (the "Fix the characters" paragraph: "A new card counts as not yet checked until you have written it in Learn or opened it, and the filter shows those alone; flag a card yourself when something looks wrong." — the v259 rule): **475 → 476 a column, ru 504 → 505, en 14 → 15**, no duplicate in any of the ten (source scan and evaluation agree). Suite `verify-newflag` (27 checks, driven through real photos: the automatic card born unchecked in memory and in IndexedDB and not flagged; the Save-now card unchecked and still flagged with v245's note; the preview's box unticked, Save card unchecked and unflagged; the generated flashcard inheriting; the Add form's card checked; the New chip, the page's mark on the Multicards tab, the row with the open tab's count on both tabs, the row ticked narrowing the list and naming the pill; the detail opened clearing it on both sides with the chip gone and the count one fewer; an edit saved and Accept clearing it; the unchecked new cards first after the due ones; Learn's row with the learnable count and its session of the unchecked cards alone, All cards clearing it; the hollow ⚐, the chevron leaving the state, the hollow tap flagging and checking with the tint ⚑, the cleared flag leaving no glyph while the block's Flag button stays; a full write through real pointer events checking the card and writing its review; the last card checked standing every filter and row down; German; no page error) — **ALL OK on v515; on v514 4 of its first 8 checks fail and the run then dies at the missing `unchecked`**, which is the flip stated plainly. `verify-writepad` 54 ALL OK with one check retargeted (v512's corner ⚑ on every card is the contract this version reverses: a checked, unflagged card has no glyph in the corner), `verify-lockwalk` (22), `verify-recut4` (19) and `verify-piczoom` (11) ALL OK. Checked by screenshot in light and German dark: the hollow ⚐ on 鸡蛋, the tint ⚑ on the flagged card, the New chips, the sheet with its row, the narrowed list. A `WHATS_NEW` line, two `TO_TEST` lines. **What it costs, named:** one card field; and a card H only ever swipes past stays unchecked for good, which is what the filter is for — his inbox of unlooked-at cards is that row now, not the ⚑. Not yet field-checked — H's next photo is the check: the hollow ⚐ in the corner and the New chip on the tile, both gone after he has written the card once.
- **The card's picture follows its text — one line 2:1, two 3:2, three or more 4:3 — the deck is cut again, and the picture can be pinched (v514, H: "go for 3 and 4" — phase 3 of `SPEC-flashcard-layout.md`, D1 and § 4):** **(1) The window.** `windowRect(r,ratio)` takes the ratio, `frameRatio(n)` gives it from the line count (2, 1.5, 4/3, never taller), `cardLines(d)` counts a card's photo lines (a sign card's `\n`, a word card's `seg` breaks) and `ratioOf(d)` joins the two; every window site of v329 passes the reading's own ratio — `finishPending`, `saveSign`, `provisionalCard`, the Edit form's hand-off and re-crop, v410's `outsideWindow` — while the Save-now placeholder and Image only take the one-line default and are re-cut when the text lands. `FRAME_RATIO` 16:9 stays for the ink-row **proposal** (`shapeBox`, v207), which is a different thing. **(2) The box.** `.picbox` carries the card's ratio inline (`aspect-ratio`) on the study card, the detail and the camera's finished card; a page front carries it as `--ratio`, read by the study card's cover-fitted box of D5; the shared PNG's box follows it too (`cardImage`); the Cards tile keeps 4:3 with the wider picture fitted. That is the deliberate step off v223's "one shape on every card": the shape is tied to the second row of buttons the learner sees anyway. At 390 × 844 the pad grows from 250 to about 272 px under a one-line card. **(3) The re-cut, `RECUT_V` 4:** `recutCard` now tells which rectangle the stored picture is — the old 16:9 window (cut again at the new ratio), already the new window (nothing to do), a split label's own frame (byte-identical, it never had a window), or none (left alone) — and **the guard compares like with like:** the fresh cut of the OLD window against the picture the card has says whether the frame still describes it (v398's `RC_CORR` 0.8), and only then is the new window written; comparing the new shape against the old picture would have refused every card the pass exists for. Measured on the suite's textured photo: three of eight eligible cards written, five skipped by construction, `recutStat` `{v:4,written:3,skipped:5}`. **(4) Pinch and pan** (`attachPicZoom`, § 4): two pointers pinch around their midpoint up to `ZOOM_MAX` 5, one pointer pans once enlarged, the view clamped so no gap opens that was not there at rest; while enlarged the box carries `touch-action:none` and its pointer events stop at the box, so neither the page's scroll nor the carousel takes the pan; a pan's closing click is eaten so it is not the v55 tap, which still swaps crop and whole photo; the next card resets it, since the DOM is rebuilt. On a page front the `pagewrap` moves as one, so the regions stay on their texts — measured, the region's centre at the same fraction before and after. Suites `verify-recut4` (19 checks: `windowRect` at the three ratios and the default; `cardLines` on a word card, a two-line card and a sign; the pass at v4 with `recutStat` written 3; the one-line card's window 480 × 240, the two-line 405 × 270, the sign 480 × 360, in memory and in IndexedDB; a card without a frame, a split label's frame and a card already at 2:1 all byte-identical; Diagnostics' line; the detail's box ratio per card, the study card's box measuring 3:2 under the pad still square and whole, a fresh `windowCut` at 2:1, the PNG's box taller on a three-line card, the tile at 4:3; no page error) and `verify-piczoom` (11 checks: at rest a drag on the picture is the swipe; a synthetic two-pointer pinch enlarging 2.25× with the transform, the class and `touch-action`; a real drag panning within bounds with no swipe and no peer; the clamp at every edge; the pan's click not swapping; the next card at rest; a page front's region at the same place after a pinch; the tap swapping to the whole photo and back; no page error) — **ALL OK on v514**, `verify-writepad` (54) and `verify-lockwalk` (22) ALL OK beside them. Checked by screenshot: the 2:1 box over the pad. A `WHATS_NEW` line (the learner's cards change under him once more), three `TO_TEST` lines. **What it costs, named:** every card with a window is re-cut once more (the third pass since v398 — about 95 ms a card, spread out, no undo); a one-line sign's window loses about 12 % of its height against 16:9; a card without a frame or a photo keeps its 16:9 picture and shows it fitted in a 2:1 box with fill at the sides, for good. - **The model's pinyin is taken only when every syllable is a Mandarin syllable (v507, H on the crop analysis of 2026-09-18 — his 小 card carried "xio" —: "Go for the pinyin fix"):** `saneP` (v187) counted **vowel groups** — one per character, and a token with none was a broken syllable — so "qiān l" was caught and "xio" was not: it has one vowel group, `i` + `o`, and stood for one character. Now every token is looked up in **`PY_SYLLABLES`**, the 419 syllables of Mandarin without their tones (the standard table plus the interjections m, n, ng, hm, hng and biáng), through `pySyllableCounts(tok)`: tone marks are stripped (NFD, the combining marks off, the diaeresis kept so ü survives), tone numbers and apostrophes go, `v` and `u:` read as ü, and the token is split into syllables every way it can be — "xiao" one, "xian" one or two (xi an), "gōngyìngshāng" three, "xio" none as one and two as xi + o, a lone "l" none. A line is kept when its tokens' counts can add up to the line's character count (a number with its unit stands aside, v323); else the app's own pinyin replaces the line as before. So "xio" for 小 is two syllables against one character and is replaced by xiǎo, "xio chéng xù" for 小程序 the same, "xiěn" for 显 and a vowel soup are replaced — and the v187 case (b for 吧), the joined word, the ambiguous join xī'ān, the number with its unit, two lines, capitals and tone numbers are all kept exactly as they were. **One thing this also mends without being asked for it:** v506's vowel regex had no `v`, so a model writing ü as `lv` or `lu:4` had its whole line thrown away for a "vowelless" token — both are kept now, and the suite labels that check as a flip too. **The ambiguity is settled by the count and nothing else:** a wrong token that happens to split into real syllables — "xiom" as xi o m — is caught only when the counts disagree, which they do whenever one character got a broken syllable; a joined answer whose split fits by chance is the price of allowing joins at all. A "same length, mostly the same characters" rule was considered and **not built**: it would need field evidence this file does not have (the v386 rule), and on H's own sign exact equality is what fired. **Two further guards:** only a placement from **one definite reading** counts — the quick look and the winning pass, both `rectOfLines` — while the close look's `textBandOf` is a quartile band over several *disagreeing* passes and has no single text, so it records none; and only while `picSeen.base` stands, so a v314/v318/v348/v393 re-ask, which deliberately threw the reader's frame away to ask again about the whole photo, is untouched. `N.agreed` carries the text (the v399 rule) and the log says *"the reader placed the frame on 坚果供应 and the AI read the same text back — the reader measured the characters, the AI only confirmed them: the frame stays"*. Eleven correct labels were thrown away **by one and a half percentage points**, and the second line passed at 0.857. **The threshold is not the fault, and the fix is not a threshold change.** The guard exists (v457) because `signAskAI` replaces `sg.lines` with the model's `zh` and `splitCards` builds the cards from `sg.ai.labels` **alone**, so a line the model did not list would be **gone** — it asks whether a line would be lost. **But the line that would be lost is the one the card would otherwise carry, and that is the text check's, not the reader's:** with the answer refused, `signAskAI` applies `r` and the single card reads DeepSeek's text — which on this photo had **already corrected 快者→快煮 and 汤费→汤粥 from the text alone, without seeing the picture**, an independent second opinion that those characters were reader slips. So `picPanel` takes the checked `r.zh` and measures against that: **1.000 on both lines** (verified as a pure function over H's own strings, 11/14 and 6/7 on the raw reading against 13/13 and 6/6 on the checked text). **The safety argument, stated rather than assumed:** where the check *drops* a real line instead of correcting one, the guard stops protecting it — and that line is lost either way, since the one card would carry the checked text without it, so nothing is traded away. **A failed check (the v451 path) has no such text and falls back to the reader's own lines**, unchanged, and so does a check whose answer holds no Chinese at all (`CJK.test(checked)`); `N.panel.checked` records which text was measured (the v399 rule). **`PANEL_COVER` 0.8 is still unfitted — this version does not fit it, it changes what it is measured against**, and `N.panel` is still what the field settles it with. Proven as a predicate rather than argued: the old test matches **0 of 2** of the new rows, the new one 2 of 2. `report.sql` sums over `u.install = <id> OR u.install LIKE <id> || ':%'` — the bare id still matched, for the rows written before that day — and returns `relay_qwen` and `relay_deepseek` beside the total, which is what the warning needs. **H must run it once in the SQL Editor**; until he does, `relay_today` reads 0 and the near-cap section is simply empty, which is the safe way for it to fail. **Then the warning itself, and what "notify" can honestly mean here: there is no push channel and there will not be one.** The app has no service-worker push handler, no VAPID keys and no subscription store, and web push on Android in China goes through FCM, which is blocked — so a real notification would be a large build that then does not arrive. **The unlock is the moment H is actually looking at the owner's rows**, so `relayWatch()` fetches the report once there and puts a line above the tab bar: "One phone is near today's relay cap: qwen 72 of 80.", or "2 phones are near today's relay cap — see All users." The answer is cached in `USERS`, so All users costs no second call (asserted: **one** fetch), and a failed fetch is **silent on purpose** — the row's own Show is where an error belongs (the v198 rule). **The line is the update note's own element and place** (`noteBar(text)`, factored out of `showUpdated`, which now calls it): one look, one ×, one `role="status"`, and `hideUpdated()` at its head so the two can never stack. **And the report says it too**, at the top where H looks first — `Near the relay cap today (2)` with one line per phone — while every phone's own block splits its total under it (`qwen 72 of 80, deepseek 10 of 400`); measured at **39 columns**, inside the box's 40 (the v250 rule). **`RELAY_WARN` is 0.8 of the cap** (`Math.ceil`, so 64 of 80 warns and 63 does not — the boundary is asserted in both directions rather than assumed). **The owner's own phone is never warned about**, since it is exempt from the per-provider caps, and it is recognised without a constant: `installId()` is the phone reading the report. **The one cost, named rather than hidden: `RELAY_CAPS={qwen:80,deepseek:400}` is a SECOND COPY of the relay function's own numbers** — the report reads a table, not the function's constants, so the two must be changed together (the v401 lesson). It is accepted because the copy cannot refuse a call or change what a phone may do; the worst drift is a warning at the wrong number in a report only H reads, and both places carry a comment naming the other. - **The AI bar is one line, and its two bulk actions are the app's own tick and cross (v481, H on v480's wrapped bar: "Please make it look sleek and professional. No two lines. Any suggestions?"):** he was right and the arithmetic says why no wording could have saved it. Rendered in the real bar at H's own 390 px, the card gives the row **358 px**, and with both labels spelled out the content wants **448 px in English, 538 in Russian, 554 in German and 615 in Spanish** — so v480's `flex-wrap` was not a stylistic choice, it was the only thing keeping the bar inside the card. **Seven layouts were measured over all ten languages before one was picked**, and six of them fail: the count sentence with two pills (max 615), with two pills at 14 px and tighter padding (590), with a pill and a text link (587), with *Accept*/*Dismiss* instead of *Accept all*/*Dismiss all* (510), with one pill and one icon button (495), and the count reduced to the bare number with two pills (381, still over in de, es and id). **The only layout that fits every language at both widths is a shortened count phrase with two 44 px icon buttons — measured 310 px at its widest**, and that is what ships: `4 AI suggestions` at the left, a filled green **tick** and a neutral **cross** at the right, both 44 px circles, the words carried on `title`/`aria-label` from the same `"Accept all"`/`"Dismiss all"` keys v480 added. The glyphs are `MARK_TICK`/`MARK_CROSS`, the pair v461 already uses for known and not-yet-known — the app's own visual language for yes and no, not a new one. **The count phrase is a key swap, not an addition:** `"AI suggestion waiting"`/`"AI suggestions waiting"` are gone from all nine columns and `"bar:AI suggestion"`/`"bar:AI suggestions"` replace them, prefixed because a bare `"AI suggestion"` is already the suggestion box's own label (the v371 collision, avoided by construction); English lives in the `en` column as the `capsule:Done` pattern does, Russian keeps its three forms. **465 keys a column and ru 494, byte-identical to v480**; en 12 → 14. **Measured over 10 languages × 390 and 360 px: 20 of 20 one line, the bar 60 px tall everywhere, both aria-labels present, nothing overflowing.** **Two defects the measurement caught that reading would not have.** The two buttons sat **12 px apart vertically** — a flex row aligns its items by their own baselines when they carry inline content, and the tick's path sits lower in its viewBox than the cross's; `align-items:center` on the group settles it. And the accept button was first given the class `ok`, which the page has carried as a **bare `.ok` rule since v82** (`font-size:14px; color:var(--ok); margin-top:12px`) — so it inherited a 12 px top margin from a rule written for a completely different thing; it is `.prim` now, and the comment says why. That is the v421 lesson (a class written for one shape borrowed by another) in its collision form. **What it costs, named and not dressed up:** two bare glyphs carry a thirty-card bulk action, so a mis-tap on the tick accepts everything — which is why both actions write the v369 undo store and More → Check-up offers **Undo last run**. `verify-dismissall` reads the labels from `aria-label` since and asserts the bar is one line (all centres within 2 px and no overflow), so a longer label or a second row fails rather than quietly wrapping — **ALL OK on v481**. **No `WHATS_NEW` line** — the v412 precedent exactly: a layout polish of a control shipped one version earlier. One `TO_TEST` line. Checked by screenshot in light, German dark and Spanish at 360 px. Not yet field-checked — H's own bar is the check.
- **A whole batch of AI suggestions is cleared in one tap (v480, H after a Check-up left 30 of them waiting, most answering `ok:true` with at most a pinyin tweak: "There should be an option to skip all AI suggestions at once."):** the green bar on the Cards tab has offered **Accept all** since v82 and had no counterpart, so thirty suggestions H did not want had to be dismissed one card at a time. **Dismiss all** sits beside it (`#ai-dismissall`, `aiDismissAll`) and is the exact bulk counterpart: `aiDismiss`'s body is `dismissed(d)` now, one shape for the single Dismiss and for the bulk one, so the two cannot drift; the whole batch is **one IndexedDB transaction** (`idbPutMany`, where Accept all still writes card by card through `applyCardUpdate`, since each of those is a text change with its own line-recutting); and it writes the **v369 undo store** exactly as Accept all does (`saveLastRun("dismiss","*",before,n)`), so More → Check-up carries **Undo last run** and one tap puts all thirty suggestions back — memory and IndexedDB, asserted both ways. **Dismissing is not accepting, and that is the check that matters:** the cards' text, pinyin and meaning are byte-identical afterwards and `mt.verified` does not move — the only thing that changes besides `ai` is a `mt.suspect` reason, which goes because a human has now seen it (the v82 single-Dismiss rule, unchanged). **The button is the sheet's own neutral Cancel look** (`.btn.plain` scoped to `.aibar`), not the tint: `.btn` is tint-soft on tint, so beside a filled red *Accept all* a tinted *Dismiss all* reads as a second red button and invites the wrong tap — the v475 lesson (a control that looks like the control beside it) in its button form. **And the bar had to be allowed to wrap, which the measurement forced rather than taste:** three items on one flex row overflowed at **390 px in German and Russian** and at 360 px in German, Spanish and Indonesian; `.aibar` is `flex-wrap:wrap` with the two buttons in their own `.aiacts2` group (`margin-left:auto`, itself wrapping), so the pair moves as a unit and stays right-aligned — measured over **10 languages × 390 and 360 px: 0 overflowing, 0 labels broken inside a button** (the v427 fit rule: ask whether the text broke, not whether the box overflowed), at the cost of the bar being two lines in every language now and three in de/es/id at 360. **Two keys in nine columns** ("Dismiss all" against each column's own word for Dismiss — de Alle verwerfen, ja すべて閉じる against its 閉じる, ru Отклонить все —, and "Dismissed the AI's suggestions on {0} at {1}." mirroring each column's own *Accepted* line, agreement-free by construction since the verb agrees with the suggestions inside the key, not with `{0}` — the v412 rule), **463 → 465 a column, ru 492 → 494, en 12**, no duplicate in any of the ten (source scan and evaluation agree). Suite `verify-dismissall` (19 checks: the bar carrying both actions with its count; one tap clearing every suggestion in memory and in IndexedDB with the bar gone, the cards' own text and `mt.verified` untouched and the suspect reason cleared; the undo store naming the run; More's row with its line, and Undo putting all four back with the bar; Accept all still applying them and writing its own store — the regression guard; no bar at all on a deck with no suggestion, the v308 rule; the German button and the German undo line) — **ALL OK on v480, and on v479 the run dies at the missing button after its first check**, which is the flip stated plainly. The derived and cardstabs suites pass. Checked by screenshot in light, German dark and Russian at 360 px. A `WHATS_NEW` line, one `TO_TEST` line. **What it costs, named:** once the next run replaces the undo store the suggestions are gone for good — the way back is another Check-up, about six relay calls for thirty cards. Not yet field-checked — H's own thirty waiting suggestions are the check: one tap, and the Undo row where he can find it.
- **The reading log belongs to a photo (v479, H after the Diagnostics dump of 2026-09-13: "Fix the interleaved reading log"):** his dump had **"the AI could not check the photo and the reading is weak — no card" standing at step 12 of 16**, before two further `recognizing` steps — one photo's line sitting in the middle of another photo's reading. `READLOG` was **one global 40-line list**, and `cropSign` **wiped it at its start**, so a reading that began while an earlier one was still finishing — v411's album batch, where the next photo starts as soon as the last has its cards while that one's AI check and `finishPending` are still running — **erased its predecessor's steps and then collected its predecessor's tail among its own**. v406 named it ("the per-photo `numbers:` records carried everything that mattered, so it waits for its own PR") and left it. **The fix is not a second store: the steps move onto the record that is already keyed by the photo.** `NUMSOF[id]` has existed since v399 and the ring of three since v405, so `logRead(id,text)` files the line on `N.log` and the misfiling is impossible by construction — `logRead` cannot be called without naming a photo. **57 call sites take the id and every one of them already had it in scope** (`aiReadPicture` through its own `rec`, the rest through their first parameter); only `findFrame` had none and gained one. **Two things it buys beyond attribution, each a defect in its own right.** (1) **The two earlier readings carry their steps at last** — until now `Earlier readings` printed `numbers:` alone, which is exactly the half a human cannot read; they are trimmed head 5 / tail 10 with "… N steps left out", keeping the frame's proposal and the quick look at one end and the outcome at the other. (2) **The progress line overwrites its own photo's line** — `readingStatus` compared against whatever was logged last by anyone, so two photos read close together overwrote each other's "recognizing … N%"; measured on the v478 tree, photo X ends with **no progress line at all** while photo Y's block carries **five**, X's 10 % and 30 % among them. **Three smaller things the rebuild forced, each with its reason.** `LAST_READ.nums` is gone — a second copy of the ring's last entry that had to be kept in step by hand, where `lastRead()` reads it from the one place. **A record joins the ring once and never rejoins** (`N.ringed`): `NUMSOF` keeps six records and the ring three, so without the flag a late line from a reading already pushed out would put it back at the head as the newest — the misattribution in its last hiding place; its steps are still filed under it, they are simply not printed. And **`numsReset` replaces the photo's ring entry in place** and carries the trailing `pre` lines (the frame's proposal, the old crop found) into the new record — v285's rule without the global wipe — so a photo proposed, located and read takes one ring slot and not three. **The numbers' own budget is untouched, which is why the two are kept apart:** `numsTrim` strips `log`, `passes` and `ringed` before it measures, and the steps ride beside the trimmed ring in the setting (`readlog.logs`, matched back by shot id at boot); steps inside that JSON would push the numbers out, which is the v395 fault (the reply cut mid-word) one store along. The passes are stored and printed for the newest reading only, as before. **Measured:** the shared text grows **5 058 → 6 048 characters** on three panel-sized readings of 18 steps each, and buys the two earlier readings their steps where they had none. **A defect found on the way and fixed:** `picOnBad`'s own `aiReadPicture` call passed no record, so that path's answer-shape lines had no photo to file under **and its prompt fingerprint was never written at all** — the v399 rule, one path further on. Suite `verify-readlog` (19 checks: a photo read end to end with its own steps, the frame's proposal first, passes and numbers under it and not inside the numbers JSON; a second photo read after it with the first still listed and its steps intact; two readings overlapping, driven through the app's own `readingStatus` — the late line in its own photo's block and not in the newer one's, each photo keeping its own progress line; every reading coming back with its steps after a restart; a phone still holding a v478 setting; Start over) — **ALL OK on v479, 9 of its 19 checks fail on v478**, and the seven that pass on both are named in the file as controls (the card is made either way, the numbers JSON never carried the steps on either tree, and "the second photo's block carries no line of the first" is vacuous on v478, which prints no shot id anywhere). Eight suites that read `READLOG` are retargeted at the ring's own logs (`LAST_READ.ring.flatMap(N=>N.log)` in place of the global list), and of those the two that drive a whole photo through the pipeline pass: `verify-quota` ALL OK — 14 checks and `verify-shared` ALL OK; `verify-page` and `verify-derived` (25) pass too. **No `WHATS_NEW` line** — Diagnostics sits behind the owner's password and a learner never sees it (the v408 rule). One `TO_TEST` line. Not yet field-checked — H's next dump after two photos in a row is the check: two blocks, each with its own steps, and no line under the wrong photo.

- **A multicard is a reference, and what Learn studies is a text that has EARNED a card (v478, H across five messages, all of `SPEC-derived-cards.md`'s core built: "please analyze whether certain buttons or certain fields appear again and again in multicards and then make flashcards for learning out of them" · "either a text appears again and again on a multicard or I tap a certain text again and again on a multicard. both cases become a flashcard" · "When I select a word on a multicard, I think I should also instantly get the option to make it a flashcard" · "I think multi cards don't really need the got it or learn again buttons" · "flash cards generated from multi cards should be somehow marked as such.", and his "Go as per your recommendation" on D1–D4):** **ONE FIELD, and nothing is deleted or merged.** A page's texts are still the split's own cards with their progress row, star, flag, tags and AI check exactly as v453 made them; what changes is that Learn studies only the ones carrying **`derived:true`**, and the lookup sheet grades nothing. The sources are **not stored**: `sourcesOf(d)` derives them from the deck, so a page photographed tomorrow joins a card's carousel by itself and there is no second copy of the truth to drift (the v401 lesson) — that is the one place this departs from the spec's `d.from`. **Three ways to earn it.** **R9, the manual one, and it is the reason the other two are allowed to be guesses:** the sheet's three grade tiles are replaced by **Make this a flashcard**, one tap, and by **Already a flashcard** once it is one; a wrong threshold then costs patience and never a card H wanted and could not have. **T1, recurrence:** the same text on `DERIVE_PAGES` 2 multicards or more — checked once at boot, so a deck that already holds its multicards earns its first cards with no tap. **T2, repetition:** `DERIVE_LOOKS` 3 look-ups of one text on one multicard, and **the third look-up IS the promotion** — the sheet shows the state at once and the write lands behind it. **Where the counter may live was decided by the spec's own measurements, not by convenience:** not keyed by card id (`cardId` recycles a freed text as the next card's id, v118, so a count would transfer between unrelated cards), not in the progress row (`importData` drops every row without a numeric `due`, which is exactly an un-promoted item's shape) and not as a field on the item (`putCard` rewrites the whole record including its crop Blob on every tap) — so it is `settings.lookups`, keyed **page + text**, which forces two things it now does: it is in **`RESET_KEYS`** (it holds the photos' own characters — the v458 leak) and its debounced writer is in `resetAll`'s `clearTimeout` line, and it is capped at `LOOK_MAX` 2000 keys, least-looked-at first. **Q5, T2's dirty signal, answered by cleaning rather than by absorbing:** a tap on the same region while its own sheet already stands no longer counts a second time; a tap that misses a small region and lands on the nearest one (v448's 44 px rule) still does, because it is a look-up either way. **THE COST, and H approved it (D3): a text that has not qualified leaves Learn AT ONCE** — his ~20 washing-machine texts drop out of the due deck the day this ships and come back one at a time. Nothing is lost: the progress rows stay, so a promoted text returns with its whole history, and **a card made on purpose joins TODAY's session** (appended at the end, which is what an `again` grade already does, v428 — without it the reward for tapping the button would be a card that appears after the next reload; the suite caught that). **The carousel (R6, R7):** a derived card whose text stands on several multicards shows them **all**, side by side, snapping, most looked-at first (D2: "order of use" is look-ups of THIS text on that multicard, the number T2 already counts, so the sort is free) — and each slide carries its own `me`, the sibling text on that photo, so the frame is drawn around this card's text wherever it stands. One source is exactly v452's page front and renders through the same `pageHTML`, so there is one way of drawing a page. **The mark (R8, D4), in both places:** a quiet pill beside Traditional on the card ("From a multicard" / "From 2 multicards") and a small two-plate chip on the Cards tile beside the flag and the AI mark. **Two keys rather than a count word, deliberately:** «Из {0} мультикарточек» wants the genitive plural after a numeral and a fixed phrase at one, which no plural table of this app gets right by itself — the v412 rule that no agreement may cross a key boundary. **v461's cross and check are NOT taken away; where they show is narrowed:** only a text that has earned a card carries one, because an unpromoted text has no learning state and a red cross meaning "you cannot do this yet" would be false about a text nobody is being asked to learn. H fought four rounds over those marks and the spec's reading was that he now wants them gone; narrowing is the smaller move and **whether they should go entirely is his call, named here rather than taken.** **And the grades stay on a marked photo that is NOT a multicard** — v448's own screen, which every photo from before v453 still is and whose texts are ordinary flashcards already; H's "multi cards don't really need the got it or learn again buttons" is about multicards, so that is the only place the grades went. `verify-photomode`'s "three grades" assertion is what guards it. **Five keys in nine columns** (the action, the state, the two pill forms and the guide's sentence), **458 → 463 a column, ru 487 → 492, en 12**, no duplicate in any of the ten, the static key check reporting the same five standing hits; the guide's Cards section gains its own paragraph in all ten (the v259 rule), and `privacy.html`'s usage list names the new counter (`regionCards` beside `regionTaps` and `regionGrades`). Suite `verify-derived` (25 checks: the clean break — the plain card alone in the queue, the Deck capsule counting the page once; the sheet with no grade tiles and the one action; the tap writing `derived` to memory AND IndexedDB, the sheet swapping in place, Learn studying it, the Cards tile with its chip, the card with its pill, and only that text marked in the page's list; two look-ups promoting nothing and the third promoting by itself; the same region tapped three times while its sheet stands counting once; T1 at boot with the queue holding exactly the plain card and the promoted one; two slides each framing this card's text on its own photo, and one source giving the single page; the counter filled and then wiped by Start over; the German action and the German guide) — **ALL OK on v478, 19 of its 25 checks fail on v477**; the six that pass on both are labelled controls in the file. **Three suites were retargeted rather than left red, each naming the contract that moved:** `verify-page` (its session check now asserts that NO text is studied until one earns a card, its sheet check asserts no grades and the action, and its Learn block promotes a second text because the first was just scheduled 30 days out), `verify-cardtiles` (the page's list starts bare and a mark appears once a text is promoted) and `verify-photomode`, which needed **no** change and is therefore the guard on the narrowing. The cardstabs, pagefront, pageswipe, starfit and aiswitch suites pass untouched. Checked by screenshot in light and German dark: the sheet, the carousel, the back. A `WHATS_NEW` line, two `TO_TEST` lines. **Measured and named, not chased:** the overflow scan over ten languages × 390 and 360 px reports `.picbox.page` and `.cs` **identically on a v477 root** — the first is the blurred fill's deliberate `width:120%` (the v465 measurement bug, named again so it is not chased a third time) and the second the star's 44 px target in a 33 px column at 360 px, both older than this change. **Not built, and named:** the spec's promote-and-merge, which deletes the sibling items — the derived card is simply one of them and the others stay as their page's dots, which is less destructive and reaches the same place; and Q4, a derived card whose only source photo was deleted, where `fullPhoto` falls back to the item's own copy and the carousel drops a slide it cannot draw. Not yet field-checked — H's washing machine is the check, and it is a hard one: his ~20 texts leave Learn at the first start, and what comes back should be the buttons he actually looks up.
- **Two tabs under Cards (v477, H: "there should be actually two different tabs for cards. under cards. One for multi cards and one for normal cards." — R4 of `SPEC-derived-cards.md`, the first piece of it built):** one scope bar under the search field (`.seg.scope`, the app's own segmented control full width, its halves equal), **Cards** and **Multicards**, and **everything below it reads one list** — `cardsList()` filters by the open tab and the search, the filter sheet, the count, the marking, the tile grid, the place ← Cards puts the list back to (v352/v445) and the swipe's neighbours all come off it, so nothing had to be taught about the split twice. **The bar appears only while a page exists** (the v308 rule: a control over an empty set is a control over nothing), so a deck with no multicard is byte-for-byte what it was — that is the suite's first check. **Cards is the default and comes first**, because it is the bigger half of every deck and a tab you land on should be the one you use most; H's own order ("one for multi cards and one for normal") is a list, not a layout. The choice rides on `S.cardsTab` and joins the screen note (v415/v423), so a reload comes back to the tab you were on, as the search already did. **One key in nine columns** ("Multicards", each column's own rendering — fr Multicartes, es Multitarjetas, ja マルチカード, ko 멀티카드, ru Мультикарточки, vi Thẻ gộp, th การ์ดรวม, id Multikartu), **457 → 458 a column, ru 486 → 487, en 12**, no duplicate in any of the ten, and the static key check reports the same five standing hits. v452 dropped "Multi-card" as a name for a **pill on the Learn front** — jargon on a surface a learner reads mid-study; a **tab** is a different job, it names a category rather than describing a card, and it is H's own word. **The guide follows the screen in the same PR** (the v259 rule): its Cards paragraph gains "Once a photo has made a multicard, two tabs split them — Cards and Multicards." in all ten columns, spliced into each column's own existing sentence rather than retranslated, so the terminology stays put. **And the filter sheet's numbers became the open tab's own, which is not decoration:** they counted raw records over the whole deck while the list counts a page once and lets it match through its texts (v453), so the two never agreed — with two tabs that gap reads as broken ("⚡ Flagged (12)" over a list of one). `tabPool()` and `anyOf()` are the list's own pool and predicate, and the sheet reads both; a row's **visibility** stays deck-wide, since a row that vanished on one tab while its filter was on is the v308 trap all over again. Suite `verify-cardstabs` (19 checks: no bar at all on a deck with no multicard; the bar with both labels and Cards lit, listing the ordinary cards alone; the Multicards tab listing the pages alone with its own count denominator; a search staying inside a tab and surviving the change; the sheet's flagged count per tab and a tag that lives only on the other tab counting 0; a page opening from the Multicards tab and ← Cards coming back to it; the swipe's neighbour being the other page, with an ordinary card deliberately seeded BETWEEN the two pages so a mixed list would give a different answer; the marking hiding the bar and All marking the tab's two pages only; a reload coming back to the tab; the two labels fitting in all ten languages at 390 and 360 px; the German labels and the German guide) — **ALL OK on v477, 15 of its 19 checks fail on v476.** **Four suites were retargeted rather than left red, and each retarget says which contract moved:** `verify-cardtiles` takes its reading on **both** tabs and states which tab each thing belongs on (and its ← Cards check compares against the scroll the shorter list actually reached, not a fixed 200 px); `verify-starfit` walks both tabs — and its first cut clicked the tab *inside* the same `page.evaluate`, which re-renders `#clist` and left every element it had already collected detached, so `getComputedStyle` came back empty and the margin check failed for a reason that had nothing to do with the app; `verify-page` reads the Cards list on the Multicards tab; and `verify-pageswipe` is **relabelled a pure regression guard** — its fixture gains a page on each side, its two list assertions branch on whether the tree has the bar, and it passes on v476 and v477 alike, which is exactly what it is for. The pagefront, camtab, taptoframe and aiswitch suites pass untouched. Checked by screenshot in light and German dark, both tabs. A `WHATS_NEW` line, one `TO_TEST` line. **What it costs, named:** a multicard is no longer found by scrolling the Cards tab — it is one tap away and nowhere else; and `detailSwipe`'s page/card dispatch is now belt-and-braces rather than a live case, kept and commented so neither screen can be handed a body of the wrong shape. Not yet field-checked — H's own deck is the check: is the bar where his thumb expects it, and is Cards the right default?
- **The AI-review switch means what it says, and the relay can be switched off at all (v476, H: "Fix the 3 points" — two of the three items v459 raised, v472 re-raised and he had twice chosen other work over):** **(1) An interrupted bulk run no longer resumes on its own while the switch is off.** `resumeTranslate`, `resumeTagAll` and `resumeRecheck` gated on `aiOn()` — whether an AI is set up at all — rather than on `aiAutoOn()`, and boot, `online` and every return to the foreground call all three; so a phone with the AI review unticked and a Check-up, Translate-all or Tag-all run half done sent **every remaining card's text** to the provider with no tap, at the next start. The switch's job is to say whether the app may call the AI **without being asked**, and a resume is exactly that, so all three gate on `aiAutoOn()` now. **Nothing is lost and the run is not abandoned:** the `translateRun`/`tagRun`/`recheckRun` settings and the stage are untouched, so the row's own button continues from where it stopped — asserted, since a run that could never be finished again would be a worse bug than the one being fixed. **And the row stopped promising something it can no longer do:** "It goes on by itself when the AI can be reached again." is appended through **`resumeNote()`** at all five sites, which returns "" while the switch is off — no new key in any column, and `sp()` keeps the join from leaving a trailing space. **(2) `aiRelay` is written somewhere at last.** It has been read by `relayOn()` and `viaRelay()` since v191 and written **nowhere**, so the relay could be switched off only by hand-editing IndexedDB — a dead setting that three audits named and none closed. The checkbox sits in the **owner's setup form**, under the picture one ("Use the app owner's relay when this phone has no key of its own"), saved by that form's Save whatever chip is lit, since the relay is the phone's and not one provider's. **It is deliberately not a second switch in the learner's row**, and that is v190's decision holding ("move the AI review details into the locked area and only leave the switch for the users"): a learner who unticks it and has no key gets an app with no AI at all — every new card unverified and pending for ever — which is a large degradation offered as a checkbox with no explanation, and the learner already has the one control that matters. It stays out of `RESET_KEYS` for the v458 reason: it is a `!==false` default, so deleting it would silently switch the relay back **on**. **`privacy.html` follows the code in the same PR** — both places that said an interrupted run "still resumes on its own" now say it resumes only while the switch is ticked and otherwise waits for the button. Suite `verify-aiswitch` (a German phone with all three runs interrupted and cards left for each: the switch off → **no AI call at all** through boot and four seconds of resume windows, no run running, the three settings still remembered, the row's failed line without the promise and with its button; the switch on → all three resume with no tap and the line does promise it, the regression guard; the owner's form carrying the relay switch ticked by default, unticking it writing `aiRelay` false to memory **and to IndexedDB**, surviving a reload and showing unticked, and a keyless phone with the relay off reading "Off."; privacy.html both ways) — **ALL OK on v476, 10 of its 16 checks fail on v475**; the two that pass on both are named in the file as controls (a v475 run simply finishes inside the four-second wait, so "no run is running" is not a flip; and seeding `aiRelay:false` by hand works on v475 too, since the setting was always read). The privacy, camtab and quota suites pass. Checked by screenshot in light and dark: the form with both checkboxes, nothing overflowing at 390 px. A `WHATS_NEW` line, one `TO_TEST` line. **What it costs, named:** a phone whose owner unticks the AI review mid-run has a stage sitting in its settings until the button is pressed again — no data is lost, but Translate all will report "20 translated, 23 left" until then. Not yet field-checked — H unticking the AI review with a Check-up half done is the check: nothing goes out at the next start, and the button still finishes it.
- **The batch line goes back to v412's own geometry, because v471's pill broke a contract that version had measured (v474, the audit's own last finding):** v471 gave the Camera tab's one remaining line the weight of a **pill** — `--tint-soft`, radius 999, 14 px, the waiting tiles' clock beside it — and it looked right on H's 390 px phone. It is wrong all the same, and the suite that found it is `verify-waiting`, which the record had been carrying as "**pre-existing**, fails 5 of its checks byte-identically on a v467 root" since v468. **That was true of the cause and false of the conclusion:** those five checks had been red since **v466**, when a waiting photo became a **tile with a clock chip** instead of a full-width row with a badge, and the suite still read `#shots .shot` only. Retargeted to read the tiles too — the words are the same key, carried by the chip's `title`/`aria-label` — it went green **except for its last case**, and that one was not fixture debt: **the batch line wrapped to two lines in French, Spanish, Korean and Russian at 360 px.** v412 spent a whole version getting that sentence onto one line in **all 30 language × count combinations**, and dropped a candidate for wrapping in 12 of 30; v471's pill wraps in **9 to 13 of 30**, by the same measurement, on H's friends' narrower phones. **Measured over every variant rather than argued:** at 360 px the line's box is 328 px whatever the padding, so the pill's 22 px of side padding and the icon's 19 px come straight out of the text — 14 px pill 13 wrapped, 13 px pill 8, 12.5 px pill 7, no icon and 6 px padding 1, and **only 4 px of side padding with no icon fits all 30**, which is v412's own geometry. So the line keeps that geometry and takes its presence from **colour and weight alone** — measured **0 of 30 wrapped at 360 px and 0 of 30 at 390 px**. It shipped for a few minutes as a full-width tinted **band** and that was wrong for a second reason the screenshot showed and the arithmetic could not: a full-width tinted rounded rect sitting **directly under From album**, itself a full-width tinted rounded button, reads as a second button and invites a tap that does nothing. **v475** takes the background away: the line is a left-aligned tint caption at 13 px weight 500, unmistakably not a control, still far more present than the grey it replaced, and the same 0 of 30 at both widths. Its own suite check asserts the background is transparent, so the band cannot come back either. The clock stays where it belongs, on the waiting tiles themselves. **The rule it stands for, and it is the v427 lesson in a third form: presence that costs width is not free in a ten-language app — check the language that has no room before, not after.** `verify-camtab`'s chip assertion is retargeted (no icon, **one line**, a transparent background and a colour that is not the grey label token, so neither the pill nor the band can come back unnoticed) and **fails on v473 and on v474**; `verify-waiting` is retargeted at the five v466 assertions and its last case measures the band, the one place the words are actually rendered. The camonly, shutter, todo and tiles suites pass. Checked by screenshot in light and German dark. **No `WHATS_NEW` line** — the v412 precedent exactly: a wording-and-weight polish of a line shipped three versions earlier. Not yet field-checked — H's next album batch is the check, and a friend's 360 px phone is the one that matters here.
- **The audit's fourth copy of a sentence v459 killed three times, and a splash colour that died at v82 (v473, the same "Komplett Audit"):** **(1) The AI review row's own STATE line still read "On, through the app owner's relay: DeepSeek (deepseek-chat) checks the text, Qwen (qwen3.7-plus) reads **the framed area when the reading is weak**."** — false twice over since v302 (`picOnBad` fires at any reader score), v439 (the picture leaves at the **quick look**, before the reading proper) and v348/v393/v450/v453 (the whole photo goes out on several paths). v459 rewrote About, the row's "What is sent" sentence and the guide, and **missed this one** — and the reason it survived a whole audit is worth the entry: **`verify-privacy` read `#ai-status`'s next sibling, the sentence UNDER the state line, and never the line itself.** It reads both now, and the two new checks **fail on v472 with the exact false sentence**. The line is "On{0}: {1} checks the text, {2} reads a picture of it when the reading is hard." in ten columns (457 a column, ru 486, en 12, no duplicate, no key added or removed), and the owner's own setup checkbox, which said the same thing in English, is "Send a picture of the text to the AI when the reading is hard". **(2) `manifest.webmanifest` still carried `#141410` for `background_color` and `theme_color`** — the lacquerware ground the design review replaced at **v82**, and a colour that exists nowhere else in the app: `index.html` has said `#F2F2F7` / `#000` since. Android takes those two from the manifest for the **splash screen and the task switcher**, so a fresh install has been flashing a dark olive for three hundred versions. Both are `#F2F2F7` now. **What it costs, named:** an installed app keeps its old manifest until the system refreshes it (the v167 lesson), so this lands on a re-install or whenever Chrome next picks the manifest up — H will not see it on his phone today. **No `WHATS_NEW` line** (the v408 rule: a corrected sentence and a splash colour are not a feature), one `TO_TEST` line. **The rest of the sweep came back clean and is recorded so it is not repeated:** no comment naming a constant's value that the constant does not have (0 of the whole file), `signs.json`, `nmt-model.json`, the three icons and `privacy.html` all present at the sizes the shell expects, the manifest's `share_target` and `scope` unchanged, and **the performance measured again at H's own scale and above** — boot to the first card **224 ms at 300 cards and 348 ms at 1000**, the Cards list **132 ms and 306 ms**, a search keystroke **14 ms and 46 ms**, the Camera tab 44 ms and 107 ms, the queue under a millisecond, **61–62 fps** after a scroll to the end.
