Named, not optimised. Not yet field-checked — More → AI review is the check: the row should say the AI reads a picture, not a frame.
- **The thirteenth audit, and the field finding that made it necessary (v472, H, 2026-09-13, with a full Diagnostics dump: "Also, hier hat weder Multicard funktioniert noch, dass die prozessierten Fotos von der Kameraseite verschwinden, wenn sie fertig sind.", then "Du machst jetzt bitte mal ein Komplett Audit, suchst nach Widersprüchen und löst sie auf und polisht komplett drüber."):** **THE OPERATIONAL FINDING FIRST, because no code change touches it: `[picture] relay error 403: Free quota exhausted. To continue accessing the model on a paid basis, please add funds or disable the "use free tier only" mode in the management console.`** Qwen's free tier on the **relay's** key is spent, so **every phone without a Qwen key of its own — H's included, which is what his own record shows — has no picture reading at all**, and that is the whole of "Multicard funktioniert nicht": no picture answer means no `apart`, no `labels`, no split, one card. It is H's Bailian account to settle, and this file's v451 entry, which said his phone reads pictures on its own key, is corrected. **What the code got wrong about it is the audit's first contradiction, and it is the v384/v395/v399/v405 fault one path further on: the app said the opposite of what happened.** `picOnBad` consumed the parked early answer as `(await early.p).pic` and logged **"the picture answer asked at the quick look 21.7 s ago is used"** whatever came back — so H's diagnostics claimed a paid-for answer was used when it had 403'd; `N.picErr` stayed **null**, the error log carried nothing from that path, and `N.early.ok` stayed `null` as if the call were still pending. `picPanel` swallowed a rejected parked promise the same way. Both go through **`noPicture()`** now — one place that writes the failure into the reading's record, into the numbers, into the error log (so the daily row and All users carry it) and into the reading log. **Then the card that should never have been built.** His shot read 自回回回还 | 还一一一 at **effScore 183**, three points over `WEAK_READ`, so v438's gate — which asks for `sg.weak` — did not fire, and the app built the card, `verified`, with the whole screenshot as its picture. Three independent signals had already said the text was worthless: **v441's own per-line test held the provisional back** (94 and 93, under `PLACE_CF`), **DeepSeek answered `bad:true` twice** ("OCR garbage: no plausible sign, menu or product text can be made of these repeated 回/还/一 characters"), and **the picture call that could have settled it was refused**. The gate is `noPic && (sg.weak || (sg.ai.bad && !sg.sureLines))` since: the reader unsure of its own lines, the text model rejecting them, and no picture answer at all. **A reading whose every line IS read surely keeps its card even against a bad verdict** — the v143 rule, and v348's finding that a text-only garbage verdict is weaker evidence than the picture's; that case is the suite's control and still makes its card. **And the row no longer claims the AI "could not be reached" when the AI answered and refused:** one key replaced in nine columns, "The AI could not check this photo, and the reading alone was not good enough for a card." — true of a dead network and of a 403 alike (457 keys a column, ru 486, en 12, no duplicate). **The breaker, and the regression it caused before it worked.** A 4xx that is not 429 is a **refusal** — no funds, a dead key, a forbidden call — and the next photo gets the same answer, so `picRefused` stands the picture path down for `PIC_DOWN` 10 minutes and any answer clears it (`picOk`); a 5xx, a timeout and a dead connection are transient and change nothing; a 429 is deliberately excluded, since a provider's rate limit clears in seconds and the relay's own daily cap has its own sentence. The shape is v189's `ORIGIN_DOWN` one layer up, and it saves H's phone 88–134 KB and twenty-odd seconds **per photo** while the quota is out. **The first cut put `pictureUp()` in `picOnBad`'s own guard and the suite caught it at once: the parked 403 then left no `picErr` at all, the no-card gate went quiet, and the garbage card came straight back.** The breaker belongs at the dial, not at the earpiece — it stops a **new** call and never the consumption of one already paid for; the weak path sets `picErr` from the stand-down for the same reason. Suite `verify-quota` (H's own shape, forced: `effScore` 183, `sureLines` false, `textLike` false, Qwen answering 403 with Bailian's own body, DeepSeek answering `bad` — the record carrying the provider's words, `N.early.ok` false, the log NOT claiming the answer was used and saying what happened instead, no card, the gate naming the text check, the photo kept with Crop, the row's new sentence, the error log, a vouching text check still making its card, the German sentence, and **one picture call for three photos**) — **ALL OK on v472, 10 of its 14 checks fail on v471**, where the card comes out as 癌本1本工地，站上 | 示兴牛示人诈吴 | … flagged, with the whole photo. **The audit's own sweeps, and what they found.** **Layout: zero overflowing elements at 390 and 360 px over seven screens × ten languages**, where v432 had left three standing findings. Two were real and both are fixed: **the card detail's six buttons overflowed the card** — `.detailacts` is `1fr 1fr`, which is `minmax(auto,1fr)`, and `.btn{white-space:nowrap}` made each track's min-content its own label, so the grid could not shrink (measured +21 px in Indonesian, +6 German, +1 Spanish at 360); it is `minmax(0,1fr)` with a label that may wrap, which is the v427 fault in its grid form — a class written for one shape borrowed by another. And **the owner's Mirror row** ran 6 px past a 360 px screen because the mirror address is one unbreakable token driving its container's min-content: `min-width:0` on the row's own column and `overflow-wrap:anywhere` on the address. (The `.lnk`/`.thumb`/`.tbg` hits the scan reports are the linked row's deliberate horizontal scroller and the tile's clipped blurred fill — the v465 measurement bug, named so it is not chased again.) **The Still-to-test list wraps nowhere again:** v435 claimed "0 lines wrap" and **30 of 174 lines did**, measured in the real box (45 monospace columns at 390 px); 30 entries are shortened and all 116 fit, counted with CJK as two columns — the first count, which used `length`, was itself wrong about the eight entries written as `\uXXXX` escapes. **Code hygiene:** `.shotfoot`, which v470's entry claims it removed and did not; the dead `const foot=""`; and the `shotDone` comment block, which still described the archive at length **and carried a truncated sentence from the v470 merge**. **Wording:** the guide's "Press and hold a card to mark several and delete them together — a photo in the Camera tab the same way" is nearly false since v470/v471 (a photo is on the tab only while it is being worked on), so it names where photos are actually pruned; and More → Your data → Photos said "The cards keep their own picture." while `oldShots` has, since v470, deleted photos that never made a card — it says so now ("Cards made from them keep their own picture. All four share one property — nothing being made and nothing happening — so **one predicate covers every one of them** and no second rule is needed. `shotDone(s)` is now the first three guards alone (`CROP`, the seven in-memory flags, `AUTOQ`) plus `s.id!==S.openShot`; the `byShot` argument is gone from it and from both call sites. **The `S.openShot` pin is not decoration, and the way it nearly shipped broken is the most useful thing in this entry.** The `rest`/`done` split runs *before* `S.openShot` is consulted anywhere, so without a pin a card-less photo whose crop H had just cancelled — exactly the moment he means to tap Crop — would **vanish from the screen while he was looking at it**, which reads as "the app deleted my photo". Driven through the real buttons on the first build, the photo went **1 → 0 on every one of them** — the exact complaint, shipped. Found by the change's own adversarial round, not by the suite. The four one-line grafts: the three cancel sites set `S.openShot=id`, and the archive toggle **clears** it, or one pinned photo lingers after "Hide them" and the hide looks broken. **One ordering is load-bearing and is commented in place:** at `data-autocancel` the pin must be set **before** `cancelAuto`, which renders from inside itself. **The rule it stands for: a guard asserted by setting its own state by hand is not tested — drive the button that is supposed to set it.** The suite drives all four now (and its own "the pin is inert to begin with" case is what makes the other three mean something). **Nothing is deleted, and that is what keeps this clear of v463's own storage measurement:** the photo stays in `S.inbox` and in IndexedDB with its pixels untouched; a hide writes no bytes, and v463's 1.16 MB → 17.26 MB probe forbids moving the photo **into the cards**, not hiding it — the two are unrelated, and `keepPhoto` is never reached. **The counter-argument answered rather than waved away:** the strongest objection is that a hidden photo cannot be pruned, and `oldShots()` (More → Your data → Photos) requires a card, so it never reached these photos anyway. "Hide them" is untouched — no column names cards in it — so the key counts stay flat: **462 a column, ru 491, en 12, no duplicate in any of the ten**, counted from the source (the v371 trap). **The guide needed no change and that was checked rather than assumed** (the v259 rule): no guide sentence anywhere describes the photo list or the archive toggle. No second element, no clip-path, nothing to keep in sync, and **no animation at all** on a screen whose job is to be read. It says *which* word, never whether you know it. **The two states, where a card is listed or opened:** `stateMark(id)` draws a red disc with a cross for one still to learn and a green disc with a check for one ticked off, as inline SVG (the app ships no icon font and no emoji in the UI), and it replaces the bare `.pdot` in the page detail's list of its own texts. - **A Multikarte is swiped like any other open card, and the photo itself takes the stroke (v460, H: "Noch ein Bug. Multicards lassen sich nicht swipen."):** two faults, and the second is the one that made it look completely dead. **(1) The page detail never wired the gesture.** v445 gave the Cards detail its carousel in `renderCardDetail`, and v453's page card renders through `renderPageDetail` instead — a different function that never called `wireSwipe`. v453's own entry recorded it as "a page reached through the Cards list has no swipe"; H found it. The page's body is `pageBodyHTML(d)` now, factored out so the swipe's peer can draw a page neighbour with it exactly as `detailCardHTML` draws an ordinary one, and both detail screens share one options object (`detailSwipe(list,li,main)`) whose `peer` dispatches on `isPage` — the v445 lesson that two copies drift. `makePeer` takes `{html,cls}` so a page arriving from the side gets its own class. The page's body sits in a `.card.bare`, which is what `wireSwipe` looks for and which takes the card's box back off (`background:none;padding:0;box-shadow:none;border-radius:0;text-align:start;max-width:none`) — **measured: the page detail is pixel-identical to v459 in light and dark, 0 of 1 341 600 pixels different.** A first cut without `text-align:start` centred the title and the count line, 13 000 pixels' worth, which is the kind of unasked look change H approved nothing about. **(2) And the whole card refused the stroke anyway, which is the real bug.** `wireSwipe`'s pointerdown has ignored `button,a,input,textarea,.chip` since v414, so a press that begins on a real control is never hijacked — but **the v448 dots are `<button class="region">` and the v453 text rows are `<button class="crow">`**, and on a page detail those two cover essentially the whole card. Measured on the fixture: a stroke starting 40 px or 120 px down (the photo) produced **no peer at all**, one starting on the title at 260 px swiped perfectly. So the only card kind that holds several texts was the one kind whose entire surface was dead. A dot and a row are **content that happens to be a button**, so they leave the exclusion (`button:not(.region):not(.crow)`); a tap still reaches them, since the gesture only takes over past `SW_SLOP` 12 px and eats only its own closing click — **both taps are asserted in the suite** (a dot still opens the v448 lookup sheet with the right text; a row still opens its card with `← Back` to the page). This also un-deadens the same shape on the ordinary card detail, where the linked-photos thumbnails are rows too. Suite `verify-pageswipe` (a seeded deck of a page with two texts between two plain cards: the page renders in a swipeable card; mid-stroke a peer stands beside it carrying a neighbour's own text; the swipe commits and leaves no peer; **a page arriving as the neighbour carries the `bare` class and shows its title, not an empty card**; the page keeps its texts, its dots and its buttons; and the two taps) — **ALL OK on v460, six of its twelve checks fail on v459.** The pagefront, page, photomode and privacy suites pass on v460. A `WHATS_NEW` line, one `TO_TEST` line. **The harness's own note (the v419/v437 shape):** `verify-photomode` times out at its line 94 whenever its seed's `seenVer` is below `APP_V` — the v416 update note rises above the tab bar and covers the 7 × 4 px test region — so its seed is at 460 here; that is the suite's, not the app's. Not yet field-checked — H swiping one of his page cards is the check: does the next card come in under his thumb from anywhere on the photo, and does a tap on a dot still open its sheet?
- **One true story about what leaves the phone (v459, H after the contradiction audit: "Go with 1, 2, 4 und 5"):** the app told **three different stories** about the same fact and two of them were false. About was right since v409 ("a picture of the text — sometimes the whole photo"); More → AI review and the guide both still said "**the framed area of a photo only when the reading is weak**" — false since v302 (`picOnBad` fires at any reader score), since v439 (the picture leaves at the **quick look**, before the reading proper) and since v348/v393/v450/v453 (the whole photo goes out on several paths) — and `privacy.html` said weak-only in two places and "in those two cases" in a third where there are more. **The same sentence was also wrong about which cards go:** it named "flagged, doubtful or pending cards" while Check-up, Translate all and Tag all send **every** card, and it omitted `gloss` and `alt` from the payload — both flagged as open at v409 and never fixed. **Both app strings are rewritten and translated into all nine columns**, reusing v409's own wording so About, the row and the guide now say the same thing in the same words: "What is sent: a card's Chinese text, pinyin, meaning, your note and the reader's other guesses — for every new card, and for every card when you tap Check-up, Translate all or Tag all. When the reading is hard, a picture of the text goes to a provider that takes pictures — sometimes the whole photo. …" and the guide's "…and, when the reading is hard, a picture of the text — sometimes the whole photo." **`privacy.html` is corrected in eight places** (the date; the intro; the first bullet's "two exceptions"; the usage bullet, which now names the second row sent on leaving the app after a card changed and completes the field list against `reportData` — `first`, `pics`, the per-model work counts and the month figures; the AI bullet, which names the gloss, the other readings, the four buttons that send card text **because you pressed them**, and the fact that **an interrupted Check-up / Translate all / Tag all run resumes by itself**; the picture bullet, rewritten around the quick-look timing and the whole-photo cases; and the deletion paragraph, rewritten for the world after v458 and naming Start over as the owner's tool it actually is). **The translations were produced per language against each column's own vocabulary and checked, not translated once and copied:** every column reuses its existing v409 key word for word where it says the same thing, each uses its own real button labels (verified to exist: de „Check-up“, fr « Bilan », es «Revisión», ja 見直し, ko 점검, ru «Проверка карточек», vi Rà soát, th ตรวจเช็ก, id Cek berkala), each keeps its own dash convention (de the en dash, which it uses 42× against 14×; fr and es the em dash), and **the v409 quantifier trap was checked mechanically**: no column smuggles nur/seulement/solo/だけ/만/только/chỉ/เท่านั้น/hanya into the photo clause, and the ones that remain render the English's own "only a count" and "nowhere else". Thai carries no sentence-final politeness particle (the standing rule, since the app cannot know the user's gender) and its longest unspaced run is 56 characters against the column's existing 74. **Measured:** 458 keys a column and 487 for Russian, **byte-identical to main** — the patch replaced two keys per column and added none —, **no duplicate key in any of the ten columns**, no placeholder invented. Layout over **10 languages × 390 and 360 px**: the row's own sentence never overflows, the guide never overflows, the document width never exceeds the viewport, and the count of overflowing elements on More is **identical to the v458 baseline at every language and width** (0 at 390 except the known German and French admin-login row, 2–3 at 360 including English — the structural row recorded since v401, not this change). What it costs: the AI row is 39–118 px taller depending on the language, since the sentence is longer and true. Suite `verify-privacy` (privacy.html: every one of the five false claims gone, the whole-photo cases named, the quick-look timing, the four buttons, the resume, the gloss and the other readings, the second daily row, Start over as it is after v458, the date; the app: the new row sentence and the new guide sentence in English, the old ones gone, About agreeing, and the German row and guide translated rather than falling back to English) — ALL OK on v459. The reset, multicard and finekeep suites pass on v459. A `WHATS_NEW` line, one `TO_TEST` line. **Named, not built then, both built as v476:** the AI-review switch does **not** stop card text — `resumeTranslate`, `resumeTagAll` and `resumeRecheck` gate on `aiOn()`, not on the switch, and boot, `online` and every return to the foreground run them, so an interrupted bulk run sends card text with no tap while the switch is off (the page now says so; making the switch mean it is a one-line change); and **`aiRelay` is read in two places and written nowhere**, so nobody can switch the relay off short of hand-editing IndexedDB, which is why the page must not tell a reader to turn it off. The guide's other privacy sentence still says the usage row goes "once a day" without the second row — left, since correcting it is another ten columns for a small gain. Not yet field-checked — H reading More → AI review and the guide on his phone is the check: does the longer sentence still read well, and is it honest enough to paste into the Play Data Safety form?
- **"Start over — Delete everything" now deletes everything (v458, H after the contradiction audit: "Go with 1, 2, 4 und 5"):** `resetAll` cleared the three IndexedDB stores and never touched `settings`, and the audit **measured what that left behind on a seeded phone: seven settings still holding Chinese read off the user's photos** — `ailog`, `errlog`, `lastRun`, `readlog`, `recheckRun`, `tagStage`, `translateStage` — **and a Progress dashboard still showing a four-day streak and two busy days over an empty deck.** The sheet has promised "All progress, cards and inbox photos" since v82 and delivered two of the three. `RESET_KEYS` names fourteen keys now (**fifteen since v512 added `charWrites`**), in three groups: **the app's own logs**, which carry the photos' own characters (`ailog` — the last three AI exchanges, the request up to `AI_LOG_REQ` and the raw reply up to `AI_LOG_RES`; `readlog` — the steps and the `numsRing`, which keeps the model's `zh` per reading; `errlog` — **unredacted**, since `noHan` runs only on the way to the daily row); **everything keyed by a card id**, which since v118 **is** the card's text while it is free (`lastRun`, `translateStage`, `tagStage`, `recheckRun`, `translateRun`, `tagRun`, `resumeView`, `autoQueue`); and **the two progress settings More → Progress actually reads** — `days` the streak and `daily` the 30-day strip — plus `lastExport`, which after a wipe should say "never". **What survives, each for its own reason, and an independent design review earned three of these:** the API keys and the provider choice (v172 exists because a key was lost once); **`aiAuto`, `aiPicture` and `aiRelay`, because all three are `!==false` defaults — deleting them would silently switch the AI review and the picture path back ON, and a privacy wipe that re-enables privacy switches is indefensible**; `installId` **and `usage`**, the owner's own continuous series (v220's "one line per browser storage" — a new id forks it; and `usage` carries no card content and has not been read by a learner-facing screen since v274, which the probe confirms: after a reset with `usage` intact, Cards learned and Reviews this week both read 0, and only the streak was wrong); `nmt`, whose 50 MB live in a cache this does not touch, so deleting the flag would make the row lie over files that are still there; `mirror`, the only update path without a VPN; and `brightPass`/`recutPass`/`recutStat`, which hold nothing and whose pass may be running at that moment and would write them straight back. **The defect inside the fix, and it is the interesting half:** deleting the keys was not enough — the first measurement came back with `usage` intact, 310 reviews and all, because `bump`, `bumpModel` and `dailyBump` each **close over the object they are about to write** and fire on a 500 ms debounce, and `saveReadLog`/`saveAiLog` would have re-created their key as an empty husk 800 ms later. All four timers are cleared first. The in-memory side goes with it (`ERRLOG`, `READLOG`, `AILOG`, `AUTOQ`, `LAST_READ`, `NUMSOF`, `TRANSLATE`, `TAGALL`, `RECHECK`), or the next debounced save writes the old arrays back. **And a refused clear no longer paints an empty deck over data that is still there:** the three store clears sat in one empty catch with the in-memory wipe and `render()` unconditional after it, so a clear a second tab blocked left the user looking at an empty app whose data was intact; the failure is caught, named in the error log, and the sheet says "Nothing was deleted — close the app's other tabs and try again." in the owner's English (Reset is behind the admin gate, so this row is H's alone — `openDB` has no `onblocked` handler, which is the likely cause and its own PR). **No `WHATS_NEW` line, and that is the v408 rule doing its job: Reset is inside `${S.admin? … }` — a learner cannot reach it at all**, which also makes `privacy.html`'s "wipe everything under More → Start over" false a second way, for v459 to fix. The sheet's own three strings stay as they are and stay translated, which is a pre-existing inconsistency with the owner-English rule and not this PR's to change. **Measured on a seeded phone (two cards, a progress row, an inbox photo, a four-day streak, two days in the strip, 310 reviews, and all seven leaky settings filled with Chinese): after the reset and a reload, 0 settings hold Chinese, the streak is 0, the strip is gone, and the keys, the installation id, the language and `usage` are still there.** Suite `verify-reset` — **ALL OK on v458, and five of its ten checks fail on v457** with the five that must not move passing on both. The multicard, finekeep, checkfail and page suites pass on v458. One `TO_TEST` line. **Named, not built: `aiRelay` is read at two places and written nowhere — there is no way for anyone to switch the relay off short of hand-editing IndexedDB**, which is why `privacy.html` must not tell a reader to turn it off. Not yet field-checked — H tapping Start over once is the check: Progress at zero afterwards, and Diagnostics with an empty AI log.
- **A "Multikarte" no longer depends on how well the reader read the photo (v457, H after the contradiction audit: "Go with 1, 2, 4 und 5"; his rule, twice: "Immer wenn auf dem Foto mehr als ein zusammenhängender Wortstring auftaucht, wird die Karte als Multikarte behandelt mit den Punkten drauf" and "wenn diese Cluster quasi als getrennte Cluster erkennt werden können, dann ist es eine Multikarte"):** the app could not do that, and the audit measured it. A page card needs `pic.labels`; `labels` come only from a picture answer; a picture answer was asked for only when the quick look's `textLike` failed (v439), the reading ended weak (v173) or the text check said `bad` (v302); and `picPanel` then refused a parked answer whenever `sureLines` was true. **Measured on one synthetic directory board — a big name over four shop plates — driven through the real pipeline three times with the same mocked Qwen answer, changing only the reader's verdict: quick look likes it, reading strong and sure → 0 calls, 1 card, no page; quick look fails, reading strong and sure → 1 call, the answer DISCARDED, 1 card, no page; quick look fails, reading strong but not sure → 1 call, 4 cards and a page.** Two changes, in that order of importance. **(1) A parked panel answer is used even when the reading was read surely — and the guard that replaces `sureLines` is narrower and right.** `sureLines` was doing the v143 rule's job by proxy, but v143 is about the *text* of a card and a panel answer is about its *segmentation*. What the guard actually protects on this path is one thing: `signAskAI` replaces `sg.lines` with the model's `zh` and `splitCards` then builds the cards from `sg.ai.labels` **alone**, so a line the reader read at 99 % that the model did not list is not merged — it is **gone**. `panelCovers(pic,lines)` asks exactly that and nothing else: a multiset of the CJK characters and digits of `pic.zh` and every label's `zh`, and every line of the reading must be covered to `PANEL_COVER` 0.8. A multiset rather than a per-label `hitCore`, since a panel row the reader read as one line (混合快速单脱水) has to match three labels of three characters each and `hitCore` refuses any pair whose lengths differ by more than one; order-free, so reading order cannot cost a card; digits count, since a number belongs to its line (v323). **A first cut compared the counts instead (`labels.length > lines.length`) and an independent design review broke it: a board whose model lists four plates without the headline would have passed that test and lost the headline for good.** The suite carries that case (`uncovered`). **This half costs no extra AI call at all** — it consumes one the quick look already sent and v447 already paid for. **(2) The early call fires on a photo whose text stands in several separated blocks, however cleanly it read.** The signal is the **ink**, not the reader: `textRegion` already walks the photo's text-like rows on a 360 px chromaticity copy and threw the gaps away; it now also returns `blocks`, the number of row runs separated by more than `MULTI_GAP` 1.2 of one line's height, and `several` is `blocks >= MULTI_BLOCKS` 2. **It had to be the ink, and that was measured rather than assumed:** on the board fixture the quick look reads the big name and **misses every plate** (`readB` 1 against `inkB` 5), so the reader's own lines can never answer this question. The reader's blocks are kept as a second route (`Math.max(inkB,readB)`). **v319's rejection of "ask the AI on every photo" stands and is tested:** a one-line sign and a two-line sign both measure **one block and cost no picture call**, on both trees. The v442 reading-stop is explicitly **not** armed on this trigger (`ok` in its guard): there the quick look *liked* the reading, so cutting the passes short would lower `effScore`, turn a good reading weak and hand the card to the model — the opposite of the point. **What it costs, named:** a clean-reading photo whose text stands in two or more blocks — a poster with a separated credit line, a sign with a plate beside it — now spends one picture call whose answer will say `apart:false` and go unused; v439 measured that 33 of 40 photos already send the picture, so the ceiling on this is the other 7, about +21 %. A photo of that kind also now has its framed area leave the device where it did not before, which is the v173 promise widening — **v458 makes the app say so** (task 4 of the same "Go"). And on a surely-read photo the v441 provisional card can now be replaced by a page, which is a flicker H will see. **And `EARLY` is cleared when a reading is abandoned** (`abandonReading`): v439 deleted it only where a finished reading hands it to `SIGN`, so Cancel on the scanning row, the v437 Crop or a frame the hand moved kept the crop and its straightened copy alive for the whole session — and v457 fires that call on more photos. Cancel still cannot un-send: by the time the button is tapped the picture has usually gone. `N.qk` carries `blocks`, `inkB`, `readB` and `several`, `N.prop.blocks` the ink's own count and `N.panel` `{labels,sure,covers,lines,used}` (the v399 rule), and both decisions have their own log line. Suite `verify-multicard` (one board drawn as a name over four plates, one 坚果供应 sign, one two-line sign: a clean-reading board asks the model with the block line and becomes a page of its four plates; a surely-read board uses the parked answer with the coverage line; **a one-line sign and a two-line sign measure one block and ask nothing**; a panel answer that drops a surely-read line is refused with its own line; the ink found blocks the reader could not) — **ALL OK on v457, five of its eight checks fail on v456 and the three that must not move pass on both.** The finekeep, checkfail, page, photomode, shared, waiting, snapkeep and pagefront suites pass on v457. A `WHATS_NEW` line, two `TO_TEST` lines. **The bound, stated: no real photo fixture survives in this scratchpad, so the block count is measured on synthetic boards and signs and on H's recorded answers, never on his own pixels** (the v386 rule — and this is a rule about *whether to ask the model*, where a wrong answer costs one call and never a wrong card, not a placement heuristic). `PANEL_COVER` 0.8 is unfitted for the same reason; `N.panel` is what settles it. Not yet field-checked — H's 798 directory board and his Meituan screen taken again are the check: one page card each, with the dots; and a plain shop sign still making one card with no picture call in its diagnostics.
- **The small plates of a board are not fine print, and the app stops deleting what the prompt just asked for (v456, H after the contradiction audit: "Go with 1, 2, 4 und 5"):** v455 told the model that on a board, a directory, a menu, a panel or a screen the small plates under a big headline belong in the answer — and `mainLines`, the v312 safety net, then deleted them again. It drops every line whose box is under `FINE_PRINT` a third of the tallest line's height from `zh`, `p` and `m`, it takes no `apart` argument, and it is called at `aiReadPicture`'s head **before** `apart` is even computed. On H's 龙人居 notice board that rule dropped **five of seven answered lines** (`drop` in his own record). So the prompt and the code were asking for opposite things about the same field, and the code won silently. **What decides now:** `apart` is computed above the filter and `mainLines` takes `keepAll` — `apart===true` (what the prompt already promises: "when \"apart\" is true … none of them counts as fine print"), **or** the model's own `kind` being one of `FINE_KEEP` — **Menu, App, Appliance, Transport, Office**, the five of the nine `KINDS` that *are* the prompt's own list ("a board, a directory, a menu, a panel or a screen"): a menu's dishes, an app screen's rows, an appliance's sub-labels (the v358 长按童锁 rule says so already), a station board's lines, a form's field labels. **Street sign, Shop, Product and Notice keep the filter**, because that is where a poster's credits, a date line and a package's small print live — v312's own case is a poster. `keepAll` returns the lines with their boxes intact and leaves `box` as the model's own union, so the frame spans the whole board, nothing lands in `snapBox`'s skip list (`droppedBoxes` stays empty) and the reader's label search gets the full region; `mainAlt`, the second reading of a box that passes the picture's edge (v340), takes the same flag. The log says "the small lines of this answer are elements, not fine print (kind Menu) — none of them is left out" and `N.pic.keptAll` carries `apart` or `kind Menu` (the v399 rule), so the field can tell which clause fired. **Where it actually changes a card:** on a successful split the cards come from `labels`, which the v312 rule never touched — so this bites exactly where the split *refuses* (`SPLIT_MAX` 30, a drawing whose reader found nothing, a frame the hand drew), and there `zh` **is** the one card's text. That is H's own case: a board of twelve plates that answers `apart:false` used to make one card saying only the mall's name. **What it costs, named:** a poster the model wrongly calls `apart:true`, or wrongly tags Menu, keeps its credits on the card and its frame spans them — the v312 complaint back, for that one answer. Suite `verify-finekeep` (one synthetic board — a 60 px name over four 16 px plates, i.e. plates at 0.27 of the tallest — answered five ways: `kind:"Menu"` keeps all four plates with the log line and `keptAll` "kind Menu" and the one card carrying every plate; `kind:"App"` the same; `apart:true` keeps them whatever the kind; **`kind:"Shop"` still drops all four and a poster still loses its credit line** — the v312 case, unchanged; one picture call in every case; no page error) — **ALL OK on v456, and the five `[flips]` checks fail on v455 with the four controls passing on both** (the v419 rule). The checkfail, page, photomode, waiting, prompt and shared suites pass on v456. A `WHATS_NEW` line, one `TO_TEST` line. **Unmeasurable here, and stated rather than dressed up: the sandbox cannot reach Qwen (the v405 rule), so no harness run can say whether v455 makes H's board answer `apart:true` in the first place** — this version only guarantees that when the model does name the plates, the app keeps them. Not yet field-checked — H's 798 directory board taken again is the check: every plate on the card, and `keptAll` in the diagnostics saying which clause kept them.
- **Small text on a board is not fine print, and the model no longer decides `apart` by the size of the characters (v455, H, 2026-09-13, three photos from the 798 art district with a full Diagnostics dump: "Der Multi Mode funktioniert leider meistens noch nicht. Und wenn er funktioniert, dann sind die Punkte oft an der falschen Stelle."):** the ring of v405 held all three readings, so the first half is diagnosed from his own record without the photos, and it is **not** a placement failure — **Qwen answered `apart:false` on all three**, so the split never ran and each photo made one card. What the three answers say, and two of them accuse the prompt in their own words: the **深夜食街 mall directory** — a board of some twelve brand plates under its own big name — came back with `"zh":"深夜食街\n新辰里"`, two lines, and a note reading "A directory sign showing various brands and the name of the shopping complex below": the model **saw** the plates, described them, and left every one of them out; the **蛙厂 poster and sign** came back `apart:false` with the note "The text appears on two separate signs: a grey vertical sign at the top and a large white poster below it" — the note contradicts the flag; and the **龙人居 notice board** answered seven lines of which the app's own v312 fine-print rule then dropped five (`drop` in the record). **The mechanism is the prompt fighting itself.** The `"zh"` clause says, unconditionally, to leave out fine print — "lines whose characters are under a third the height of the largest characters" (v312, for a poster's credits) — and a directory's plates, a menu's dishes and a panel's sub-labels are all exactly that beside their own headline; the model builds `"zh"` first, drops them, and then sees one text and answers `apart:false`. The v449 sentence that was meant to stop this ("every Chinese text on the picture is an element, not only the main items … leave nothing out") sits **inside the `"labels"` clause, which only applies once `apart` is already true**, so it could never reach the decision. Three clauses now: small text is **not** fine print when it is an element of its own — on a board, a directory, a menu, a panel or a screen the small plates, rows, brand names and buttons under a big headline belong in the answer; **"decide `apart` from what the picture shows, never from the size of the text"**, naming the directory whose own name is large and whose plates are small, and two signs standing apart in one photo (a banner over a doorway and a sign on the wall behind it — the 来局 shape v449 filed as a special case, now come back twice); and, earned by H's own two notes, **if what you would write in `"note"` is that the texts stand on separate signs, plates, boards or screens, then `apart` is true**. The prompt goes 6 502 → 7 206 characters, and its fingerprint (v399) lists v455. **Unmeasurable here, and it is stated rather than dressed up: the sandbox cannot reach Qwen (the v405 rule), so no harness run can show whether the model obeys** — H's next directory board is the measurement. The v312 rule itself is untouched, so a poster's credits still leave the card. **And the same record shows the v453 album tell misfiring on every one of the three:** all three are camera photos of a street, all carry `src.cam:""` (no EXIF Make/Model) and `dims:false`, and all three were therefore filed as screenshots and read whole — the cost v453 named ("a camera photo whose EXIF an app stripped on the way"), occurring not once but on three of three. **It changed nothing here** — the ink rows had proposed the whole photo anyway on all three (`reg` [0,0,1,1], [0,0.084,1,1], [0,0,1,1]) — so it is recorded and not acted on; if a field record ever shows a band the whole-image rule threw away, the second tell (the pixels being the screen's own size) is what the rule should require. **The second half of H's complaint — the dots in the wrong place — could not be diagnosed and nothing was built for it:** his two screenshots show a 798 directory board as a page with its dots scattered over the brick wall beside the plates, and a vending-machine photo whose one visible dot sits on the wall, and **neither photo's record is in the ring any more** (it holds three readings and three newer ones had pushed them out). The v415 shape: the first thing to say, and the check is the same board taken again with Diagnostics **right after**, or the photo file itself (the v386 rule — five versions of guessing ended the day H sent the washing machine). Suite `verify-prompt` (the three clauses once each, the v312 and v449 clauses still there, the rendered length the fingerprint claims, no page error) — **ALL OK on v455, five of its eight checks fail on v454**; the page, photomode (seed at 455), checkfail and waiting suites pass on v455. A `WHATS_NEW` line, one `TO_TEST` line. Not yet field-checked — the 798 directory board and the 蛙厂 signs taken again are the check: several cards, and the dots' own record in the diagnostics.
- **A batch from the album goes on after the first photo, and the photos still in the queue say so (v454, H, 2026-09-13: "Wenn ich mehrere Fotos auf einmal aus Pictures hochlade, dann sollte bei den Fotos, die noch in der Warteschlange sind, bitte Waiting... oder so stehen. Sonst denkt man, dass sich die App verschluckt hat und gar nix passiert."):** two things, and the second was found by the suite written for the first. **(1) The line.** A photo of the batch still in `AUTOQ` — queued, not yet reading — shows one quiet line in its own row's box, **"Waiting for its turn …"** (`renderShots`, the `.badge` look of the frame's own hint, no bar and no shimmer: nothing is happening to this photo yet, and the `.batchline` above already says how many are to go and that the app has to stay open, v411/v412). The same shopfront one minute later (shot_822, 小厨娘淮扬菜, six characters 1440 × 240, six squares) snapped to 1422 × 218 and was right — the A/B pair the fix is measured on, both byte-exact from the phone. **The rule:** a single-line box whose width is its height times its own character count (`|w/h − k| ≤ SNAP_SQUARE` 0.25 k) is a measurement, not a guess — the characters ARE its height —, so when the snap keeps under `SNAP_KEEP` 0.65 of that height it has found something other than the line (fine print under it, a bright patch, a sub-line) and **the AI's box stays**; the log says "the AI's box is 9 characters wide and one character tall, so it was measured, not guessed — the snap kept 51 % of its height: the AI's box stays" and `N.snapKept` carries the ratio. It runs in `cropSign` **after** the v324/v326 `beyond` bands have joined, on the box as it stands. **The two tests are coupled on purpose:** a box taller than one line of k characters fails the first, so the second can only fire where the height is the character height. **The width is deliberately not tested**, and the reason is a field-confirmed case: H's 业主直租 sign (v305) legitimately loses 40 % of its width when the snap drops the QR code standing in the line's own band, and its box (four characters plus a square code, w/h ≈ 5 against k 4) passes the consistency test — a width rule would have put the code back. **The failure mode this accepts is a crop with room around the text, never one that cuts it** (v380's rule). (`regionLine`, one key in ten columns; a marked photo has two cards at least, so the plural is always right). The v358 list "11 cards from this photo" with a card each under a freshly split photo is gone — the photo itself carries them (D2 of the spec). **A photo that made one card is untouched:** the finished card of v325, the switch being the split's own (`REGION_MIN` 2 = `SPLIT_MIN`), so the shop-sign flow H approved does not move. **The tap opens a sheet over the photo** (`openLookup`, `.ask.lookup` + `.sheet.lookup` — the v222 sheet **without the scrim and not modal**: the page keeps scrolling and the next dot can be tapped while it stands, which swaps the content in place; a tap anywhere else, the ×, or Escape closes it, `closeLookup`): the characters in the Hanzi font (the traditional form with its pill when the card has one), the pinyin with the speaker, the meaning with the language pill, the **three grade tiles** of v421 (`data-g` for the colours, `data-lg` for the wiring — a first cut had `data-lg` alone and the screenshot showed three grey tiles), and **More**, the existing key, which opens the card detail with **← Back** (`S.detailFrom="inbox"`, `backToPhoto`, `INBOX_SCROLL`) and Delete card there returns to the photo too; a tab tap clears `detailFrom`. No picture in the sheet — the photo is right there. **The grade is the decision (H):** `gradeRegion` writes the review through **`recordGrade`** — the schedule, the leech flag, the streak's day and the day's count, factored out of Learn's `grade()` so both write the same way — counts it as a review, and the dot takes the card's colour at once; a sheet closed without a grade writes nothing (`regionTaps` and `regionGrades` in `usage` and the daily row say how often a lookup becomes a grade; `privacy.html` names them). In phase 1 every region is a card already, so the grade only grades; in phase 2 it makes the card first. **A tap beside a small region still opens it:** the `.regions` container resolves a tap that missed every region to the nearest one whose box, grown to `REGION_HIT` 44 px around its centre, holds the point (measured: a 7 × 4 px region opens from 14 px beside it). **Regions are derived from the cards at render time and nothing is written to the photo record** — a put of an inbox record rewrites its Blob, and 237 photos at boot would be some 70 MB of writes for data the cards already carry; phase 2 stores the model's own regions on the record, since a text without a card has no other home. What it costs: one Map of cards by photo per inbox render (measured: 200 marked photos with 1 003 regions render in 56 ms, 56 fps after a scroll to the end), and a grade given on the photo does not touch the Learn session's queue — a card graded Easy there that was already in today's queue comes up once more in Learn (named, not fixed). The cause is one reference height: the join's width cap is `ow>RL_SIDEW*h` with `h=c.y1-c.y0`, and `cut[j]` has **already** been extended upward by the v392 pictogram join by the time that block runs, so `h` is the label-plus-icon height and the cap admits a whole three-character neighbour whose run the reader failed to name. It is measured against the label's own **character** height since (`rowBand[rowIx[j]]`, falling back to the picked run's height); two constants unchanged, one derived value swapped. **And one more fault, older than v396, that `roundGrid` exposed:** the per-label fallback picture at the split's last gate was `PLACED[id]||seenBase` — the *snapped* frame, trimmed by `snapBox` to the ink the search found, which by construction omits exactly the labels the search missed. It is `seenBase` there now, the frame the AI actually read the text from. **Line 4503 must not be touched** — that is v380's `splitWhole` path, field-confirmed on H's washing machine, and no suite reaches it; changing both lines makes every fallback the whole photo at 5.9× the area. On `oven-bottom` this is the difference between five cards of **blank oven-door glass** and ①吐司 ②牛排 ③全鸡 ④鸡翅 ⑤大虾. Measured, cards / on their own label / honest whole-photo / **neighbour carries**: `oven-top` v397 6/3/0/0, v396 6/4/0/**4**, v398 6/4/2/**0**; `oven-touch` v397 6/1/0/**1**, v396 6/6/0/**20**, v398 6/2/4/**0**; `oven-bottom` v397 5/**0**/0/0, v396 5/4/0/0, v398 5/4/0/0; `dish-lower` 5/5/0/0 on all three; H's washer with his verbatim answer 13 placed / **0** carries on v397 and v398, 13/**1** on v396. **`DIAL_PITCH` is inert on every fixture in existence** (the candidate with the gate removed gives identical frames on all four panels and the washer) — it ships on H's word and its field case, the oven's "five cards, each a quarter of the panel", does not reproduce in the harness. **`picW` cannot be exercised here either**: its whole reason is H's dishwasher reading at 1637 px against an 800 px picture, a non-integer ratio that destroys roundness, and the harness's ratio is exactly 2, so the change is inert. Only H's own dishwasher answer in the AI log can show it firing. **Measured and dropped, do not attempt again without the named test:** the camera hunt's A/B split of the five changes (PR-A green everywhere, PR-B carrying the whole regression, so landing A alone silently arms B); deleting the vertical-overlap line in the free-standing-element block (all three skeptics broke it — shrinking a corridor moves its midpoint toward the label and flips the centring and occupancy tests *reject → accept*, handing 混合 a 29 %-wide slab carrying 快速, 袜子 and 洗衣液); sloped bands in `labelRunsOf` (the estimator fits +0.010 where the truth is −0.052, wrong sign, and with the true slope forced in the result is unchanged — it is contrast, not alignment); lowering `labelRunsOf`'s ink threshold from 0.15 (recovers 蛋糕, loses 烤鱼, regresses the washer 13 → 11).
- **PWA:** installed and verified on the Xiaomi; runs offline (SW cache-first); `navigator.storage.persist()` granted. **Versioning:** SW cache `zt-vN` in `sw.js` and the label `PWA vN` in `index.html` (`.ver` — **hidden since v225**, H's "Go" on the design review: a developer's line, not a user's; it stays in the page because the shell check, the mirror update and About read it, and More → About shows "PWA vN." to the user) move in lockstep — bump both on **every** change to cached files. The app updates itself (update check on load/foreground, auto-reload on `controllerchange` — deferred to the next foreground while the app is in use since v279); the worker's install fetches the shell with `cache:"reload"` — GitHub Pages sends `max-age=600`, and after two deploys within ten minutes a new worker once filled its cache with the previous shell (the phone showed the v70 page with the v69 script: header v70, no drag in the sheet). **Boot self-check** (`shellCheck`): `APP_V` in `app.js` must equal the `PWA vN` label — **bump both, plus `zt-vN`, on every change**; if they differ, the page posts `refresh` to the worker, which refills its cache from the server (`cache:"reload"`) and the page reloads once (through `reloadSoon` since v279, see below; guard: at most once per 10 min, setting `shellFixAt`); it runs after registration and on the first `controllerchange`; the vendor cache `zt-ocr-v1` survives shell updates — bump it only when vendor files change.
- **The reload after an update waits until the app is idle (v279, H after eight builds in two hours: "nach Laden eines neuen Builds flackert die App … Passiert das nach jedem Update auch bei den Usern?" → the answer: one reload per update, two with a mixed shell; the flicker was the pace of the deploys → "Go" on the deferral):** until v278 the page reloaded the moment the new worker took over, in the middle of whatever H was doing. Now `reloadSoon()` decides: within `RELOAD_GRACE` 3 s of the load (the app was just opened, the first screen is up) or while the app is in the background the page reloads at once, as before; later `RELOAD_DUE` is set and the reload comes when the app next comes to the foreground (`visibilitychange`). The same for the shell check's "refreshed" reload and the hourly mirror check's "updated"; a tap on the mirror row's **Check now** still reloads at once (`MIRROR.forced`) — the user asked for it. The old page keeps running meanwhile with the new worker's cache, which is harmless (the vendor cache is separate, the page's own files are already loaded). Suite `verify-reload` (a synthetic `controllerchange` in the first seconds reloads at once, one after the grace leaves the page with `RELOAD_DUE`, a hide changes nothing, the return to the foreground reloads, an update while hidden reloads at once); the shell and english suites pass. **The mirror suite fails in this session on both v278 and v279** with "The mirror is not reachable: Failed to fetch" from the worker's fetch of the suite's fake mirror — a sandbox or harness problem, not the app (the shell suite, which uses the same reload path, passes). Not yet field-checked — the next update after v279 is the check: H should see no reload while using the app, and the new version on the next return to the foreground or the next open. **Never while a photo is on its way from the camera (v316, H right after the v315 update: "Ich habe gerade ein Foto gemacht und bin danach direkt auf der Learn Seite gelandet. Foto ist weg. Warum?" — Diagnostics at v315 with the previous reading's log restored from the setting and no line for the new photo):** the camera app in front is the page hidden, the new worker took over meanwhile, `reloadSoon` reloaded the hidden page at once, and the camera handed its photo to a page that was gone — the file input's change never reached the app, the photo never reached the inbox. (The v279 rule also reloads on the return to the foreground, which comes before the change event; the same loss.) Now `PICKING` is set by the tap on Take photo or From album and cleared by the input's `change` or `cancel` (at most `PICK_MAX` ten minutes), and `reloadBusy()` = `picking()` or a frame standing (`CROP`, the photo open in crop mode, Crop again too): `reloadSoon` only sets `RELOAD_DUE` then, hidden or not, and the return to the foreground reloads only when neither holds — so the reload comes with the next foreground after the photo is saved or cancelled. Suite `verify-reload` (Take photo tapped arms the flag; headless Chromium then fires the input's `cancel` at once, since no dialog opens, so the case arms the flag again by hand — a worker change while hidden: no reload, `RELOAD_DUE` set; the return to the foreground: no reload; the photo landing in crop mode: a hide and return still no reload; the frame gone: the next return reloads); the english suite passes. Not yet field-checked — the next update taken through the camera is the check. What it cannot do: bring the lost photo back, and a page Android discards while the camera runs (memory) reloads all the same and loses the photo as well — that is the system's, not the update's. **The reload comes at the next pause, on the same screen, and the mirror is fresh within minutes (v327, H: "make sure that new software versions always load automatically without the need for manual refresh"):** three faults kept an update from showing by itself. A reload deferred past the 3 s grace waited for the next return to the foreground, so an update that arrived while H used the app (the worker's install takes a few seconds, longer than the grace) showed only after leaving and reopening the app. The mirror was asked at most once an hour. And jsDelivr keeps its own copy of a branch's files for hours, so a phone without a VPN saw a new version late even when it asked. Now: **(1) the idle reload** — once a reload is due, every `RELOAD_POLL` 2 s the page asks `reloadIdle()`: no finger for `IDLE_MS` 4 s (`LAST_TOUCH` from pointerdown, keydown, input, touchstart, wheel), the page visible, no photo on its way and no frame (`reloadBusy`, v316), no Edit or Add form, no reading waiting (`PENDING`, `READING`), no Translate-all run, no sheet or drawing sheet open, nothing typed in the Feedback box — and then `reloadNow()` notes the screen in setting `resumeView` (mode, the open card, the Cards search, the scroll) and reloads; `boot` puts the screen back (within `RESUME_MAX` 3 min; a card that is gone falls back to the list) and drops the setting, so the reload is a flicker on the same screen. The rules of v279 and v316 stay: within the grace or in the background at once, never while a photo is picked or a frame stands; the return to the foreground reloads as before; the mirror row's Check now reloads at once through `reloadNow` too. **(2) The mirror every ten minutes** (`MIRROR_EVERY`, on start, on foreground and on a timer while the app is open; hourly until v326), and `reg.update()` on the same timer. **(3) The mirror's cache purged on every push to main** — `.github/workflows/purge-mirror.yml` calls `purge.jsdelivr.net` for the shell files (index, app, styles, lang, sw, manifest, signs, nmt-model, privacy); the purge API needs no key; the sandbox cannot reach jsDelivr (403 through the proxy), so whether the purge answers is seen in the repo's Actions tab — **seen 2026-09-12** (H: "Bekommen user app updates ohne VPN?", then "Yes" to the check): 112 runs since v327, every one green, and the v437 run's log shows all nine files answered `"status":"finished"`, `"throttled":false`, both providers `CF` and `FY` true, eleven seconds after the merge — so a phone without a VPN sees a new version within one `MIRROR_EVERY` of the merge, not within jsDelivr's own cache life. The workflow itself never fails (a dead curl only echoes), so its green tick alone proves nothing; the job log is what says it. Still VPN-only, unchanged: a first install when github.io is blocked, `sw.js` itself, the 50 MB model, the Claude provider. What it costs: a reload while H reads a card front without touching it for four seconds — the same card comes back, the session's queue is rebuilt from the deck (a card marked "again" earlier in the session may come later than it would have); a mirror fetch of index.html every ten minutes while the app is open. Suite `verify-reload` (the early reload; a due reload held while the finger taps every second on More, then coming within 4 s of the last touch with More restored at the same scroll and the setting gone; the Cards detail with the search restored; the Add form holding the reload with the finger at rest and the reload after leaving it; an update in the background at once; the v316 pick cases, the standing frame holding through 5 s at rest); the english, shell and autocard suites pass. Not yet field-checked — the next update is the check: it should appear within seconds of a pause, on the screen H was on.
- **No VPN needed to use the app (H's requirement):** the installed app runs from its cache, DeepSeek is reachable from China, and updates also arrive through a **mirror** — More → Updates without a VPN (setting `mirror`, default jsDelivr **`fastly.jsdelivr.net/gh/henglicam/zeichentrainer@main/` since v483** — see the next sentence; `cdn.jsdelivr.net` until v482, **field-verified reachable from H's phone without VPN**, which turned out to be one phone's luck rather than a property of the host). **The default is `fastly.`, not `cdn.` (v483, 2026-09-14):** `cdn.jsdelivr.net` is **DNS-hijacked in mainland China** — it resolves to long-blocked Facebook/Twitter addresses or to nothing at all, reported to hit about **two fifths** of users, with measurements from August 2026 putting it at reachable-but-unstable, TTFB 493–1086 ms ([jsDelivr #18392](https://github.com/jsdelivr/jsdelivr/issues/18392), [21cloudbox](https://www.21cloudbox.com/support/jsdelivr-china.html)); jsDelivr lost its China PoPs and its ICP filing, and the issue tracker has been carrying this for years. A phone in that two fifths gets **neither** github.io **nor** the mirror — no updates, and no reader files on a fresh install —, and the app cannot tell, since a hijacked DNS answer is a dead fetch like any other. `fastly.jsdelivr.net` is jsDelivr's own alternative endpoint, the same paths and the same content, and is not hijacked. **Field-confirmed on H's Xiaomi, 2026-09-14, without a VPN:** the Mirror row read "Up to date. The mirror has v482.", which is the whole path — the worker fetched `index.html` from fastly and parsed the version label out of it. Changed in `MIRROR_DEFAULT` (`app.js`) and in the worker's own pre-`tellMirror` fallback (`sw.js`); `purge-mirror.yml` keeps `purge.jsdelivr.net`, which is the purge API's own host and purges the file across jsDelivr's network rather than per endpoint. **It reaches only phones with no stored `mirror` setting** — `mirrorURL()` is `S.settings.mirror||MIRROR_DEFAULT` — so H's own phone keeps what he typed, and so does anyone who ever edited the field. **What is not measured:** whether `fastly.` stays clear (it is one hostname of a service that has been squeezed in China for years, and the next block would be as silent as this one), and whether a second fallback hop is worth building — falling back to `cdn.` would help nobody, and `gcore.jsdelivr.net` is an untested guess. The real answer is the second origin H has already chosen (Cloudflare Pages, below), which makes the mirror a fallback rather than the only path). The page posts `mirror-update` (with its own version label) to the worker on start/foreground (at most hourly) or on "Check now"; the worker reads `PWA vN` from the mirror's index.html and, if newer, fetches the shell assets into the current cache — content types by extension, because jsDelivr hands HTML out as text/plain — and the page reloads (`mirrorUpdate` in `sw.js`, `mirrorCheck` in `app.js`). **Vendor files come from the mirror too** (H: "text recognition does not work without VPN" — the reader's ~12 MB are fetched on first use, and github.io was unreachable): the worker tries the origin, and on failure or a non-OK answer fetches `MIRROR + vendor/…` (all OCR/dictionary files are under jsDelivr's 20 MB cap; types by extension), caching the result in `zt-ocr-v1`; the page tells the worker the mirror setting on start (`tellMirror`). **A silent origin counts as a failure** (v189, H's phone without the VPN: "Reading the text … still at: loading the reader …" for good — github.io behind the wall answers with nothing, and the fallback waited for an error that never came): a vendor fetch from the origin gets `ORIGIN_WAIT` 6 s, then the mirror takes over, and after one such failure the mirror is asked first for `ORIGIN_DOWN` five minutes (`withTimeout`, `originDownUntil` in `sw.js`); measured: the first file 6 s, the rest milliseconds, the whole reader download 6.6 s against a silent origin. **A page no worker controls reads through the mirror all the same, and asks the worker to take it over (v335, H, 2026-09-08, the Xiaomi without the VPN: "Now he really loads forever!" — Diagnostics `SW no`, the reading at "loading the reader …" for minutes, and `Uncaught Error: TypeError: Failed to fetch @tesseract.min.js:2`):** the v189 rule is the worker's, and without a controlling worker every reader file went straight to github.io, which answers with nothing behind the wall; Tesseract's own fetch of the core or the language file then never settled, and nothing ended the reading. Why the worker had stopped controlling the page is not known (earlier diagnostics the same day said `SW yes` with the same user agent; the registration is not dropped by a failed update, and `sw.js` never unregisters) — Diagnostics say more since: `SW no (registration active)` / `(registration failed: …)` / `(registration none)` (`SW_REG`) and `· reader files from the mirror` when the page chose it. Three things now. **(1) The claim:** once `navigator.serviceWorker.ready` resolves and the page has no controller, the page posts `claim` and the worker calls `clients.claim()` — the page is controlled at once, no reload (the first-controller branch of `controllerchange` runs `tellMirror` and the shell check); a worker that is active but not controlling — a hard reload, a worker that activated while the page was open without claiming — is the state this fixes; a page with no worker at all (a first install behind the wall, a failed registration) gets (2). **(2) The page's own origin-then-mirror rule** (`vendorBase`, `vendorFetch`): with no controller the page asks github.io once per session for `vendor/t2s.txt` with `cache:"no-store"` and `ORIGIN_WAIT` 6 s; silent → the mirror (`mirrorURL()+"vendor/"`) for every reader file, the note "no worker controls the page and github.io did not answer within 6 s — the reader's files come from the mirror" in the error log (so the daily row and All users carry it, v271) and in Diagnostics' head line. Every file the page loads itself goes through `vendorFetch` — the scripts (`loadScript` fetches `./vendor/…` and runs it from a blob URL, with or without the worker), the dictionary, the character tables, the strokes, the Text recognition download —, from the reader's cache `zt-ocr-v1` first when the page has no worker (`caches.match`), and a file fetched past the worker is put into that cache under its origin address, so the worker serves it later and a reload without the worker reads it from the phone. Tesseract's worker and core come as blob URLs from `vendorFetch` (`tessPaths`; the core's URL carries `#core.js`, since the worker only checks that the path ends in "js" — measured: the `.wasm.js` is a single-file build, no separate `.wasm` is fetched), the language file Tesseract fetches itself from the base the probe chose — this build's `initialize` step cannot take the data directly (it joins `data` instead of `code` into the language name; `{code,data}` was tried and failed with "Failed loading language '31,139,…'"), so without the worker 1.7 MB come from the network on every start. **(3) A stalled load ends:** `vendorFetch` reads every body chunk by chunk and ticks (`readerTick`), Tesseract's logger ticks, and `withStall` fails the scripts' load and every `makeWorker` when nothing moved for `READER_STALL` 90 s (a `let`, the harness shortens it) — "the reader did not load within 90 s — no answer from github.io or the mirror" as "Reading failed: …" in the box, the auto card's row says the same instead of "Nothing could be read" (`failPending` takes the message), the error log has it, and the next reading tries again (`_ocrLoading` cleared); the dictionary loads outside the stall race, since it is optional and 2.5 MB. What it costs: a phone without the worker fetches the language file on every start and pays the 6 s probe once per session; a connection under about 20 kB/s on the language file is a stall now. Measured in the harness (no `sw.js`, the origin silent on every vendor file, a jsDelivr-like mirror with real content types): the reader reads 坚果 from the mirror 6.8 s after the call — the probe's one request to github.io, six files from the mirror, five of them in the cache for the worker —, a second worker fetches only the language file, a reload reads everything but the language file from the cache; a mirror silent on the language file ends the load at the stall text after 14 s with `READER_STALL` 8 s and the auto card's row names it; a worker that activates without claiming leaves the page uncontrolled (`controller` null, `reg.active` set) and the claim makes it controlled with the page's variables kept. Chromium's hard reload and its service-worker bypass both keep the controller, so the hard-reload case is not reproducible in the harness. Suite `verify-nosw` (those cases, the Diagnostics head line, the error log's vendor line); the english, twopass, vendor-mirror, vendor-hang, diag, reload, shell and savenow suites pass. Not yet field-checked — H's next photo without the VPN is the check: Diagnostics should say `SW yes` again after one start, or `SW no (registration …)` with the reader's files from the mirror and the reading ending either way. **The worker helps only while it controls the page:** H's diagnostics of the hanging reading said `SW no` with a desktop user agent (no "Mobile") — Chrome's "Desktop site" switch, ticked for the Bailian key page, was on for the app too, and a page without the worker fetches every vendor file straight from github.io. More → **Text recognition** shows how many of the ten reader files are on the phone and offers **Download** (`OCR_FILES`, `renderOcrRow`). The worker script itself only ever comes from github.io (it just carries the cache name). Still VPN-only: a first install if github.io is blocked, the 50 MB model download (jsDelivr caps files at 20 MB), the Claude provider. **The first install is the one thing the mirror cannot fix, and the way out is a second origin (H, 2026-09-12: "Können wir die VPN Pflicht am Anfang bitte umgehen? Müssen komplett VPN-frei auskommen.", then "Ich werde A machen, aber später."):** jsDelivr serves `index.html` as `text/plain` on purpose, so it can never host the page, and a service worker may only come from its own origin — **no code change can remove the VPN from a first install while the origin is github.io.** Two ways out were offered and **H chose A, to be done later**: **A — Cloudflare Pages on a domain of H's own** (the repo hooked up, no build, every merge deploys as today; `*.pages.dev` is DNS-poisoned in China so the domain is required; ~10 €/year and a card). Its side effects are all wanted: the shell and `sw.js` come from an origin reachable without a VPN, the mirror becomes the fallback rather than the only path, GitHub Pages' `max-age=600` and with it the v426 mixed-shell window disappear, and `assetlinks.json` becomes trivial for the Play Store, since the domain root *is* the site root and the separate `henglicam/henglicam.github.io` repo is no longer needed. **B — Supabase Storage as the second origin** (H's project answers without a VPN, a public bucket, an Action uploading the shell on every push; free, no domain, but no directory index — the URL ends in `/index.html` —, a second deploy path, and whether Storage serves HTML inline or as a download is **unmeasured**, a two-minute test in the dashboard). **Both are a second origin, so the IndexedDB is a second deck:** H's cards live under github.io and move by export/import, the share link changes, and github.io stays as the old origin. **The sandbox cannot measure reachability from China for either** — that is H's phone to say; the cheap pre-test before buying a domain is whether `cdnjs.cloudflare.com` loads on his phone without the VPN, since that is Cloudflare's own edge. Nothing is built and nothing may be built here without H's word: the domain purchase and the Cloudflare account are his, and only after they exist do the code changes (`APP_URL`, the share text, the mirror default, the purge workflow) have anything to point at. **VPN-off only: Qwen** (v173 — Bailian answered the phone without the VPN and refused through it).

- **The licences are in the app, not only in the repo (v425, H asked what law the web app already has to keep, then "OK, umsetzen"):** `vendor/LICENSES.txt` has been complete since the vendor files went in, and it was linked **nowhere** — neither `app.js` nor `index.html` nor `privacy.html` named it. Apache-2.0 (Tesseract, its core, both tessdata models, OpenCC), MPL-2.0 (Bergamot), MIT (pinyin-pro), CC BY-SA 4.0 (CC-CEDICT, and the derived `cedict.tsv.gz` is under it too) and the Arphic licence of the stroke medians all ask for the notice to be delivered **with the work**; a file that happens to sit in a public repo is a weak reading of that, and inside a TWA package it is weaker still. More → About now ends in a row **Open source licenses** — "The software and data the app is built on, and who made them." with **Open** (`#lic-open`), which opens `./vendor/LICENSES.txt` in a tab. No new file, no copy of the text to keep in step, and the path goes through the worker's own vendor route (v189), so it comes from the mirror behind the wall and is cached in `zt-ocr-v1` after the first look; it is deliberately **not** in the shell list, as `privacy.html` is not. Two keys in all nine non-English columns ("Open source licenses" and the sentence; "Open" was already there from the guide's row), 443 a column and 471 for Russian with its plural keys, no duplicate in any column. Suite `verify-lic` (the row last in More under the About row and inside the About group, its rounded bottom corners, the title, the sentence and the button, the file reachable at the relative path and naming Apache, CC BY-SA and MPL, the tap opening that address, the German three, no overflow at 390 px); checked by screenshot in light and dark; the static key check reports no key missing that was not missing before. **Two things it is not:** it does not make the licences available offline (an attribution notice has to ship with the distribution, not work without a network), and it is not a `WHATS_NEW` line — a learner notices the row and has no reason to care. **Then all six were actually verified against the upstream texts (same day, H: "Bist du sicher, dass das alles public und kostenlos ist?"), and every one permits commercial sale** — fetched and read: `mozilla/firefox-translations-models/LICENSE` and `browsermt/bergamot-translator/LICENSE` are both MPL-2.0 as claimed; the npm package `cedict-json`, which is where `cedict.tsv.gz` came from, declares `CC-BY-SA-4.0` (mdbg.net itself is blocked by the sandbox's proxy, so the notice is verified at the source actually used, not at MDBG); Make Me a Hanzi's `COPYING` puts `graphics.txt` — the file the stroke medians come from — under the Arphic Public License while its `dictionary.txt` is LGPL and is **not used here**; and the ARPHIC PUBLIC LICENSE (1999) text from SPDX's `license-list-data` settles the money question in its own words, "If you wish, you can charge for this service". **None of the six reaches the app's own code**: Apache-2.0 and MIT are permissive, MPL-2.0 is file-level and the files ship unmodified, CC BY-SA's ShareAlike binds the derived database and not a work merely aggregated with it, and the Arphic text says so explicitly ("mere aggregation of another work not based on the Font with the Font on a volume of a storage or distribution medium does not bring the other work under the scope of this License"). No upstream `NOTICE` file exists for any of the four Apache-licensed items (all four 404), so Apache-2.0 §4(d) asks for nothing further. **Two duties were unmet and are now met:** the Arphic licence asks that "you retain this license file (ARPHICPL.TXT) unaltered in all copies", and `LICENSES.txt` had pointed at the makemeahanzi repository for it — where that path 404s — so the text is bundled as **`vendor/ARPHICPL.TXT`**; and its §2 a) wants the modification and its date named, so `LICENSES.txt` now says what was dropped from `graphics.txt` and that it happened on 3 September 2026. Neither file is a shell asset or in `OCR_FILES`, so no version marker moved. **The standing constraint, and it matters for the Play Store: `strokes.txt.gz` and `cedict.tsv.gz` must stay freely available to everyone under their own licences even after the app is sold** — the Arphic §2 b) ("you must make such modifications Freely Available as a whole to all third parties under the terms of this License") and CC BY-SA's ShareAlike both say so, and today that is satisfied only because this repository is public. **Selling the app is fine; taking those two files private, or shipping them only inside a paid package, is not.** That is a direct limit on H's earlier "once online, I will kill the web version".
