No word or gloss tables on the back (H: redundant) —, then **three grades in the traffic light's colours — Hard (red), Medium (amber), Easy (green)** — with no interval line under them (v421; after grading the next card appears at the top of the screen) — and underneath **☆ Star**, **⚑ Flag** and **✎ Edit** on one line (v427, v431), and last of all **the other cards with the same text** (v122, H: "if one character connects to various photos, then link them" — `linkedHTML`/`sameText`: a row "Also on another photo / N other photos" with their crops, newest first, `wireLinks`; on the study back and in the card detail alike — in the card detail a tap opens that card's detail; **the row is one line in the Cards list's box look since v345** (H, after the v344 polish: "Ideas how to improve 'on x other photos' as well?" — four ideas offered, "Go with 1"): the thumbs wrapped, so four photos broke 3 + 1 under the centred label; now the row is one line that scrolls sideways as the tag chips do (`flex-wrap:nowrap`, `overflow-x:auto`, no scrollbar, `justify-content:safe center` while it fits), and each tile carries the list's box look — the crop fitted with a subdued blurred copy behind it (`img.thumbbg` beside `img.thumb`, the v232/v234 values) instead of the crop sitting small on grey. The tile is 74×44 (78×50 until then), so four fit the card at 390 px and the touch target keeps its 44 px; a fifth scrolls. The v328 override `.shot .result .thumbs img{width:auto}` went with it — the linked row sizes its own two pictures now. **The three ideas not taken** (do not build them unasked): a status or date under each thumbnail, Learn showing one card of a set of duplicates and skipping the rest, and one card holding several photos — the last is a deck format change, and v118 decided the opposite, that the same text from another photo becomes its own card. Suite `verify-link` (the row's nowrap and auto overflow, one `img.thumb` and one `img.thumbbg` per other card); the detail, autocard and english suites pass; checked by screenshot on a seeded 农夫山泉 with four other photos in light, dark and on the Learn back with the peek ring. **Below the actions, and bigger (v422, H: "Die 'also in another photo' Zeile nach unten schieben. Mir gefällt auch noch nicht das Layout für den kleinen Thumbnails. Irgendwie sieht das alles komisch und unsauber aus. Vielleicht sind sie einfach zu klein"):** the row stood inside `backHTML`, between the parts row and the grades — reference material in the middle of the answer-then-grade path, with the four tiles reading as a cluttered strip right above the buttons. `backHTML` no longer carries it; each of its three callers places it below its own actions — the study card after the Flag/Edit row (with a hairline above it, `.card .linked`, since there it follows other content inside the card), the detail under the SRS line (no hairline: it sits on the page's own ground), the camera's finished card at the end of its back. And the tiles are **96 × 54** (74 × 44 from v345), the Cards list's own 16:9: three fit the card at 390 px with a peek of the fourth, which is what says the row scrolls. Nothing else changes — one line, no wrap (v345's finding), the same hairline and blurred fill, the same tap. Measured: the tiles at 96 × 54 and the row below the actions in both screens; the link, detail, cards and english suites pass; checked by screenshot on a seeded 供应 with four other photos in light and dark, on the Learn back and in the detail. Not yet field-checked. Not yet field-checked; **in Learn a tap shows that photo on the card in place** and a second tap returns (`S.peek`, the thumb ringed in the tint, reset on the next card; v155, H: "when tapping an 'also on another photo' card, I'm getting out of the learn mode. That should not happen" — until v154 the tap left the session for the Cards tab)) (`S.editFrom="study"`, Back/Save return to the revealed card). No example sentences (H's decision). **The closed card is pushed sideways to pick another card of the session (v414, carousel since v417; H: "koennen wir bitte im Lernmodus Swipes nach rechts und links erlauben, sodass man sich quasi die Karten aussuchen kann, die man testen moechte? I think that only makes sense In the closed card view, not after opening the card"; described in three lines, "Go for the swipes (number 3)"):** a horizontal stroke on the front moves through `S.queue` and **grades nothing** — `S.idx` alone changes, so the schedule and the progress rows are untouched. **What a skipped card actually does, corrected here (v417):** the v414 entry claimed it "keeps its place and comes round again", and that is **false** — `grade()` only ever does `S.idx++`, so a card swiped past sits behind the index and does not return in that session unless it is swiped back to; it is still due and the next session's queue picks it up, which is what makes skipping safe, but the header's Due capsule is `S.queue.length-S.idx` and so drops by one on every skip as if the card were done. Skipping *is* the feature H asked for, so the behaviour stands and only the sentence was wrong; the counter is named rather than changed.

**The model is a carousel, not Tinder (v417, H after seeing v414: "I'm still unhappy with the swipe" → asked what was wrong, he picked "it doesn't feel like Tinder" and "it should do more"; then "Okay, dann vergiss das mit dem Hoch- und Runterswipen, sondern nur rauftippen für Öffnen und Schließen", and then the model itself: "Ich moechte die Karten quasi nach links schieben und die naechste Karte kommt von rechts rein und rastet geschmeidig ein und das Gleiche in die andere Richtung. Die muessen nicht so zur Seite wegkippen wie bei Tinder"):** v414 faded the card out and animated the next one in from the side afterwards, which is a transition, not a gesture — the next card was never on screen while the thumb moved, so nothing was being *pushed*. Now the neighbour rides beside the card: on the first horizontal move `makePeer` builds a `.card.peer` from `frontHTML` of `S.queue[S.idx±1]`, places it absolutely against the card's own `offsetLeft`/`offsetTop`/`offsetWidth` (`#main` is `position:relative` for this, and every absolute already inside it has its own positioned ancestor — checked, so no containing block moves) and parks it one card width plus `SW_GAP` 16 px to the side; both then carry `translateX` of the same `dx`, so the pair moves as one strip. Past `SW_MIN` 60 px the pair slides `SW_MS` 220 ms on `cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1)` until the neighbour is centred and `render()` redraws at the new index — the card is already visually in place, so there is no entry animation and **`SWIPED`, `.inR`/`.inL` and the `cardinR`/`cardinL` keyframes are gone**. Under the threshold the pair slides back. **No tilt and no fade** — H named both as the part he did not want. The finger turning round mid-stroke rebuilds the peer for the other side (`want!==step` past the slop); at either end of the queue there is no peer, the card gives a quarter of the stroke and springs back as before. **The vertical gestures H first suggested are dropped on his own instruction** — down-to-open and up-to-close ("vergiss das … nur rauftippen für Öffnen und Schließen"): the tap on the character keeps both jobs, as it has since v82. Do not bring them back unasked. **And a defect of v414 went with it, measured rather than reasoned:** the slop test killed the gesture for the whole touch (`pid=null`) the first time vertical travel beat horizontal, so a stroke beginning with a little downward drift never became a swipe however far it then went sideways — a probe that moves 20 px down and then 140 px left moves **0 cards on v416 and 1 on v417** (run against the stashed v416 tree, not assumed). The latch is gone: the handler simply waits until `|ax|` passes the slop *and* beats `|ay|`, and the browser stays the arbiter of a real scroll — `.card.swipe` is `touch-action:pan-y`, so a genuine pan cancels the pointer and ends the gesture by itself. The rest of v414 stands: a press beginning on a button, link, field or chip is never a swipe; the stroke's own closing click is eaten by a capture-phase listener so it cannot reveal the card; the handler stands down whenever the back is open or the queue holds one card (`S.revealed`, `S.queue.length<2`, so "Test this card" from the list is unaffected), since once the answer is up the four grades own the screen — H's own boundary; `prefers-reduced-motion` turns the slide off. The front's hint and the guide's Learn sentence are unchanged and still true. **No `WHATS_NEW` line** — v414's own note already tells the learner what the gesture does, and this is the feel of a gesture shipped the same day, the v412 case exactly. The closed-card hint is `swipeHint(d)` now, one helper shared by `renderStudy` and the peer, so the two cannot drift apart and the peer is exactly as tall as the card it replaces. Suite `verify-swipe` gains `carousel` (mid-stroke: a `.card.peer` exists, absolutely positioned, carrying the *next* card's own glyph, standing to the right of the card, with no `rotate` in the card's transform and no inline opacity; after the commit the peer is gone) beside its twelve v414 checks; the english, guide, whatsnew, detail, cards, order, pullrefresh, savenow and link suites pass, and **the autocard and progress suites time out on `.card .glyph` — identically on the stashed v416 tree, so pre-existing and not from this change**; checked by screenshot in light and dark, mid-stroke and after the snap. Not yet field-checked — H's next session on the Xiaomi is the check: does the next card come in under his thumb and snap, and does the page still scroll? **The neighbour is centred on the card, not hung from its top (v418, H on v417: "Beim links, rechts swipen springen unterschiedlich hohe Karten in der Vertikalen. Bitte vermeiden."):** v417 placed the peer at the card's own `offsetTop`, which is right only while both cards are the same height — and Learn **centres** the card in what is left of the screen, so a two-line sign card sits 20 px lower than a one-character one while their middles are the same pixel (measured). A shorter or taller neighbour therefore slid in at the wrong height and hopped to its place at the render. The peer is appended, measured and then offset by half the difference, so it rides where it will land. Measured over three swaps (short→tall, tall→short, and back): the vertical jump at the snap is **20 px on v417 and 0 px on v418**, with the peer's centre on the card's within a pixel. **Field-confirmed 2026-09-11** (H, on v418: "Swipe looks good" — the carousel of v417 with the height fix of v418). **The pair travels to the screen's edge, not one card width (v420, H on his Xiaomi Mix Fold unfolded: "Sieht der Swipe im aufgeklappten Zustand auf dem großen Screen noch etwas komisch aus, weil die Karten links und rechts dann einfach plötzlich verschwinden. Die müssten eigentlich dann rausfliegen."):** `shift` was `card.offsetWidth+SW_GAP`, which is the right distance only because a phone's card is nearly as wide as its screen. A card is capped at 440 px, so on a wide screen one card width carries the outgoing card nowhere — measured at 1840 px it finished the slide at **285–725 of the viewport, fully visible**, and then blinked out at the render, while the neighbour was created in plain sight 456 px to the side instead of arriving from the edge. `shift` is `Math.max(card.offsetWidth+SW_GAP, par.offsetWidth-card.offsetLeft, card.offsetLeft+card.offsetWidth)` since — the distance that puts the leaving card past one edge and the arriving one beyond the other, taken from the layout rather than the transformed box, and covering both directions with one number so the pair still moves as one strip. **On a phone it is the card width again and nothing moves**: measured at 390 px the whole gesture is byte-identical (the outgoing card ends at −326 either way), while 1160 px goes from −55 to −362 and 1840 px from 285 to −326. Transforms do not add scrollable overflow here — `documentElement.scrollWidth` equals the viewport at 390, 1160 and 1840 px, before and after. Suite `verify-swipe` gains `fold` (a 1840 px context: the neighbour parked off-screen at rest, the outgoing card's right edge at or past 0 when the slide ends, no sideways scroll, the index moved) — measured false/false on v419 and true/true on v420; the carousel and noHop cases are unchanged. Checked by screenshot at 1840 px: the next card enters from the right edge. Not yet field-checked — H's next swipe on the unfolded Mix Fold is the check. Suite `verify-swipe` gains `noHop`, which seeds a deck of deliberately different heights, checks that the case is actually exercised (`heightsDiffer`) and that the jump is at most 2 px in both directions.


- **The open card is pushed sideways to the next card of the Cards list (v445, H: "Bitte Cards auch swipebar machen", then, on the two readings offered, "Open cards swipe"):** the card detail carries Learn's carousel. A horizontal stroke on the open card brings the previous or next card **of the Cards list** in beside it and snaps — `SW_SLOP` 12, `SW_MIN` 60, `SW_GAP` 16, `SW_MS` 220, the same `shift` of v420, the same peer. The neighbours are the list's own order, so a search or a ticked filter decides who they are, exactly as the row tap did. **The other reading — a row swiped in the list to reveal Delete / Star — was named to H and not built; do not build it unasked.** **`wireSwipe(card)` is `wireSwipe(card,o)`** with `o={n, idx, peer(i), go(i), centred, busy}`: the caller owns the list and what a move means, so one gesture serves the session queue and the Cards list instead of two copies, and Learn's own guards (`S.revealed`, `S.queue.length<2`) move to its call site. `par` is `card.offsetParent||card.parentElement` — #main on both screens, since the detail card sits inside a `.pane` that is not positioned — the peer's ids are stripped, and the v418 vertical centring is Learn's alone (`o.centred`), the detail card being top-aligned in its pane. **`cardsList()`** is the sort/filter/search on its own so the detail learns the order without building the list's HTML, and **`detailCardHTML(d,sw)`** is the detail card's body so the render and the peer copy cannot drift — the v417 lesson, where Learn's hint had to become `swipeHint` for the same reason. **The swipe changes the card, and the two pieces of view state go opposite ways because they mean different things:** `S.detailHide` is a way of *reading* — "I am testing myself" — and survives the swipe, since the detail is not a test that must come closed (which is why Learn resets `S.revealed` and this does not); `S.fullPic` is about *this photo* — "show me the whole picture of this card" — so it is dropped at the commit, as every other path that changes the card drops it (the row tap, the linked hop, Learn's next card), and the peer is built with it already off, or the neighbour would slide in showing its whole photo and jump to the crop the moment it landed. **A first cut dropped the `S.fullPic` reset along with the scroll reset, and the suite caught it** — the two lines sat together and the comment above them then claimed the opposite of what the code did, which is the v404 class of fault (a comment stating something false) one line from the change itself. **`backToList()` puts the row of the card you ended on back where the tapped row sat** (`LIST_CARD`, `LIST_OFF` beside `LIST_SCROLL`); with no swipe that is v352's pixel exactly — measured 420 == 420 on both trees — and a row that is gone falls back to the remembered scroll. **Four skeptics ran against it before it shipped and three of them landed, which is the entry's real content.** **(1) The ghost commit (high):** `peer`/`go` read the `list` array captured when the card was drawn, so a card deleted between the wire and the commit rode in as a ghost and landed the detail on a dead id, which falls back to the list **without a word** (measured: `{detail:null, mode:'cards', hasCard:0}`, no page error). The deck is read **live** through `cardOf` now, as Learn has always done. **(2) The scroll reset (high):** `go` copied Learn's `window.scrollTo(0,0)`, which on Learn is a no-op — the closed card never scrolls, `maxScroll` 0 — while the detail's page routinely scrolls (measured 348/491/687). The peer is placed in document coordinates, so it slid into exactly the right place and then the render teleported the page: **scroll 200 → a 199.8 px jump**, the v418 complaint reproduced on the new surface at up to 25× the magnitude. The scroll is kept. **(3) The pane's furniture (medium):** `.card.peer` is a sibling of `.pane` and paints above it, so a taller neighbour slid over Test / Edit / Star / Flag / Share / Delete card, the SRS line and the linked row — **527 px of overlap, the six buttons visibly sliced** — none of which move with the gesture. `o.busy` toggles `.pane.swiping`, and everything under the card steps aside for the stroke and comes back with the render. **(4) The filter (medium):** `renderCards` clears a filter that matches nothing (the v308 rule) and `renderCardDetail` did not, so an Accept or a cleared star taken **on the open card** made `li` −1 and the swipe vanished mid-session, and accepting the last one left the detail showing a card its own list said did not exist. That normalisation is `normaliseFilters()` now and both screens call it. **Two pre-existing faults of v414/v417 came with the new surface and are fixed here**, measured byte-identical on v444 first: a **pointercancel** — the platform taking the gesture away — still committed the move if it had travelled 60 px, and left `ate` set so the capture-phase click eater **swallowed the next tap anywhere in the card**, which on the detail is the Accept of an AI suggestion (measured: `acceptTap1` did nothing, `acceptTap2` worked). A cancelled gesture springs back and clears `ate`. **Measured:** Learn is **byte-identical** across 9 strokes plus a turn-round, at 390×844, 360×740 and 1840×1200, twice — **0 differences**, with a negative control (`SW_GAP` 16→22 on a v444 copy) reporting 8, so the zero is a real measurement; `verify-swipe` gives byte-identical 106-line reports on both trees. No object-URL leak (30 alternating swipes created **0** new blob URLs — `urlOf`'s WeakMap and the THUMB cache mean the peer reuses the card's), no stray peers after any case, 0 duplicate ids in the document, no horizontal overflow. Suite `verify-cardswipe` (the peer mid-stroke with the *next* list card's own text, absolutely positioned in the card's offsetParent, no ids; the commit; back the other way; both ends springing back; a search and a ticked filter deciding the neighbours; the answer-hidden state surviving; ← Cards landing on the tapped pixel with no swipe and on the ended-on row after one; a stroke on a button not being a swipe; the hint; and Learn's own carousel as the regression case) — **10 of its 14 cases fail on a v444 tree**, and the two that pass on both are named in the file as deliberate: the no-swipe ← Cards invariance, which cannot fail on v444 by construction, and the Learn regression case. **The scroll case is the one that had to be built to fail, and it is worth its own sentence** (the v419/v439 rule): `g3_scrollKept` runs at a 390×560 viewport, because a plain card overflows 390×844 by only 26 px while a real card on H's phone — picture, meaning, parts row, linked row — scrolls by hundreds; there it scrolls the open card to 200, strokes, and reads the scroll and the card's own top back. On the tree with the reset it comes back **200 → 0 with the card that had just snapped into place teleported 200 px** (top −75 → 125); on the shipped tree **200 → 200, jump 0**. It also had to be told where to put its finger: the helper's default start point is the card's top plus a quarter of its height, which on a card scrolled past the top of the screen lands on the **sticky top bar** and is swallowed — a fixture artifact that read exactly like a dead gesture, and the case now starts inside the card's visible part and clear of the header. The guide's Cards paragraph gained its clause in all ten columns (the v259 rule), key counts unchanged at 451 a column and 480 for ru, no duplicate in any column. **Named and left alone, all measured pre-existing and identical on v444:** a second stroke inside the 220 ms commit window is lost (gap 40/120 → one card, 260 → two, on both trees), so flicking quickly through the list loses every second swipe; and `par` following CSS rather than the DOM means that if any ancestor between the card and #main ever becomes positioned, `shift` is computed against the wrong width and v420 breaks on a wide screen with nothing in any suite to catch it (measured: `.pane{position:relative}` takes `shift` from 1150 to 460 at 1840 px). **Also left alone, deliberately:** a card reached through the linked-photos row while a filter is on is not in the list, so it simply has no swipe and no hint — honest, and `LIST_CARD` is cleared on that path so ← Cards falls back to v352's scroll rather than putting a swiped-to row at an offset belonging to another part of the list. A `WHATS_NEW` line. Not yet field-checked — H's next scroll through the Cards list is the check: does the next card come in under his thumb, does the page still scroll, and does his reading position survive?

**Three grades in the traffic light's colours, and no arithmetic under them (v421, H: "die Auswahlknöpfe müssen viel einfacher und weniger sein. Nur Easy, Medium, and Hard, in den Ampelfarben Rot, Grün und Gelb", then, on what the whole loop should feel like: "Ich swipe die Karten nach links und rechts, fang mir die Lösung an und sag, das war easy, das war mittel oder das war hart. Zack, zack, ohne groß Nachdenken" — described in three lines, "Go"):** the back carried four tiles — **Again · Hard · Good · Easy** — each with the next interval under its label (`<10 min`, `3 d`, `8 d`). Two things made that a decision rather than a reflex: *Again* and *Hard* are two words for two kinds of **not** knowing, and the interval line is arithmetic the learner is invited to weigh. Now three tiles, each in one of the traffic light's colours and each carrying its word alone: **Hard** red, **Medium** amber, **Easy** green, worst to best, which is also the traffic light's own order. **The mapping, and it is the one consequential decision in the change:** Hard is the scheduler's `again` (the card comes back later in the same session — red means stop, and the card was not known), Medium is `good` (the normal interval), Easy is `easy` unchanged. The fourth grade `hard` — "I knew it, barely, come back tomorrow" — is no longer reachable from the screen; `schedule()` keeps it, since progress rows written by it exist and its `fails` rule still reads it. **Nothing about the schedule itself moved:** every card keeps the interval, ease and due date it has, and the only behaviour change is that a half-known card now repeats today instead of tomorrow — harsher, and H's call. `previewInterval` is gone with the interval line, and with it the four keys it was the only caller of (`<10 min`, `<1 d`, `1 d`, `{0} d`) plus `Again` and `Good`, from all nine non-English columns; `Medium` came in (Mittel, Moyen, Medio, 普通, 보통, Средне, Vừa, ปานกลาง, Sedang) and the guide's Learn paragraph was rewritten in all nine, per the v259 rule that a screen which changes takes the guide's sentence with it in the same PR — 448 keys a column → **443**, ru 476 → **471**. **The colours are the soft surface with the strong label of `.btn.danger`**, not filled tiles: a filled amber tile with white on it does not carry its text, while `--warn` `#B5730B` on `--warn-soft` in light and `#E8A93C` on its own soft ground in dark both read cleanly — `--warn`/`--warn-soft` are the two tokens this adds. **One defect the measurement caught and reading would not have:** the page-wide `.lbl` rule (`color:var(--label2); margin-right:8px`) beat the colour the tile *inherits*, so the first build rendered three correctly coloured grounds with three grey labels 8 px off centre — inheritance loses to any matching rule, however weak, and `.grade .lbl` now sets `color:inherit;margin:0`. (The 8 px offset was there under the four tiles too, unnoticed since v82.) **Measured** at 390 px: three tiles of 102 × 62 px, at 360 px 92 × 62, and **0 clipped labels in all ten languages at both widths** — where the four-tile row's floor was 391 px in Russian and 373 in German (v401), so the row that used to overflow H's own phone in two languages now fits everywhere with room. Checked by screenshot in light and dark and in German. Suites: cards, detail, guide, swipe and whatsnew pass; english passes on every content check (its only failure is the harness's own service-worker registration on `localhost`, which the aiframe, swipe and whatsnew runs show too). Not yet field-checked — H's next session on the Xiaomi is the check: three taps that need no thinking.

**A reload in Learn comes back on the same card (v423, H at v421, 2026-09-11: "hatte ich gerade eine Karte offen und er ist von alleine zur naechsten Karte gesprungen" — his diagnostics said `page 421 · script 421 · readers 0/4` eleven minutes after v421 was merged, which is a page that had just reloaded itself):** boot always ran `S.queue=buildQueue(false); S.idx=0; S.done=0; S.revealed=false`, and `resumeView` (v327/v415) carried only the mode, the open card, the Cards search and the scroll — so **every** reload in Learn restarted the session at the top of a freshly built queue. That is the v327 idle reload after an update (which fires after four seconds without a finger, i.e. exactly while a card is being read), a pull-to-refresh, and a page Android discards for memory. A card graded earlier in the session is no longer due, so the rebuilt queue begins somewhere else and the app looks as if it jumped by itself; the header's Done capsule went back to 0 with it, and an open answer closed. `viewNow` now carries the session as well when the mode is study — the queue's **ids**, the place in it, whether the answer is open, the day's count and the Pull-forward flag — and boot restores them, dropping any id whose card is gone or has no text and clamping the index; `noteViewSoon`'s key gains the card and the open answer, so each card is noted as it comes up rather than once on entering Learn. **Measured against a v422 baseline, the same probe on both trees:** a card graded Hard stays due today, so the rebuild puts it back at the front — on v422 the reload moves from 决 to 光 (index 1 → 0), on v423 it stays on 决; the Done count and the queue's own order are kept, and a card deleted while the page was away is dropped from the restored queue. What it still cannot restore: a single-card test from the Cards list (`S.single`/`S.saved`) — a reload there comes back in the ordinary session; the note is skipped for it rather than written wrong. What it costs: one small settings write per card instead of one per screen, and a few hundred short ids in the note. Suite `verify-resume` (the five cases above, plus a fresh open still starting at the top of a new session — the v183/v415 rule); the pullrefresh, order, english and whatsnew suites pass. **The reload suite does not run in this session at all** — it waits for `navigator.serviceWorker.controller` and the harness's worker never registers (`Failed to update a ServiceWorker … Not found`, the same line the other suites log and ignore); measured identically on a v422 baseline root, so it is the sandbox, not the change. Not yet field-checked — H's next update taken mid-session is the check: the same card, still open.

**A card you find hard no longer comes straight back at you (v428, H at v427, 2026-09-11: "Jetzt haengt der star filter bei dieser einen karte" — a Learn session showing Due 1 / Done 0 and the same 骑车勿盯 card after every tap):** `grade()` has always done `if(g==="again") S.queue.push(c)` — the card goes to the end of the queue — and when the session holds nothing after the current card, that end **is now**: the page re-renders byte-identical, `S.done` does not move, the Due capsule does not move, and the app looks frozen. It has always been true and never bit, because a session was always many cards; **two changes since made a one-card session ordinary.** v421 turned the four grades into three, so **Hard is `again`** — the grade a learner taps for anything they did not know, where the old four-way split sent most of those to `hard` (tomorrow, out of the session). And v425's Starred filter is a deliberately narrow set: H's own deck has **11** starred cards of which **one** was due or new, the other ten scheduled nine days out, so his session was a single card and every Hard tap redrew it — **and the pill said "Starred (11)" over it the whole time.** Reproduced in the harness on his shape before anything was changed: three taps, three times `c0`, `done` 0, the queue growing 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 with the same id pushed onto it. **The rule now: the same card is never shown twice in a row with nothing in between.** When `again` is graded and the queue holds nothing after the current card, the next cards of the same filter are pulled forward first (`aheadCards`, by due date, up to `NEW_PER_SESSION` 8, skipping what the session already holds) and the card goes behind them; `S.ahead` is set, so the done screen says "Pulled-forward round finished." as it does after the button. Measured on H's shape: Hard now gives the next starred card with the queue at 10 and the Due capsule 1 → 9 — the nine others, which is what the pill had promised all along. **Nothing changes in a full session** (five cards due: Hard pushes the card, the queue goes 5 → 6, the next card is the next one, nothing pulled, `ahead` false), and **a deck of one card still repeats** — there is nothing else to show and the done screen would be a lie. The Learn filter is one rule now (`learnDeck()`, lifted out of `buildQueue` so the session and the pull-forward read the same set — two copies would drift, the v401 lesson). **No `WHATS_NEW` line:** the pull-forward fires only where the alternative is a frozen screen, and a note promising that hard cards come back later would over-state it. Suite `verify-again` (H's shape — one card, then Hard giving another card with the queue at 10 and `ahead` set, and three taps never repeating the same card; five cards due with nothing pulled and `ahead` false; a deck of one repeating); the star, swipe, resume, order and link suites pass, and the english, filter, cards and progress suites fail byte-identically on a v427 baseline (the harness's own service-worker line, and two failures older than this change). Not yet field-checked — H's next starred session is the check: does Hard move him on? **The question it left open was put to H and answered the same hour — see v429 below.**

**Starred studies every starred card, not only the ones due today (v429, H: "Gute frage zu starred. Your recommendation?" → the recommendation, then "Go"):** v428 stopped the loop and left the dissonance behind it — the pill counts **11** and the session offered **1**. That is SRS-correct and reads as broken, and the reason it reads as broken is what the star *is*. **A tag is a category** (Appliance, 167 cards): "study my Appliance cards" rightly means the due ones among them. **A star is a hand-picked short list** — H taps it while scrolling, on the one card that matters — so picking Starred means "these". `learnDeck()` says whether the star filter really applied (it stands down when nothing in reach is starred, v425), and `buildQueue` then appends every remaining starred card after the due and new ones, by due date: **the plan still leads, and the rest follow.** **The eight-card cap is lifted in a starred session** (`NEW_PER_SESSION` exists to stop a learner drowning in new cards, not to withhold the ones they picked themselves — measured: ten new starred cards give a session of 11 where the ordinary deck caps at 8). **Tags are untouched**, and so is every unfiltered session. **What it costs, and H was told before the "Go":** the pulled-forward cards are reviewed earlier than the plan says, so their intervals move — Medium pushes them further out, Hard drops them to today. That is the price of drilling and it is what the star is for. No cap on the session's length: 50 stars give 50 cards, and the length is controlled by the stars themselves. **Measured:** H's own shape (11 starred, one of them new, ten scheduled nine days out) gives a queue of **11** with the new card first, the scheduled ones after it in due order, the header reading **Due 11** under the pill "Starred (11)"; the same deck with the star off gives 3 (two due, one new); a tag over the same eleven cards still gives 1. **Considered and rejected:** drilling without writing the schedule (Anki's cram mode) — cleaner for the statistics, but then the three grades do nothing in a starred session, which would have to be explained, and explaining is the opposite of H's "zack, zack, ohne groß Nachdenken". **v428's own suite moved with this:** its one-card session came from the star, which no longer produces one, so `verify-again` uses a **tag** over the same shape — the honest record that v429 took that case away from the star while the loop guard still matters for tags and for the whole deck. The guide's star sentence follows the screen (the v259 rule): "… the filter then shows them alone, and Learn studies all of them, due or not." in all ten languages, one key replaced, no key added or removed (445 a column, ru 473 — the counts this file recorded at v425 were two low), no duplicate in any column, and the static key check reports only its two known open findings (`kind:`, `{0} ({1})`). A `WHATS_NEW` line, since a learner notices it. Suite `verify-starred` (the star off giving the ordinary session; the star on giving all eleven with the new one first, the Due capsule at 11 and the pill agreeing; the scheduled ones after the due ones and in due order; the eight-new cap lifted for the starred session and kept without it; a tag still a category; the filter standing down when nothing is starred); the again, star, guide, order, whatsnew, resume and link suites pass, the english and filter suites fail only on the harness's own service-worker line. Checked by screenshot in light and German dark. Not yet field-checked — H's next Starred session is the check: eleven cards, and does drilling them feel right or does the schedule drift?

Wir haben schon lange keinen Context Feld mehr", then "Ja" to clearing it out):** the screenshot he was looking at came from the harness, which still seeds the pre-v33 built-in deck (`base-deck.json`, 23 of its 25 cards carry `w`/`wp`/`wm`) — not from the app, where **no path had created a context word for a long time**: neither a card from a photo nor the Add form (`#f-word` there is the Characters field, not a context word). What was left was dead weight that only an ancient card could still reach: `wordBlock` in `backHTML` (`if (d.w)`), the Edit form's three fields (`if (!isSign && d.w)`) with their save branch, `.rule`/`.word`/`.word .w`/`.word .wp`/`.wm` in the CSS — `.rule` had exactly one user, that block — the Cards search over `d.w`/`d.wp`/`d.wm`, and two keys in nine columns ("Context word, pinyin, meaning (optional)", "to learn"): 443 keys a column → **441**, ru 469. **The data is not deleted**: a card that has the fields keeps them, and export and import carry them like any other field — only nothing shows, edits or searches them. What changes for a user: a card from the old built-in deck loses the 学习 xuéxí / to learn block under its meaning and the three fields in its Edit form, and the search no longer matches a context word's meaning — the cards suite's `SEARCH "contract"` case relied on exactly that (`合 / 合同 / contract`) and is the one expectation this change breaks, on purpose. - **Line breaks — the card text follows the photo, automatically (H's rule):** the front never wraps on its own; every word card gets the wide box and the font is fitted to the longest line (`frontLines`, `frontBox`; the 260 px square for up to three characters went in v223). **A number stays in the word card's lines (v338, H's 24小时营业, 2026-09-08 — the front showed 小时营业 while the pinyin and the parts row had the 24: "Hier fehlt das 24 in der 2. Zeile"):** the front draws a word card's lines from `seg`, and two places built `seg` from Chinese characters alone — `readingCard` filtered the reading's parts by `CJK`, and `segWithBreaks` (the Edit form's rebuild) walked the line's Chinese characters only. Now `readingCard` keeps a part matching `NUM_PART` too, and `segWithBreaks` cuts a number with its Latin unit (`NUM_TOKEN`) as a word of its own between the dictionary words — `["24","小时","营业"]`, `["净含量","380ml"]`, `["3","月","1","日","全国","上映"]` (the CJK unit joins at display through `mergeUnits`). **Cards from before v338 are repaired once at boot** (`fixNumberSegs`): a word card whose text has more digits than its `seg` gets its lines rebuilt — the old lines' Chinese characters keep their line, the numbers between them follow the text's order — after the dictionary is loaded (without it the next start repairs), written in one transaction. Suite `verify-units` (a seeded 24小时营业 with `seg` ["小时","营业"] repaired to ["24","小时","营业"] in memory and in IndexedDB with the front reading 24小时营业, a two-line 2人3日 keeping its lines, `segWithBreaks` on three lines); the english, edit, cards and wrap suites pass. Not yet field-checked — H's 24小时营业 card after the update is the check: 24 in the box. **The line's width counts digits and spaces (v339, H's 绿皮书 sign card, 2026-09-08 — the second line 3月1日 全国上映 ran past the text box: "warum geht hier das 映 über die graue Box hinaus?"):** `fitLines` sized the font by `glyphs`, the count of Chinese characters, so that line measured six wide while the digits and the space make it about eight. Now `lineUnits(s)` measures a line in character widths — a Chinese character 1, a digit or a Latin letter 0.6, a space 0.35, other punctuation 0.5 — and `fitLines` fits the font and picks the longest line by it; the sign card's font cap and `headFont` keep the character count. Suite `verify-units` (the 绿皮书 sign card at 390 px: both lines inside the box, the helper's count 7.55; screenshot `units-fit`); the wrap, box, english and sign-card suites pass. Not yet field-checked — H's 绿皮书 card after the update is the check: 映 inside the box. **One exception (v152, H's 16-character escalator sign ran past the card: "statt überlaufende Zeile bitte zweizeilig"):** a photo line too long for the box is shown on two (or more) lines, cut nearest its middle between the card's words (`fitLines`, words from `seg` via `frontWords` or `segs`), while the fitted font would fall under 30 px in the reticle or 22 px in a sign card's text — display only, the stored lines stay; and the box width is measured from the card (`frontWidth`: main's inner width capped at 440, minus the card's padding — until v151 it was guessed from the window and overflowed the card on the phone). Where the lines come from: the reader keeps Tesseract's lines (sign cards: `c` with `\n`; word cards: a `"\n"` token in `seg`); the AI's answer is re-cut to those lines when the model drops the `\n` (`recutLines`: old break offsets, so a corrected character keeps them and an added one only lengthens the last line); a rename keeps them the same way (`segWithBreaks`); the Edit form shows word cards with one strip and one line input per photo line (the hint sentence about it was confusing and is gone). Cards without any line data (before v39) get their lines **estimated once at boot** from the crop's shape (`autoBreaks`: L ≈ √(n·h/w), cut at word boundaries, stored with `lb:"auto"`); cards with real line data are `lb:"photo"` and never touched.

They were not: a flex item *shrinks* rather than overflows, so the German labels wrapped **inside** their buttons and the row rendered as three ragged two-line columns with the glyph stranded above its word (seen in the screenshot, not in the numbers). **A fit check must ask whether the text broke, not whether the box overflowed** — `range.selectNodeContents(el).getClientRects().length>1` is the question, and it is now the one the suite asks. Why the hash and not a secret: the function first read a secret `REPORT_PASSWORD` (v197–v198); H set it in the dashboard, re-deployed, and the function still answered "wrong password" on every call while the app's hash proved the phone sent the right password — why the secret never reached the function was not found from the phone, so the secret went and the hash sits in the code (v199), and the report rendered at once. **Reading the rows on the phone:** the dashboard's Table Editor hides the table list on a narrow screen (H saw only "Create a table"), so H uses the SQL Editor (`…/project/xttuotninuwxnpcbyejn/sql/new`): `select created_at, data from reports order by created_at desc;` for the raw list, and a saved per-user query — `select distinct on (data->>'install') …` with the counts cast from `data`, ordered by `data->>'install', created_at desc` — for one line per phone; the id under Usage sharing (v171) is what a friend reads out so H finds their line. (Supabase's project creation was down in Singapore on 2026-09-04; H created the project later the same day.)

I don't think so" — right: the app installs from Safari, Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet alike, only the menu entry differs): **the first row of the "Share" section** (the first section of More until v274, the second since v275, under Learning) — "Send the link to a friend. The app installs from any browser, no store." with a **Share** button (`shareApp`, `#app-share`): the share sheet with `APP_SHARE_TEXT` ("识字 Zeichentrainer — learn the Chinese characters you see around you.
